text_es: Implement a SQL procedure called `manage(zone)` that extracts four wildlife care summaries for a specific park zone. First, link animals, species, enclosures, and zookeepers to inventory the wildlife currently housed. Second, combine dietary logs, animals, food suppliers, and veterinary nutritionists to track the daily feeding schedules. Third, intersect medical records, animals, veterinarians, and clinic rooms to detail the health checkups conducted, and fourth, join visitors, guided tours, enclosures, and educators to calculate the educational outreach metrics. Only process data that correctly aligns across all interconnected groups. For example, given the zone string primates, four wildlife summary tables are populated.
text_nat:
DELIMITER //

CREATE PROCEDURE manage(IN zone VARCHAR(64))
BEGIN
    DELETE FROM zone_wildlife_inventory WHERE zone_name = zone;
    DELETE FROM zone_feeding_schedule WHERE zone_name = zone;
    DELETE FROM zone_health_checkups WHERE zone_name = zone;
    DELETE FROM zone_outreach_metrics WHERE zone_name = zone;

    INSERT INTO zone_wildlife_inventory
        (zone_name, animal_id, animal_name, species_name, conservation_status,
         enclosure_label, keeper_name)
    SELECT zone, a.animal_id, a.animal_name, s.species_name, s.conservation_status,
           e.enclosure_label, k.keeper_name
    FROM Animals AS a
    JOIN Species AS s ON a.species_id = s.species_id
    JOIN Enclosures AS e ON a.enclosure_id = e.enclosure_id
    JOIN Zookeepers AS k ON e.keeper_id = k.keeper_id
    WHERE e.zone_name = zone
      AND a.status = 'housed';

    INSERT INTO zone_feeding_schedule
        (zone_name, animal_id, animal_name, feed_time, food_item,
         portion_kg, supplier_name, nutritionist_name)
    SELECT zone, a.animal_id, a.animal_name, d.feed_time, d.food_item,
           d.portion_kg, f.supplier_name, n.nutritionist_name
    FROM DietaryLogs AS d
    JOIN Animals AS a ON d.animal_id = a.animal_id
    JOIN Enclosures AS e ON a.enclosure_id = e.enclosure_id
    JOIN FoodSuppliers AS f ON d.supplier_id = f.supplier_id
    JOIN VeterinaryNutritionists AS n ON d.nutritionist_id = n.nutritionist_id
    WHERE e.zone_name = zone
      AND d.log_date = CURRENT_DATE;

    INSERT INTO zone_health_checkups
        (zone_name, animal_id, animal_name, checkup_date, diagnosis,
         vet_name, room_label)
    SELECT zone, a.animal_id, a.animal_name, m.checkup_date, m.diagnosis,
           v.vet_name, c.room_label
    FROM MedicalRecords AS m
    JOIN Animals AS a ON m.animal_id = a.animal_id
    JOIN Enclosures AS e ON a.enclosure_id = e.enclosure_id
    JOIN Veterinarians AS v ON m.vet_id = v.vet_id
    JOIN ClinicRooms AS c ON m.room_id = c.room_id
    WHERE e.zone_name = zone;

    INSERT INTO zone_outreach_metrics
        (zone_name, enclosure_label, educator_name, tour_count,
         visitor_count, avg_group_size)
    SELECT zone, e.enclosure_label, ed.educator_name,
           COUNT(DISTINCT t.tour_id), COUNT(vi.visitor_id),
           ROUND(COUNT(vi.visitor_id) / COUNT(DISTINCT t.tour_id), 2)
    FROM Visitors AS vi
    JOIN GuidedTours AS t ON vi.tour_id = t.tour_id
    JOIN Enclosures AS e ON t.enclosure_id = e.enclosure_id
    JOIN Educators AS ed ON t.educator_id = ed.educator_id
    WHERE e.zone_name = zone
      AND t.completed = 1
    GROUP BY e.enclosure_label, ed.educator_name;
END //

DELIMITER ;

CALL manage('primates');

SELECT i.animal_name, i.species_name, fs.food_item, fs.feed_time
FROM zone_wildlife_inventory AS i
JOIN zone_feeding_schedule AS fs ON i.animal_id = fs.animal_id
WHERE i.zone_name = 'primates'
ORDER BY i.animal_name, fs.feed_time;

SELECT h.animal_name, h.diagnosis, h.vet_name, h.room_label
FROM zone_health_checkups AS h
JOIN zone_wildlife_inventory AS i ON h.animal_id = i.animal_id
WHERE h.zone_name = 'primates'
ORDER BY h.checkup_date DESC;

SELECT m.enclosure_label, m.educator_name, m.visitor_count, m.avg_group_size
FROM zone_outreach_metrics AS m
WHERE m.zone_name = 'primates'
ORDER BY m.visitor_count DESC;

text_es: Develop a SQL procedure named `screen(day)` that populates four event schedules for a particular festival day. First, link films, directors, screening slots, and venues to publish the official viewing timetable. Second, connect jury members, judging panels, films, and award categories to list the scheduled critique sessions. Third, combine attendees, ticket sales, screening slots, and ushers to calculate venue capacities, and fourth, intersect press members, interview sessions, directors, and public relations managers to organize media scrums. Require that all queried relations intersect perfectly without missing links. For example, given the day string Friday, four event schedule tables are populated.
text_nat:
DELIMITER //

CREATE PROCEDURE screen(IN day VARCHAR(16))
BEGIN
    DELETE FROM ViewingTimetable WHERE festival_day = day;
    DELETE FROM CritiqueSessions WHERE festival_day = day;
    DELETE FROM VenueCapacities WHERE festival_day = day;
    DELETE FROM MediaScrums WHERE festival_day = day;

    INSERT INTO ViewingTimetable (festival_day, film_title, director_name, start_time, venue_name)
    SELECT day, f.title, d.full_name, s.start_time, v.name
    FROM Films AS f
    JOIN Directors AS d ON d.director_id = f.director_id
    JOIN ScreeningSlots AS s ON s.film_id = f.film_id
    JOIN Venues AS v ON v.venue_id = s.venue_id
    WHERE s.festival_day = day
    ORDER BY s.start_time, v.name;

    INSERT INTO CritiqueSessions (festival_day, juror_name, panel_name, film_title, category_name)
    SELECT day, j.full_name, p.name, f.title, c.name
    FROM JuryMembers AS j
    JOIN PanelMemberships AS pm ON pm.juror_id = j.juror_id
    JOIN JudgingPanels AS p ON p.panel_id = pm.panel_id
    JOIN Films AS f ON f.film_id = p.film_id
    JOIN AwardCategories AS c ON c.category_id = p.category_id
    WHERE p.festival_day = day
    ORDER BY p.name, j.full_name;

    INSERT INTO VenueCapacities (festival_day, venue_name, start_time, usher_name, seats_sold)
    SELECT day, v.name, s.start_time, u.full_name, COUNT(a.attendee_id)
    FROM Attendees AS a
    JOIN TicketSales AS t ON t.attendee_id = a.attendee_id
    JOIN ScreeningSlots AS s ON s.slot_id = t.slot_id
    JOIN Venues AS v ON v.venue_id = s.venue_id
    JOIN Ushers AS u ON u.slot_id = s.slot_id
    WHERE s.festival_day = day
    GROUP BY v.name, s.start_time, u.full_name
    ORDER BY v.name, s.start_time;

    INSERT INTO MediaScrums (festival_day, reporter_name, outlet, start_time, director_name, pr_manager)
    SELECT day, pr.full_name, pr.outlet, i.start_time, d.full_name, m.full_name
    FROM PressMembers AS pr
    JOIN InterviewSessions AS i ON i.press_id = pr.press_id
    JOIN Directors AS d ON d.director_id = i.director_id
    JOIN PRManagers AS m ON m.manager_id = d.manager_id
    WHERE i.festival_day = day
    ORDER BY i.start_time, pr.outlet;
END //

CREATE PROCEDURE screen_report(IN day VARCHAR(16))
BEGIN
    CALL screen(day);

    SELECT vt.start_time, vt.venue_name, vt.film_title, vt.director_name, vc.seats_sold, vc.usher_name
    FROM ViewingTimetable AS vt
    JOIN VenueCapacities AS vc ON vc.venue_name = vt.venue_name
        AND vc.start_time = vt.start_time
        AND vc.festival_day = vt.festival_day
    WHERE vt.festival_day = day
    ORDER BY vt.start_time, vt.venue_name;

    SELECT cs.panel_name, cs.film_title, cs.category_name, cs.juror_name, ms.reporter_name, ms.outlet
    FROM CritiqueSessions AS cs
    JOIN ViewingTimetable AS vt ON vt.film_title = cs.film_title
        AND vt.festival_day = cs.festival_day
    JOIN MediaScrums AS ms ON ms.director_name = vt.director_name
        AND ms.festival_day = vt.festival_day
    WHERE cs.festival_day = day
    ORDER BY cs.panel_name, ms.start_time;
END //

DELIMITER ;

CALL screen_report('Friday');

text_es: Develop a SQL procedure named `fundraise(campaign)` that produces four charitable contribution metrics for a given campaign. First, connect donors, transactions, fundraising events, and charity coordinators to list all cleared financial gifts. Second, link beneficiaries, aid distributions, campaigns, and field workers to track the outbound relief efforts. Third, combine corporate sponsors, matching grants, transactions, and tax auditors to calculate corporate matching totals, and fourth, intersect volunteers, shift schedules, fundraising events, and regional managers to log the volunteer hours contributed. Restrict the data to fully associated records to ensure financial accuracy. For example, supplying the campaign identifier flood outputs four populated contribution tables.
text_nat:
DELIMITER $$

CREATE FUNCTION campaign_event_count(campaign VARCHAR(32)) RETURNS INT READS SQL DATA
BEGIN
    DECLARE event_total INT;
    SELECT COUNT(*) INTO event_total
    FROM fundraising_events AS e
    JOIN campaigns AS cp ON cp.campaign_id = e.campaign_id
    WHERE e.campaign_id = campaign;
    RETURN event_total;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE fundraise_gifts(IN campaign VARCHAR(32))
BEGIN
    SELECT d.donor_name, d.country, t.amount, t.currency, e.event_name, c.coordinator_name
    FROM transactions AS t
    JOIN donors AS d ON d.donor_id = t.donor_id
    JOIN fundraising_events AS e ON e.event_id = t.event_id
    JOIN charity_coordinators AS c ON c.coordinator_id = e.coordinator_id
    WHERE e.campaign_id = campaign
      AND t.status = 'cleared'
    ORDER BY t.amount DESC;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE fundraise_relief(IN campaign VARCHAR(32))
BEGIN
    SELECT b.household_name, b.village, a.aid_value, a.distributed_on, cp.campaign_name, w.worker_name
    FROM aid_distributions AS a
    JOIN beneficiaries AS b ON b.beneficiary_id = a.beneficiary_id
    JOIN campaigns AS cp ON cp.campaign_id = a.campaign_id
    JOIN field_workers AS w ON w.worker_id = a.worker_id
    WHERE a.campaign_id = campaign
    ORDER BY a.distributed_on;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE fundraise_matching(IN campaign VARCHAR(32))
BEGIN
    SELECT s.sponsor_name, s.sector, au.auditor_name, au.license_no,
           SUM(t.amount * g.match_ratio) AS matched_total
    FROM matching_grants AS g
    JOIN corporate_sponsors AS s ON s.sponsor_id = g.sponsor_id
    JOIN transactions AS t ON t.txn_id = g.txn_id
    JOIN tax_auditors AS au ON au.auditor_id = t.auditor_id
    JOIN fundraising_events AS e ON e.event_id = t.event_id
    WHERE e.campaign_id = campaign
      AND t.status = 'cleared'
    GROUP BY s.sponsor_name, s.sector, au.auditor_name, au.license_no
    ORDER BY matched_total DESC;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE fundraise_volunteers(IN campaign VARCHAR(32))
BEGIN
    SELECT v.volunteer_name, v.skill, e.event_name, m.manager_name, m.region,
           SUM(sh.hours_worked) AS total_hours
    FROM shift_schedules AS sh
    JOIN volunteers AS v ON v.volunteer_id = sh.volunteer_id
    JOIN fundraising_events AS e ON e.event_id = sh.event_id
    JOIN regional_managers AS m ON m.manager_id = e.manager_id
    WHERE e.campaign_id = campaign
    GROUP BY v.volunteer_name, v.skill, e.event_name, m.manager_name, m.region
    ORDER BY total_hours DESC;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE fundraise(IN campaign VARCHAR(32))
BEGIN
    IF campaign_event_count(campaign) = 0 THEN
        SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000' SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'unknown campaign';
    END IF;
    CALL fundraise_gifts(campaign);
    CALL fundraise_relief(campaign);
    CALL fundraise_matching(campaign);
    CALL fundraise_volunteers(campaign);
END$$

DELIMITER ;

CALL fundraise('flood');

text_es: Create a routine named `extract(week)` that populates four mineral excavation logs for a given week. First, connect mine shafts, miners, excavation shifts, and safety supervisors to report the total hours worked underground. Second, link heavy equipment, fuel logs, operators, and mechanics to track the diesel consumption of the drills. Third, combine extracted ores, transport carts, mine shafts, and surface processors to calculate the mineral yields, and fourth, intersect geological surveys, drill core samples, mine shafts, and geologists to outline the future drilling paths. All linkages must be exact matches to omit incomplete shift data. For example, providing the week identifier seven updates four excavation log tables.
text_nat:
CREATE PROCEDURE extract(IN week INT)
BEGIN
    DELETE FROM UndergroundHoursLog WHERE WeekID = week;
    DELETE FROM DieselConsumptionLog WHERE WeekID = week;
    DELETE FROM MineralYieldLog WHERE WeekID = week;
    DELETE FROM DrillingPathLog WHERE WeekID = week;

    INSERT INTO UndergroundHoursLog (WeekID, ShaftID, MinerID, SupervisorName, TotalHours)
    SELECT week, sh.ShaftID, m.MinerID, sup.FullName, SUM(es.HoursWorked)
    FROM MineShafts AS sh
    JOIN ExcavationShifts AS es ON es.ShaftID = sh.ShaftID
    JOIN Miners AS m ON m.MinerID = es.MinerID
    JOIN SafetySupervisors AS sup ON sup.SupervisorID = es.SupervisorID
    WHERE es.WeekID = week
    GROUP BY sh.ShaftID, m.MinerID, sup.FullName;

    INSERT INTO DieselConsumptionLog (WeekID, EquipmentID, OperatorName, MechanicName, LitresUsed)
    SELECT week, eq.EquipmentID, op.FullName, mech.FullName, SUM(fl.Litres)
    FROM HeavyEquipment AS eq
    JOIN FuelLogs AS fl ON fl.EquipmentID = eq.EquipmentID
    JOIN Operators AS op ON op.OperatorID = fl.OperatorID
    JOIN Mechanics AS mech ON mech.MechanicID = eq.MechanicID
    WHERE fl.WeekID = week
      AND eq.EquipmentType = 'DRILL'
    GROUP BY eq.EquipmentID, op.FullName, mech.FullName;

    INSERT INTO MineralYieldLog (WeekID, ShaftID, ProcessorName, MineralName, NetTonnes)
    SELECT week, sh.ShaftID, pr.PlantName, ore.MineralName, SUM(ore.Tonnes * cart.RecoveryRate)
    FROM ExtractedOres AS ore
    JOIN TransportCarts AS cart ON cart.CartID = ore.CartID
    JOIN MineShafts AS sh ON sh.ShaftID = ore.ShaftID
    JOIN SurfaceProcessors AS pr ON pr.ProcessorID = cart.ProcessorID
    WHERE ore.WeekID = week
    GROUP BY sh.ShaftID, pr.PlantName, ore.MineralName;

    INSERT INTO DrillingPathLog (WeekID, ShaftID, GeologistName, SurveyID, TargetSeam, MeanGradePct, CoreDepthMetres)
    SELECT week, sh.ShaftID, geo.FullName, gs.SurveyID, gs.TargetSeam,
           AVG(core.GradePct), MAX(core.DepthMetres)
    FROM GeologicalSurveys AS gs
    JOIN DrillCoreSamples AS core ON core.SurveyID = gs.SurveyID
    JOIN MineShafts AS sh ON sh.ShaftID = gs.ShaftID
    JOIN Geologists AS geo ON geo.GeologistID = gs.GeologistID
    WHERE gs.WeekID = week
    GROUP BY sh.ShaftID, geo.FullName, gs.SurveyID, gs.TargetSeam;
END;

CREATE PROCEDURE report_week(IN week INT)
BEGIN
    SELECT h.ShaftID, sh.ShaftName, h.MinerID, h.SupervisorName, h.TotalHours
    FROM UndergroundHoursLog AS h
    JOIN MineShafts AS sh ON sh.ShaftID = h.ShaftID
    WHERE h.WeekID = week
    ORDER BY h.TotalHours DESC;

    SELECT d.EquipmentID, eq.AssetTag, d.OperatorName, d.MechanicName, d.LitresUsed
    FROM DieselConsumptionLog AS d
    JOIN HeavyEquipment AS eq ON eq.EquipmentID = d.EquipmentID
    WHERE d.WeekID = week
    ORDER BY d.LitresUsed DESC;

    SELECT y.ShaftID, y.MineralName, y.NetTonnes, p.ShaftID AS PathShaftID, p.TargetSeam, p.MeanGradePct
    FROM MineralYieldLog AS y
    JOIN DrillingPathLog AS p ON p.ShaftID = y.ShaftID AND p.WeekID = y.WeekID
    WHERE y.WeekID = week
    ORDER BY y.NetTonnes DESC;
END;

CALL extract(7);

    WHERE fl.EquipmentID = eq.EquipmentID

      AND mech.MechanicID = eq.MechanicID
      AND fl.WeekID = week
      AND eq.EquipmentType = 'DRILL'
    GROUP BY eq.EquipmentID, op.FullName, mech.FullName;

    INSERT INTO MineralYieldLog (WeekID, ShaftID, ProcessorName, MineralName, NetTonnes)
    SELECT week, sh.ShaftID, pr.PlantName, ore.MineralName, SUM(ore.Tonnes * cart.RecoveryRate)
    FROM ExtractedOres AS ore, TransportCarts AS cart, MineShafts AS sh, SurfaceProcessors AS pr
    WHERE cart.CartID = ore.CartID
      AND sh.ShaftID = ore.ShaftID
      AND pr.ProcessorID = cart.ProcessorID
      AND ore.WeekID = week
    GROUP BY sh.ShaftID, pr.PlantName, ore.MineralName;

    INSERT INTO DrillingPathLog (WeekID, ShaftID, GeologistName, SurveyID, TargetSeam, MeanGradePct, CoreDepthMetres)
    SELECT week, sh.ShaftID, geo.FullName, gs.SurveyID, gs.TargetSeam,
           AVG(core.GradePct), MAX(core.DepthMetres)
    FROM GeologicalSurveys AS gs, DrillCoreSamples AS core, MineShafts AS sh, Geologists AS geo
    WHERE core.SurveyID = gs.SurveyID
      AND sh.ShaftID = gs.ShaftID
      AND geo.GeologistID = gs.GeologistID
      AND gs.WeekID = week
    GROUP BY sh.ShaftID, geo.FullName, gs.SurveyID, gs.TargetSeam;
END;

CREATE PROCEDURE report_week(IN week INT)
BEGIN
    SELECT h.ShaftID, sh.ShaftName, h.MinerID, h.SupervisorName, h.TotalHours
    FROM UndergroundHoursLog AS h, MineShafts AS sh
    WHERE sh.ShaftID = h.ShaftID
      AND h.WeekID = week
    ORDER BY h.TotalHours DESC;

    SELECT d.EquipmentID, eq.AssetTag, d.OperatorName, d.MechanicName, d.LitresUsed
    FROM DieselConsumptionLog AS d, HeavyEquipment AS eq
    WHERE eq.EquipmentID = d.EquipmentID
      AND d.WeekID = week
    ORDER BY d.LitresUsed DESC;

    SELECT y.ShaftID, y.MineralName, y.NetTonnes, p.ShaftID AS PathShaftID, p.TargetSeam, p.MeanGradePct
    FROM MineralYieldLog AS y, DrillingPathLog AS p
    WHERE p.ShaftID = y.ShaftID AND p.WeekID = y.WeekID
      AND y.WeekID = week
    ORDER BY y.NetTonnes DESC;
END;

text_es: Create a set of SQL views to manage hotel operations. First, build a daily arrival view that links active reservations with guest details, assigned rooms, and the specific room categories. Next, formulate a housekeeping schedule view that matches occupied rooms with their assigned cleaning staff, the specific cleaning zones, and the current reservation details. Finally, create a guest folio summary that combines finalized billing accounts with the original reservation, the guest profile, and the selected premium amenities. The logic must exclusively return records where all these related details are fully populated and matched. For example, looking up a reservation returns the arrival date, guest name, room number, and room category description as a single row.
text_nat:
CREATE VIEW v_daily_arrivals AS
SELECT
    r.reservation_id,
    r.arrival_date,
    g.guest_id,
    g.last_name || ', ' || g.first_name AS guest_name,
    g.loyalty_tier,
    rm.room_number,
    rt.type_code,
    rt.description AS room_category,
    rt.base_rate,
    r.adults + r.children AS party_size
FROM Reservations AS r
INNER JOIN Guests AS g ON g.guest_id = r.guest_id
INNER JOIN Rooms AS rm ON rm.room_id = r.room_id
INNER JOIN RoomTypes AS rt ON rt.room_type_id = rm.room_type_id
WHERE r.status = 'ACTIVE';

CREATE VIEW v_housekeeping_schedule AS
SELECT
    hz.zone_id,
    hz.zone_name,
    hz.floor_number,
    rm.room_number,
    s.staff_id,
    s.last_name || ', ' || s.first_name AS attendant_name,
    a.shift_date,
    a.shift_start,
    r.reservation_id,
    r.departure_date,
    CASE WHEN r.departure_date = a.shift_date THEN 'CHECKOUT CLEAN' ELSE 'STAYOVER' END AS service_type
FROM HousekeepingAssignments AS a
INNER JOIN Rooms AS rm ON rm.room_id = a.room_id
INNER JOIN HousekeepingZones AS hz ON hz.zone_id = a.zone_id
INNER JOIN Staff AS s ON s.staff_id = a.staff_id
INNER JOIN Reservations AS r ON r.room_id = rm.room_id
WHERE rm.occupancy_status = 'OCCUPIED'
  AND r.status = 'ACTIVE'
  AND a.shift_date BETWEEN r.arrival_date AND r.departure_date;

CREATE VIEW v_guest_folio_summary AS
SELECT
    f.folio_id,
    f.closed_at,
    f.total_charges - f.total_payments AS balance_due,
    r.reservation_id,
    r.arrival_date,
    r.departure_date,
    g.last_name || ', ' || g.first_name AS guest_name,
    am.amenity_name,
    ra.quantity * am.unit_price AS amenity_total
FROM Folios AS f
INNER JOIN Reservations AS r ON r.reservation_id = f.reservation_id
INNER JOIN Guests AS g ON g.guest_id = r.guest_id
INNER JOIN ReservationAmenities AS ra ON ra.reservation_id = r.reservation_id
INNER JOIN Amenities AS am ON am.amenity_id = ra.amenity_id
WHERE f.status = 'FINALIZED'
  AND am.is_premium = 1;

SELECT
    fs.guest_name,
    fs.folio_id,
    fs.balance_due,
    SUM(fs.amenity_total) AS premium_amenity_charges
FROM v_guest_folio_summary AS fs
INNER JOIN v_daily_arrivals AS da ON da.reservation_id = fs.reservation_id
GROUP BY fs.guest_name, fs.folio_id, fs.balance_due
ORDER BY premium_amenity_charges DESC;

SELECT
    hs.room_number,
    hs.attendant_name,
    fs.guest_name,
    fs.balance_due
FROM v_housekeeping_schedule AS hs
INNER JOIN v_guest_folio_summary AS fs ON fs.reservation_id = hs.reservation_id
WHERE hs.service_type = 'CHECKOUT CLEAN'
  AND fs.balance_due > 0
ORDER BY fs.balance_due DESC;

SELECT
    da.arrival_date,
    da.guest_name,
    da.room_number,
    da.room_category,
    hs.attendant_name
FROM v_daily_arrivals AS da
INNER JOIN v_housekeeping_schedule AS hs ON hs.room_number = da.room_number
WHERE hs.shift_date = da.arrival_date
ORDER BY da.room_number;

SELECT arrival_date, guest_name, room_number, room_category
FROM v_daily_arrivals
WHERE reservation_id = 10457;

SELECT zone_name, room_number, attendant_name, service_type
FROM v_housekeeping_schedule
WHERE shift_date = DATE '2026-09-18'
ORDER BY zone_name, room_number;

text_es: Develop a SQL database script for a satellite operator. First, construct a bandwidth allocation view that connects active data contracts with the corporate clients, the assigned transponders, and the host satellites. Second, create a ground station link report that matches communication logs with the receiving ground stations, the specific satellites transmitting, and the regional network operators. Third, formulate a maintenance log view that combines scheduled service records with the affected ground stations, the assigned maintenance crews, and the specific replacement part manifests. The queries must only return rows where full linkage exists between all specified entities. For example, a contract lookup yields the contract length, client name, transponder frequency, and satellite name.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE clients (
    client_id      INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    client_name    VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    billing_region VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE satellites (
    satellite_id   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    satellite_name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL,
    orbit_slot     VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE transponders (
    transponder_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    satellite_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES satellites (satellite_id),
    frequency_mhz  DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL,
    bandwidth_mhz  DECIMAL(8, 2) NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE contracts (
    contract_id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    client_id      INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES clients (client_id),
    transponder_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES transponders (transponder_id),
    term_months    INTEGER NOT NULL,
    status         VARCHAR(12) NOT NULL
);

CREATE VIEW vw_bandwidth_allocation AS
SELECT ct.contract_id, ct.term_months, cl.client_name, cl.billing_region,
       tp.frequency_mhz, tp.bandwidth_mhz, sa.satellite_id, sa.satellite_name
FROM contracts AS ct
JOIN clients AS cl ON cl.client_id = ct.client_id
JOIN transponders AS tp ON tp.transponder_id = ct.transponder_id
JOIN satellites AS sa ON sa.satellite_id = tp.satellite_id
WHERE ct.status = 'ACTIVE';

CREATE VIEW vw_satellite_utilisation AS
SELECT sa.satellite_id, sa.satellite_name, sa.orbit_slot,
       COUNT(ct.contract_id) AS active_contracts,
       SUM(tp.bandwidth_mhz) AS allocated_mhz
FROM satellites AS sa
JOIN transponders AS tp ON tp.satellite_id = sa.satellite_id
JOIN contracts AS ct ON ct.transponder_id = tp.transponder_id
WHERE ct.status = 'ACTIVE'
GROUP BY sa.satellite_id, sa.satellite_name, sa.orbit_slot;

CREATE TABLE network_operators (
    operator_id   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    operator_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    region        VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE ground_stations (
    station_id   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    station_name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL,
    operator_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES network_operators (operator_id)
);
CREATE TABLE comm_logs (
    log_id        INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    station_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES ground_stations (station_id),
    satellite_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES satellites (satellite_id),
    contact_start TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
    signal_db     DECIMAL(6, 2) NOT NULL
);

CREATE VIEW vw_ground_station_links AS
SELECT lg.log_id, lg.contact_start, lg.signal_db, gs.station_name,
       sa.satellite_id, sa.satellite_name, op.operator_name, op.region
FROM comm_logs AS lg
JOIN ground_stations AS gs ON gs.station_id = lg.station_id
JOIN satellites AS sa ON sa.satellite_id = lg.satellite_id
JOIN network_operators AS op ON op.operator_id = gs.operator_id;

SELECT DISTINCT ba.client_name, ba.satellite_name, gl.station_name, gl.operator_name
FROM vw_bandwidth_allocation AS ba
JOIN vw_ground_station_links AS gl ON gl.satellite_id = ba.satellite_id
ORDER BY ba.client_name, gl.station_name;

CREATE TABLE crews (
    crew_id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    crew_name  VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL,
    supervisor VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE part_manifests (
    manifest_id   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    manifest_code VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
    part_count    INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE maintenance_schedules (
    service_id   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    station_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES ground_stations (station_id),
    crew_id      INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES crews (crew_id),
    manifest_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES part_manifests (manifest_id),
    service_date DATE NOT NULL,
    work_summary VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL
);

CREATE VIEW vw_maintenance_log AS
SELECT ms.service_id, ms.service_date, ms.work_summary, gs.station_id,
       gs.station_name, cr.crew_name, cr.supervisor, pm.manifest_code, pm.part_count
FROM maintenance_schedules AS ms
JOIN ground_stations AS gs ON gs.station_id = ms.station_id
JOIN crews AS cr ON cr.crew_id = ms.crew_id
JOIN part_manifests AS pm ON pm.manifest_id = ms.manifest_id;

SELECT contract_id, term_months, client_name, frequency_mhz, satellite_name
FROM vw_bandwidth_allocation
ORDER BY satellite_name, frequency_mhz;

SELECT satellite_name, orbit_slot, active_contracts, allocated_mhz
FROM vw_satellite_utilisation
ORDER BY allocated_mhz DESC;

SELECT station_name, satellite_name, operator_name, contact_start, signal_db
FROM vw_ground_station_links
WHERE signal_db < 3.0
ORDER BY contact_start DESC;

SELECT op.operator_name, ml.station_name, ml.crew_name, ml.supervisor,
       ml.manifest_code, ml.part_count, ml.service_date
FROM vw_maintenance_log AS ml
JOIN ground_stations AS gs ON gs.station_id = ml.station_id
JOIN network_operators AS op ON op.operator_id = gs.operator_id
WHERE ml.service_date >= DATE '2024-01-01'
ORDER BY op.operator_name, ml.service_date;

text_es: Create SQL queries for an urban bike share program. The first query must generate a station status report by combining docking stations with their assigned neighborhood zones, the local maintenance contractors, and the power grid connections. The second query builds a repair history view linking closed repair tickets with the serviced bicycles, the responsible mechanics, and the specific bicycle models. The third query analyzes parts consumption by matching part usage logs with the closed repair tickets, the spare parts catalog, and the parts suppliers. Ensure the logic purely isolates records with complete corresponding data in every linked table. For example, querying a station yields the station name, zone description, contractor name, and grid status.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Zones (zone_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, zone_name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL, zone_desc VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE Contractors (contractor_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, contractor_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL, zone_id INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE Stations (station_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, station_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL, dock_count INTEGER NOT NULL, zone_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE GridConnections (grid_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, station_id INTEGER NOT NULL, grid_status VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL, last_checked DATE);
CREATE TABLE BikeModels (model_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, model_name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL, frame_type VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE Bicycles (bike_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, bike_tag VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL, model_id INTEGER, home_station INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE Mechanics (mechanic_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, mechanic_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL, certification VARCHAR(40));
CREATE TABLE RepairTickets (ticket_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, bike_id INTEGER, mechanic_id INTEGER,
    opened_on DATE NOT NULL, closed_on DATE, status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE Suppliers (supplier_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, supplier_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL, lead_time_days INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE Parts (part_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, part_name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL, unit_cost DECIMAL(8,2) NOT NULL, supplier_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE PartUsage (usage_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, ticket_id INTEGER, part_id INTEGER, quantity INTEGER NOT NULL);

CREATE VIEW StationStatusReport AS
SELECT s.station_name, z.zone_desc, c.contractor_name, g.grid_status
FROM Stations AS s
INNER JOIN Zones AS z ON s.zone_id = z.zone_id
INNER JOIN Contractors AS c ON c.zone_id = z.zone_id
INNER JOIN GridConnections AS g ON g.station_id = s.station_id;

CREATE VIEW FleetPlacement AS
SELECT s.station_name, z.zone_name, bm.model_name, COUNT(*) AS bikes_docked
FROM Bicycles AS b
INNER JOIN Stations AS s ON b.home_station = s.station_id
INNER JOIN Zones AS z ON s.zone_id = z.zone_id
INNER JOIN BikeModels AS bm ON b.model_id = bm.model_id
GROUP BY s.station_name, z.zone_name, bm.model_name;

CREATE VIEW RepairHistory AS
SELECT t.ticket_id, t.closed_on, b.bike_tag, m.mechanic_name, bm.model_name
FROM RepairTickets AS t
INNER JOIN Bicycles AS b ON t.bike_id = b.bike_id
INNER JOIN Mechanics AS m ON t.mechanic_id = m.mechanic_id
INNER JOIN BikeModels AS bm ON b.model_id = bm.model_id
WHERE t.status = 'closed'
  AND t.closed_on IS NOT NULL;

CREATE VIEW MechanicWorkload AS
SELECT m.mechanic_name, m.certification, bm.frame_type, COUNT(*) AS tickets_closed
FROM RepairTickets AS t
INNER JOIN Mechanics AS m ON t.mechanic_id = m.mechanic_id
INNER JOIN Bicycles AS b ON t.bike_id = b.bike_id
INNER JOIN BikeModels AS bm ON b.model_id = bm.model_id
WHERE t.status = 'closed'
  AND t.closed_on IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY m.mechanic_name, m.certification, bm.frame_type;

CREATE VIEW PartsConsumption AS
SELECT p.part_name, sup.supplier_name, SUM(u.quantity) AS units_used,
       SUM(u.quantity * p.unit_cost) AS total_cost
FROM PartUsage AS u
INNER JOIN RepairTickets AS t ON u.ticket_id = t.ticket_id
INNER JOIN Parts AS p ON u.part_id = p.part_id
INNER JOIN Suppliers AS sup ON p.supplier_id = sup.supplier_id
WHERE t.status = 'closed'
  AND t.closed_on IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY p.part_name, sup.supplier_name;

CREATE VIEW SupplierReorderPlan AS
SELECT sup.supplier_name, sup.lead_time_days, p.part_name, SUM(u.quantity) AS units_used
FROM Suppliers AS sup
INNER JOIN Parts AS p ON p.supplier_id = sup.supplier_id
INNER JOIN PartUsage AS u ON u.part_id = p.part_id
INNER JOIN RepairTickets AS t ON u.ticket_id = t.ticket_id
WHERE t.status = 'closed'
  AND t.closed_on IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY sup.supplier_name, sup.lead_time_days, p.part_name
HAVING SUM(u.quantity) > 10;

SELECT station_name, zone_desc, contractor_name, grid_status
FROM StationStatusReport
WHERE station_name = 'Riverside Plaza';

SELECT station_name, zone_name, model_name, bikes_docked
FROM FleetPlacement
ORDER BY station_name, bikes_docked DESC;

SELECT ticket_id, bike_tag, mechanic_name, model_name
FROM RepairHistory
ORDER BY closed_on DESC;

SELECT mechanic_name, certification, frame_type, tickets_closed
FROM MechanicWorkload
ORDER BY tickets_closed DESC;

SELECT part_name, supplier_name, units_used, total_cost
FROM PartsConsumption
ORDER BY total_cost DESC;

SELECT supplier_name, lead_time_days, part_name, units_used
FROM SupplierReorderPlan
ORDER BY lead_time_days DESC, units_used DESC;

text_es: Write a SQL module to map data center infrastructure. The first view details server placement by combining active servers with their assigned racks, the enclosing data halls, and the specific hardware models. The second view analyzes thermal loads by linking cooling logs with the targeted data halls, the specific cooling units, and the responsible facility engineers. The third view maps network topology by matching bandwidth usage logs with the source servers, the top of rack network switches, and the billed corporate tenants. The logic must strictly demand matching relationships across all connected elements to guarantee valid reports. For example, checking a server yields the server IP, rack slot, hall identifier, and hardware manufacturer.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE data_halls (hall_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, hall_code VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL, floor_level INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE hardware_models (model_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, model_name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL,
    manufacturer VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL, rated_watts INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE racks (rack_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, rack_label VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    hall_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES data_halls (hall_id));
CREATE TABLE servers (server_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, server_ip VARCHAR(45) NOT NULL,
    rack_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES racks (rack_id), rack_slot INTEGER NOT NULL,
    model_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES hardware_models (model_id), is_active CHAR(1) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE facility_engineers (engineer_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, full_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    shift_code VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE cooling_units (unit_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, unit_tag VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    capacity_kw DECIMAL(8,2) NOT NULL, engineer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES facility_engineers (engineer_id));
CREATE TABLE cooling_logs (log_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, logged_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
    hall_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES data_halls (hall_id), unit_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES cooling_units (unit_id),
    inlet_temp_c DECIMAL(5,2) NOT NULL, heat_load_kw DECIMAL(8,2) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE tenants (tenant_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL, billing_plan VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE network_switches (switch_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, switch_tag VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    rack_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES racks (rack_id), uplink_gbps INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE bandwidth_logs (usage_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, sampled_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
    server_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES servers (server_id),
    switch_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES network_switches (switch_id),
    tenant_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants (tenant_id), egress_gb DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL);

CREATE VIEW vw_server_placement AS
SELECT S.server_id, S.server_ip, S.rack_slot, R.rack_label, H.hall_code, H.floor_level,
       M.model_name, M.manufacturer, M.rated_watts
FROM servers AS S
INNER JOIN racks AS R ON S.rack_id = R.rack_id
INNER JOIN data_halls AS H ON R.hall_id = H.hall_id
INNER JOIN hardware_models AS M ON S.model_id = M.model_id
WHERE S.is_active = 'Y';

CREATE VIEW vw_thermal_load AS
SELECT L.log_id, L.logged_at, H.hall_code, U.unit_tag, U.capacity_kw, L.inlet_temp_c, L.heat_load_kw,
       E.full_name AS engineer_name, E.shift_code
FROM cooling_logs AS L
INNER JOIN data_halls AS H ON L.hall_id = H.hall_id
INNER JOIN cooling_units AS U ON L.unit_id = U.unit_id
INNER JOIN facility_engineers AS E ON U.engineer_id = E.engineer_id;

CREATE VIEW vw_network_topology AS
SELECT B.usage_id, B.sampled_at, S.server_ip, W.switch_tag, W.uplink_gbps,
       T.tenant_name, T.billing_plan, B.egress_gb
FROM bandwidth_logs AS B
INNER JOIN servers AS S ON B.server_id = S.server_id
INNER JOIN network_switches AS W ON B.switch_id = W.switch_id
INNER JOIN tenants AS T ON B.tenant_id = T.tenant_id;

SELECT P.hall_code, P.installed_watts, T.total_load_kw
FROM (SELECT hall_code, SUM(rated_watts) AS installed_watts FROM vw_server_placement GROUP BY hall_code) AS P
INNER JOIN (SELECT hall_code, SUM(heat_load_kw) AS total_load_kw FROM vw_thermal_load GROUP BY hall_code) AS T
        ON P.hall_code = T.hall_code
ORDER BY T.total_load_kw DESC;

SELECT H.hall_code, T.tenant_name, SUM(B.egress_gb) AS egress_gb
FROM bandwidth_logs AS B
INNER JOIN servers AS S ON B.server_id = S.server_id
INNER JOIN racks AS R ON S.rack_id = R.rack_id
INNER JOIN data_halls AS H ON R.hall_id = H.hall_id
INNER JOIN tenants AS T ON B.tenant_id = T.tenant_id
GROUP BY H.hall_code, T.tenant_name
ORDER BY H.hall_code, egress_gb DESC;

SELECT W.switch_tag, W.uplink_gbps, COUNT(S.server_id) AS attached_servers
FROM network_switches AS W
INNER JOIN servers AS S ON W.rack_id = S.rack_id AND S.is_active = 'Y'
GROUP BY W.switch_tag, W.uplink_gbps
ORDER BY attached_servers DESC;

SELECT server_ip, rack_slot, hall_code, manufacturer
FROM vw_server_placement
ORDER BY hall_code, rack_label, rack_slot;

SELECT hall_code, unit_tag, engineer_name, MAX(inlet_temp_c) AS peak_temp_c, SUM(heat_load_kw) AS total_load_kw
FROM vw_thermal_load
GROUP BY hall_code, unit_tag, engineer_name
ORDER BY total_load_kw DESC;

SELECT tenant_name, switch_tag, SUM(egress_gb) AS billed_egress_gb
FROM vw_network_topology
GROUP BY tenant_name, switch_tag
ORDER BY tenant_name, billed_egress_gb DESC;

CREATE VIEW vw_server_placement AS

       E.full_name AS engineer_name, E.shift_code

  AND L.unit_id = U.unit_id
  AND U.engineer_id = E.engineer_id;

CREATE VIEW vw_network_topology AS
SELECT B.usage_id, B.sampled_at, S.server_ip, W.switch_tag, W.uplink_gbps,
       T.tenant_name, T.billing_plan, B.egress_gb

WHERE B.server_id = S.server_id
  AND B.switch_id = W.switch_id
  AND B.tenant_id = T.tenant_id;

SELECT P.hall_code, P.installed_watts, T.total_load_kw
FROM (SELECT hall_code, SUM(rated_watts) AS installed_watts FROM vw_server_placement GROUP BY hall_code) AS P,
     (SELECT hall_code, SUM(heat_load_kw) AS total_load_kw FROM vw_thermal_load GROUP BY hall_code) AS T
WHERE P.hall_code = T.hall_code
ORDER BY T.total_load_kw DESC;

SELECT H.hall_code, T.tenant_name, SUM(B.egress_gb) AS egress_gb
FROM bandwidth_logs AS B, servers AS S, racks AS R, data_halls AS H, tenants AS T
WHERE B.server_id = S.server_id
  AND S.rack_id = R.rack_id
  AND R.hall_id = H.hall_id
  AND B.tenant_id = T.tenant_id
GROUP BY H.hall_code, T.tenant_name
ORDER BY H.hall_code, egress_gb DESC;

SELECT W.switch_tag, W.uplink_gbps, COUNT(S.server_id) AS attached_servers
FROM network_switches AS W, servers AS S
WHERE W.rack_id = S.rack_id AND S.is_active = 'Y'
GROUP BY W.switch_tag, W.uplink_gbps
ORDER BY attached_servers DESC;

SELECT server_ip, rack_slot, hall_code, manufacturer
FROM vw_server_placement
ORDER BY hall_code, rack_label, rack_slot;

SELECT hall_code, unit_tag, engineer_name, MAX(inlet_temp_c) AS peak_temp_c, SUM(heat_load_kw) AS total_load_kw

text_es: Develop a SQL script for aviation food service. The first view must map meal assignments by linking scheduled flights with the loaded catering carts, the approved menu plans, and the destination airports. The second view tracks culinary production by combining meal preparation logs with the specific menu plans, the supervising chefs, and the industrial kitchen stations. The third view handles supply chain tracking by matching ingredient deliveries with the food suppliers, the receiving kitchens, and the quality assurance inspectors. All queries must strictly utilize intersecting relationships where complete data exists. For example, a flight lookup outputs the flight number, cart identifier, menu theme, and destination city.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Airports (airport_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, iata_code CHAR(3) NOT NULL, city VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE MenuPlans (menu_plan_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, theme VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL, calories INTEGER NOT NULL, approved CHAR(1) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE CateringCarts (cart_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, cart_code VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL, tray_capacity INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE Chefs (chef_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, full_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL, grade VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE Suppliers (supplier_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, supplier_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL, country VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE Inspectors (inspector_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, inspector_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL, certificate_no VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE Flights (flight_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, flight_number VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL, departure_time TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
    destination_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES Airports (airport_id));
CREATE TABLE Kitchens (kitchen_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, kitchen_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    airport_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES Airports (airport_id));
CREATE TABLE KitchenStations (station_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, station_label VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL,
    kitchen_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES Kitchens (kitchen_id));
CREATE TABLE MealAssignments (assignment_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tray_count INTEGER NOT NULL,
    flight_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES Flights (flight_id),
    cart_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES CateringCarts (cart_id),
    menu_plan_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES MenuPlans (menu_plan_id));
CREATE TABLE PreparationLogs (log_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, portions_made INTEGER NOT NULL, prepared_on DATE NOT NULL,
    menu_plan_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES MenuPlans (menu_plan_id),
    chef_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES Chefs (chef_id),
    station_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES KitchenStations (station_id));
CREATE TABLE IngredientDeliveries (delivery_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, ingredient VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL,
    net_weight_kg DECIMAL(9,2) NOT NULL, received_on DATE NOT NULL,
    supplier_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES Suppliers (supplier_id),
    kitchen_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES Kitchens (kitchen_id),
    inspector_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES Inspectors (inspector_id));

CREATE VIEW v_flight_meal_service AS
SELECT F.flight_number, C.cart_code, M.theme AS menu_theme, A.city AS destination_city, MA.tray_count
FROM MealAssignments AS MA
JOIN Flights AS F ON MA.flight_id = F.flight_id
JOIN CateringCarts AS C ON MA.cart_id = C.cart_id
JOIN MenuPlans AS M ON MA.menu_plan_id = M.menu_plan_id
JOIN Airports AS A ON F.destination_id = A.airport_id
WHERE M.approved = 'Y';

CREATE VIEW v_culinary_production AS
SELECT P.log_id, M.theme AS menu_theme, CH.full_name AS chef_name, S.station_label, K.kitchen_name,
       P.portions_made, P.prepared_on
FROM PreparationLogs AS P
JOIN MenuPlans AS M ON P.menu_plan_id = M.menu_plan_id
JOIN Chefs AS CH ON P.chef_id = CH.chef_id
JOIN KitchenStations AS S ON P.station_id = S.station_id
JOIN Kitchens AS K ON S.kitchen_id = K.kitchen_id;

CREATE VIEW v_supply_chain_tracking AS
SELECT D.delivery_id, SP.supplier_name, SP.country, K.kitchen_name, A.iata_code AS kitchen_airport,
       I.inspector_name, D.ingredient, D.net_weight_kg, D.received_on
FROM IngredientDeliveries AS D
JOIN Suppliers AS SP ON D.supplier_id = SP.supplier_id
JOIN Kitchens AS K ON D.kitchen_id = K.kitchen_id
JOIN Inspectors AS I ON D.inspector_id = I.inspector_id
JOIN Airports AS A ON K.airport_id = A.airport_id;

SELECT F.flight_number, C.cart_code, MA.tray_count, C.tray_capacity
FROM MealAssignments AS MA
JOIN Flights AS F ON MA.flight_id = F.flight_id
JOIN CateringCarts AS C ON MA.cart_id = C.cart_id
WHERE MA.tray_count > C.tray_capacity
ORDER BY F.flight_number, C.cart_code;

SELECT F.flight_number, M.theme AS menu_theme, MA.tray_count, SUM(P.portions_made) AS portions_ready
FROM MealAssignments AS MA
JOIN Flights AS F ON MA.flight_id = F.flight_id
JOIN MenuPlans AS M ON MA.menu_plan_id = M.menu_plan_id
JOIN PreparationLogs AS P ON M.menu_plan_id = P.menu_plan_id
WHERE P.prepared_on <= CAST(F.departure_time AS DATE)
GROUP BY F.flight_number, M.theme, MA.tray_count
ORDER BY F.flight_number;

SELECT flight_number, cart_code, menu_theme, destination_city
FROM v_flight_meal_service
ORDER BY flight_number, cart_code;

SELECT chef_name, station_label, SUM(portions_made) AS total_portions
FROM v_culinary_production
GROUP BY chef_name, station_label
ORDER BY total_portions DESC;

SELECT supplier_name, kitchen_name, inspector_name, SUM(net_weight_kg) AS kg_received
FROM v_supply_chain_tracking
GROUP BY supplier_name, kitchen_name, inspector_name
ORDER BY kg_received DESC;

text_es: Create SQL queries for clinical research data. First, construct a patient enrollment view that links active trial phases with the participating patients, the experimental drugs, and the primary research clinics. Second, build an observation report that matches daily observation logs with the evaluated patients, the administering doctors, and the specific dosage schedules. Third, generate a compliance audit by combining safety incident reports with the affected trial phases, the reviewing ethics committees, and the assigned regulatory officers. The queries must exclusively combine rows that have fully populated matches in every referenced table. For example, checking a phase yields the phase number, patient initials, drug compound name, and clinic address.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE clinics (clinic_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, clinic_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL, address VARCHAR(160) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE drugs (drug_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, compound_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE patients (patient_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, initials CHAR(3) NOT NULL, birth_year INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE doctors (doctor_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, doctor_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL, license_no VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE ethics_committees (committee_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, committee_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE officers (officer_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, officer_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL, agency VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE trial_phases (phase_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, phase_number INTEGER NOT NULL, status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    drug_id INTEGER REFERENCES drugs(drug_id), clinic_id INTEGER REFERENCES clinics(clinic_id),
    committee_id INTEGER REFERENCES ethics_committees(committee_id));
CREATE TABLE enrollments (enrollment_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, phase_id INTEGER REFERENCES trial_phases(phase_id),
    patient_id INTEGER REFERENCES patients(patient_id), enrolled_on DATE NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE dosage_schedules (schedule_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, enrollment_id INTEGER REFERENCES enrollments(enrollment_id),
    milligrams NUMERIC(8,2) NOT NULL, frequency VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE observation_logs (log_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, schedule_id INTEGER REFERENCES dosage_schedules(schedule_id),
    doctor_id INTEGER REFERENCES doctors(doctor_id), logged_on DATE NOT NULL, finding VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE safety_incidents (incident_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, phase_id INTEGER REFERENCES trial_phases(phase_id),
    officer_id INTEGER REFERENCES officers(officer_id), severity VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL, reported_on DATE NOT NULL);

CREATE VIEW v_patient_enrollment AS
SELECT tp.phase_number, p.initials, d.compound_name, c.address, e.enrolled_on
FROM trial_phases AS tp
JOIN enrollments AS e ON e.phase_id = tp.phase_id
JOIN patients AS p ON p.patient_id = e.patient_id
JOIN drugs AS d ON d.drug_id = tp.drug_id
JOIN clinics AS c ON c.clinic_id = tp.clinic_id
WHERE tp.status = 'ACTIVE';

CREATE VIEW v_observation_report AS
SELECT ol.logged_on, ol.finding, p.initials, doc.doctor_name, ds.milligrams, ds.frequency
FROM observation_logs AS ol
JOIN dosage_schedules AS ds ON ds.schedule_id = ol.schedule_id
JOIN enrollments AS e ON e.enrollment_id = ds.enrollment_id
JOIN patients AS p ON p.patient_id = e.patient_id
JOIN doctors AS doc ON doc.doctor_id = ol.doctor_id;

CREATE VIEW v_compliance_audit AS
SELECT si.incident_id, si.severity, si.reported_on, tp.phase_number,
       ec.committee_name, o.officer_name, o.agency
FROM safety_incidents AS si
JOIN trial_phases AS tp ON tp.phase_id = si.phase_id
JOIN ethics_committees AS ec ON ec.committee_id = tp.committee_id
JOIN officers AS o ON o.officer_id = si.officer_id;

SELECT tp.phase_number, c.clinic_name, COUNT(DISTINCT e.patient_id) AS enrolled_patients
FROM trial_phases AS tp
JOIN clinics AS c ON c.clinic_id = tp.clinic_id
JOIN enrollments AS e ON e.phase_id = tp.phase_id
GROUP BY tp.phase_number, c.clinic_name
ORDER BY enrolled_patients DESC;

SELECT d.compound_name, o.agency, si.severity, COUNT(*) AS incident_count
FROM safety_incidents AS si
JOIN trial_phases AS tp ON tp.phase_id = si.phase_id
JOIN drugs AS d ON d.drug_id = tp.drug_id
JOIN officers AS o ON o.officer_id = si.officer_id
GROUP BY d.compound_name, o.agency, si.severity
ORDER BY d.compound_name, incident_count DESC;

SELECT c.clinic_name, doc.doctor_name, AVG(ds.milligrams) AS mean_dose, COUNT(ol.log_id) AS logs_recorded
FROM observation_logs AS ol
JOIN doctors AS doc ON doc.doctor_id = ol.doctor_id
JOIN dosage_schedules AS ds ON ds.schedule_id = ol.schedule_id
JOIN enrollments AS e ON e.enrollment_id = ds.enrollment_id
JOIN trial_phases AS tp ON tp.phase_id = e.phase_id
JOIN clinics AS c ON c.clinic_id = tp.clinic_id
GROUP BY c.clinic_name, doc.doctor_name
ORDER BY logs_recorded DESC;

SELECT phase_number, initials, compound_name, address
FROM v_patient_enrollment
ORDER BY phase_number, initials;

SELECT initials, doctor_name, milligrams, frequency, finding
FROM v_observation_report
WHERE logged_on >= DATE '2024-01-01'
ORDER BY logged_on DESC;

SELECT phase_number, committee_name, officer_name, agency, COUNT(*) AS incident_count
FROM v_compliance_audit
WHERE severity IN ('SERIOUS', 'CRITICAL')
GROUP BY phase_number, committee_name, officer_name, agency
ORDER BY incident_count DESC;

SELECT c.clinic_name, doc.doctor_name, AVG(ds.milligrams) AS mean_dose, COUNT(ol.log_id) AS logs_recorded

text_es: Create a set of SQL views to document a telecom grid. The first view maps the physical network by linking laid fiber cables with the connection nodes, the specific city sectors, and the cable manufacturers. The second view audits installation work by combining splicing records with the installed fiber cables, the splicing technicians, and the testing equipment used. The third view tracks active service by matching customer connections with the specific connection nodes, the installed router equipment, and the subscribed service plans. Restrict the results entirely to instances where the data perfectly matches across all joined sets. For example, a cable lookup returns the cable length, node identifier, sector name, and manufacturer brand.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Sectors (sector_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, sector_name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL);

CREATE TABLE Manufacturers (manufacturer_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, brand VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL);

CREATE TABLE Nodes (node_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, node_code VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    sector_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES Sectors(sector_id));

CREATE TABLE FiberCables (cable_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, length_m DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,
    node_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES Nodes(node_id),
    manufacturer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES Manufacturers(manufacturer_id));

CREATE TABLE Technicians (technician_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tech_name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL,
    certification VARCHAR(30));

CREATE TABLE TestEquipment (equipment_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, equipment_name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL,
    calibrated_on DATE);

CREATE TABLE SpliceRecords (splice_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    cable_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES FiberCables(cable_id),
    technician_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES Technicians(technician_id),
    equipment_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES TestEquipment(equipment_id),
    splice_date DATE NOT NULL, loss_db DECIMAL(5,3) NOT NULL);

CREATE TABLE ServicePlans (plan_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, plan_name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL,
    downstream_mb INTEGER NOT NULL);

CREATE TABLE Routers (router_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, model VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL, firmware VARCHAR(20));

CREATE TABLE CustomerConnections (connection_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    node_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES Nodes(node_id),
    router_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES Routers(router_id),
    plan_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES ServicePlans(plan_id), activated_on DATE NOT NULL);

CREATE VIEW vw_physical_network AS
SELECT FC.cable_id, FC.length_m, N.node_code, S.sector_name, M.brand
FROM FiberCables AS FC
JOIN Nodes AS N ON FC.node_id = N.node_id
JOIN Sectors AS S ON N.sector_id = S.sector_id
JOIN Manufacturers AS M ON FC.manufacturer_id = M.manufacturer_id;

CREATE VIEW vw_installation_audit AS
SELECT SR.splice_id, SR.splice_date, SR.loss_db, FC.cable_id, FC.length_m,
       T.tech_name, T.certification, TE.equipment_name, TE.calibrated_on
FROM SpliceRecords AS SR
JOIN FiberCables AS FC ON SR.cable_id = FC.cable_id
JOIN Technicians AS T ON SR.technician_id = T.technician_id
JOIN TestEquipment AS TE ON SR.equipment_id = TE.equipment_id;

CREATE VIEW vw_active_service AS
SELECT CC.connection_id, CC.customer_name, CC.activated_on, N.node_code,
       R.model AS router_model, R.firmware, P.plan_name, P.downstream_mb
FROM CustomerConnections AS CC
JOIN Nodes AS N ON CC.node_id = N.node_id
JOIN Routers AS R ON CC.router_id = R.router_id
JOIN ServicePlans AS P ON CC.plan_id = P.plan_id;

CREATE VIEW vw_sector_demand AS
SELECT S.sector_name, COUNT(CC.connection_id) AS subscriber_count,
       SUM(P.downstream_mb) AS committed_downstream_mb
FROM Sectors AS S
JOIN Nodes AS N ON S.sector_id = N.sector_id
JOIN CustomerConnections AS CC ON N.node_id = CC.node_id
JOIN ServicePlans AS P ON CC.plan_id = P.plan_id
GROUP BY S.sector_name;

CREATE VIEW vw_technician_workload AS
SELECT T.tech_name, T.certification, COUNT(SR.splice_id) AS splices_done,
       MAX(SR.splice_date) AS last_splice, AVG(SR.loss_db) AS mean_loss_db
FROM Technicians AS T
JOIN SpliceRecords AS SR ON T.technician_id = SR.technician_id
JOIN FiberCables AS FC ON SR.cable_id = FC.cable_id
JOIN Nodes AS N ON FC.node_id = N.node_id
GROUP BY T.tech_name, T.certification;

SELECT PN.sector_name, PN.brand, SD.subscriber_count, SD.committed_downstream_mb,
       SUM(PN.length_m) AS cable_metres, AVG(IA.loss_db) AS mean_splice_loss
FROM vw_physical_network AS PN
JOIN vw_installation_audit AS IA ON PN.cable_id = IA.cable_id
JOIN vw_sector_demand AS SD ON PN.sector_name = SD.sector_name
GROUP BY PN.sector_name, PN.brand, SD.subscriber_count, SD.committed_downstream_mb
ORDER BY PN.sector_name, PN.brand;

    plan_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES ServicePlans(plan_id), activated_on DATE NOT NULL);

CREATE VIEW vw_physical_network AS
SELECT FC.cable_id, FC.length_m, N.node_code, S.sector_name, M.brand
FROM FiberCables AS FC, Nodes AS N, Sectors AS S, Manufacturers AS M
WHERE FC.node_id = N.node_id
AND N.sector_id = S.sector_id
AND FC.manufacturer_id = M.manufacturer_id;

CREATE VIEW vw_installation_audit AS
SELECT SR.splice_id, SR.splice_date, SR.loss_db, FC.cable_id, FC.length_m,
       T.tech_name, T.certification, TE.equipment_name, TE.calibrated_on
FROM SpliceRecords AS SR, FiberCables AS FC, Technicians AS T, TestEquipment AS TE
WHERE SR.cable_id = FC.cable_id
AND SR.technician_id = T.technician_id
AND SR.equipment_id = TE.equipment_id;

CREATE VIEW vw_active_service AS
SELECT CC.connection_id, CC.customer_name, CC.activated_on, N.node_code,
       R.model AS router_model, R.firmware, P.plan_name, P.downstream_mb
FROM CustomerConnections AS CC, Nodes AS N, Routers AS R, ServicePlans AS P
WHERE CC.node_id = N.node_id
AND CC.router_id = R.router_id
AND CC.plan_id = P.plan_id;

CREATE VIEW vw_sector_demand AS
SELECT S.sector_name, COUNT(CC.connection_id) AS subscriber_count,
       SUM(P.downstream_mb) AS committed_downstream_mb
FROM Sectors AS S, Nodes AS N, CustomerConnections AS CC, ServicePlans AS P
WHERE S.sector_id = N.sector_id
AND N.node_id = CC.node_id
AND CC.plan_id = P.plan_id
GROUP BY S.sector_name;

CREATE VIEW vw_technician_workload AS
SELECT T.tech_name, T.certification, COUNT(SR.splice_id) AS splices_done,
       MAX(SR.splice_date) AS last_splice, AVG(SR.loss_db) AS mean_loss_db
FROM Technicians AS T, SpliceRecords AS SR, FiberCables AS FC, Nodes AS N
WHERE T.technician_id = SR.technician_id
AND SR.cable_id = FC.cable_id
AND FC.node_id = N.node_id
GROUP BY T.tech_name, T.certification;

SELECT PN.sector_name, PN.brand, SD.subscriber_count, SD.committed_downstream_mb,

AND PN.sector_name = SD.sector_name
GROUP BY PN.sector_name, PN.brand, SD.subscriber_count, SD.committed_downstream_mb
ORDER BY PN.sector_name, PN.brand;

text_es: Write a SQL script to manage emergency logistics. The first view maps regional aid by linking deployed supply pallets with the receiving relief shelters, the designated disaster zones, and the donor aid organizations. The second view tracks transit routes by combining delivery manifests with the transport trucks, the volunteer drivers, and the origin warehouses. The third view monitors camp capacities by matching daily census logs with the specific relief shelters, the assigned camp coordinators, and the local medical teams. Require the logic to purely return data where relationships are fully defined across all linked groups. For example, a pallet query outputs the pallet contents, shelter name, zone region, and organization name.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE aid_organizations (organization_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, organization_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE disaster_zones (zone_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, zone_region VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE relief_shelters (shelter_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, shelter_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    zone_id INTEGER REFERENCES disaster_zones (zone_id));
CREATE TABLE supply_pallets (pallet_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, pallet_contents VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
    shelter_id INTEGER REFERENCES relief_shelters (shelter_id),
    organization_id INTEGER REFERENCES aid_organizations (organization_id));
CREATE TABLE origin_warehouses (warehouse_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, warehouse_city VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE transport_trucks (truck_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, plate_code VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    load_tonnes DECIMAL(6,2));
CREATE TABLE volunteer_drivers (driver_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, driver_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE delivery_manifests (manifest_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, depart_on DATE NOT NULL,
    destination_shelter_id INTEGER REFERENCES relief_shelters (shelter_id),
    truck_id INTEGER REFERENCES transport_trucks (truck_id),
    driver_id INTEGER REFERENCES volunteer_drivers (driver_id),
    warehouse_id INTEGER REFERENCES origin_warehouses (warehouse_id));
CREATE TABLE camp_coordinators (coordinator_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, coordinator_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE medical_teams (team_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, team_label VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL, clinic_beds INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE census_logs (log_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, log_date DATE NOT NULL, head_count INTEGER NOT NULL,
    shelter_id INTEGER REFERENCES relief_shelters (shelter_id),
    coordinator_id INTEGER REFERENCES camp_coordinators (coordinator_id),
    team_id INTEGER REFERENCES medical_teams (team_id));

CREATE VIEW regional_aid_map AS
SELECT p.pallet_contents, s.shelter_name, z.zone_region, o.organization_name
FROM supply_pallets AS p
JOIN relief_shelters AS s ON p.shelter_id = s.shelter_id
JOIN disaster_zones AS z ON s.zone_id = z.zone_id
JOIN aid_organizations AS o ON p.organization_id = o.organization_id;

CREATE VIEW transit_routes AS
SELECT m.manifest_id, m.depart_on, t.plate_code, t.load_tonnes,
       d.driver_name, w.warehouse_city, s.shelter_name
FROM delivery_manifests AS m
JOIN transport_trucks AS t ON m.truck_id = t.truck_id
JOIN volunteer_drivers AS d ON m.driver_id = d.driver_id
JOIN origin_warehouses AS w ON m.warehouse_id = w.warehouse_id
JOIN relief_shelters AS s ON m.destination_shelter_id = s.shelter_id;

CREATE VIEW camp_capacity_monitor AS
SELECT c.log_date, c.head_count, s.shelter_name,
       k.coordinator_name, t.team_label, t.clinic_beds
FROM census_logs AS c
JOIN relief_shelters AS s ON c.shelter_id = s.shelter_id
JOIN camp_coordinators AS k ON c.coordinator_id = k.coordinator_id
JOIN medical_teams AS t ON c.team_id = t.team_id;

SELECT cm.shelter_name, cm.log_date, cm.head_count, cm.clinic_beds,
       tr.plate_code, tr.driver_name, tr.warehouse_city
FROM camp_capacity_monitor AS cm
JOIN transit_routes AS tr ON cm.shelter_name = tr.shelter_name
                         AND cm.log_date = tr.depart_on
WHERE cm.head_count > cm.clinic_beds
ORDER BY cm.log_date, cm.shelter_name;

SELECT w.warehouse_city, t.plate_code, COUNT(*) AS trips, SUM(t.load_tonnes) AS tonnes_dispatched
FROM delivery_manifests AS m
JOIN origin_warehouses AS w ON m.warehouse_id = w.warehouse_id
JOIN transport_trucks AS t ON m.truck_id = t.truck_id
GROUP BY w.warehouse_city, t.plate_code
ORDER BY tonnes_dispatched DESC;

SELECT s.shelter_name, z.zone_region, k.coordinator_name, MAX(c.head_count) AS peak_head_count
FROM census_logs AS c
JOIN relief_shelters AS s ON c.shelter_id = s.shelter_id
JOIN disaster_zones AS z ON s.zone_id = z.zone_id
JOIN camp_coordinators AS k ON c.coordinator_id = k.coordinator_id
WHERE s.shelter_id NOT IN (SELECT shelter_id FROM supply_pallets WHERE shelter_id IS NOT NULL)
GROUP BY s.shelter_name, z.zone_region, k.coordinator_name
ORDER BY peak_head_count DESC;

SELECT ram.organization_name, ram.zone_region, tr.warehouse_city, COUNT(*) AS linked_pallets
FROM regional_aid_map AS ram
JOIN transit_routes AS tr ON ram.shelter_name = tr.shelter_name
GROUP BY ram.organization_name, ram.zone_region, tr.warehouse_city
ORDER BY ram.organization_name, linked_pallets DESC;

text_es: Develop a SQL module for emergency response analysis. First, create a dispatch summary view that links closed incidents with the responding fire engines, the specific neighborhoods, and the categorized hazard types. Second, build a station readiness report that matches apparatus maintenance logs with the specific fire engines, the home fire stations, and the fleet mechanics. Third, generate a command overview by combining incident command logs with the major incidents, the assigned battalion chiefs, and the communication channels used. The queries must only combine records that have explicitly matching counterparts in all referenced categories. For example, an incident lookup returns the incident time, engine callsign, neighborhood name, and hazard description.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Neighborhoods (
  neighborhood_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, neighborhood_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL);

CREATE TABLE HazardTypes (
  hazard_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, hazard_category VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL,
  hazard_description VARCHAR(160) NOT NULL);

CREATE TABLE Stations (
  station_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, station_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL, district VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL);

CREATE TABLE Engines (
  engine_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, callsign VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
  station_id INTEGER REFERENCES Stations (station_id));

CREATE TABLE Incidents (
  incident_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, reported_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
  status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL, alarm_level INTEGER NOT NULL,
  engine_id INTEGER REFERENCES Engines (engine_id),
  neighborhood_id INTEGER REFERENCES Neighborhoods (neighborhood_id),
  hazard_id INTEGER REFERENCES HazardTypes (hazard_id));

CREATE TABLE Mechanics (
  mechanic_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, full_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL, shift VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL);

CREATE TABLE MaintenanceLogs (
  log_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, serviced_on DATE NOT NULL, work_summary VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
  out_of_service_hours NUMERIC(6,2) NOT NULL, engine_id INTEGER REFERENCES Engines (engine_id),
  mechanic_id INTEGER REFERENCES Mechanics (mechanic_id));

CREATE TABLE BattalionChiefs (
  chief_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, chief_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL, battalion VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL);

CREATE TABLE CommChannels (
  channel_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, channel_code VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL, frequency_mhz NUMERIC(7,3) NOT NULL);

CREATE TABLE CommandLogs (
  command_log_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, logged_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL, directive VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
  incident_id INTEGER REFERENCES Incidents (incident_id),
  chief_id INTEGER REFERENCES BattalionChiefs (chief_id),
  channel_id INTEGER REFERENCES CommChannels (channel_id));

CREATE VIEW DispatchSummary AS
SELECT I.incident_id, I.reported_at, E.callsign, N.neighborhood_name, H.hazard_description
FROM Incidents AS I
JOIN Engines AS E ON I.engine_id = E.engine_id
JOIN Neighborhoods AS N ON I.neighborhood_id = N.neighborhood_id
JOIN HazardTypes AS H ON I.hazard_id = H.hazard_id
WHERE I.status = 'CLOSED';

CREATE VIEW StationReadiness AS
SELECT S.station_name, S.district, E.callsign, M.serviced_on, M.work_summary,
       M.out_of_service_hours, MEC.full_name AS mechanic_name
FROM MaintenanceLogs AS M
JOIN Engines AS E ON M.engine_id = E.engine_id
JOIN Stations AS S ON E.station_id = S.station_id
JOIN Mechanics AS MEC ON M.mechanic_id = MEC.mechanic_id;

CREATE VIEW CommandOverview AS
SELECT C.incident_id, C.logged_at, C.directive, I.reported_at, I.alarm_level,
       B.chief_name, B.battalion, CH.channel_code
FROM CommandLogs AS C
JOIN Incidents AS I ON C.incident_id = I.incident_id
JOIN BattalionChiefs AS B ON C.chief_id = B.chief_id
JOIN CommChannels AS CH ON C.channel_id = CH.channel_id
WHERE I.alarm_level >= 3;

CREATE VIEW HazardLoadByStation AS
SELECT S.station_name, S.district, H.hazard_category, COUNT(*) AS closed_incidents
FROM Incidents AS I
JOIN Engines AS E ON I.engine_id = E.engine_id
JOIN Stations AS S ON E.station_id = S.station_id
JOIN HazardTypes AS H ON I.hazard_id = H.hazard_id
WHERE I.status = 'CLOSED'
GROUP BY S.station_name, S.district, H.hazard_category;

CREATE VIEW IncidentCommandBrief AS
SELECT D.reported_at, D.callsign, D.neighborhood_name, D.hazard_description,
       C.chief_name, C.battalion, C.channel_code, C.directive
FROM DispatchSummary AS D
JOIN CommandOverview AS C ON D.incident_id = C.incident_id;

SELECT reported_at, callsign, neighborhood_name, hazard_description FROM DispatchSummary
WHERE neighborhood_name = 'Riverside' ORDER BY reported_at DESC;

SELECT station_name, callsign, serviced_on, mechanic_name, out_of_service_hours
FROM StationReadiness WHERE district = 'North' ORDER BY serviced_on DESC;

SELECT station_name, hazard_category, closed_incidents FROM HazardLoadByStation
WHERE closed_incidents > 5 ORDER BY closed_incidents DESC;

SELECT reported_at, callsign, chief_name, channel_code, directive FROM IncidentCommandBrief
WHERE channel_code = 'TAC-2' ORDER BY reported_at;

text_es: Write a script that creates three views for a yoga studio. The first view must retrieve upcoming class schedules by linking classes, instructors, room assignments, and class types, returning the instructor name, room number, and type description, restricted to classes scheduled in the morning. The second view tracks attendance by combining member profiles, booking records, payment transactions, and membership tiers to show the member name, booking date, and tier level for all paid bookings where the tier is premium. The third view monitors equipment by joining studio props, damage reports, replacement orders, and supplier catalogs to output the prop name, report date, and supplier name, but only for items supplied by local vendors. Only include records that have complete associations across all specified tables. Example input: classes scheduled at nine in the morning, a premium member booking a class, a local vendor replacing a broken mat. Example output: instructor Jane in room five for vinyasa, member John on Tuesday for premium, mat reported on Monday from local vendor.
text_nat:
CREATE VIEW UpcomingMorningClasses AS
SELECT
    I.InstructorName,
    R.RoomNumber,
    CT.TypeDescription,
    C.ScheduledAt
FROM Classes AS C
INNER JOIN Instructors AS I ON C.InstructorID = I.InstructorID
INNER JOIN RoomAssignments AS RA ON C.ClassID = RA.ClassID
INNER JOIN Rooms AS R ON RA.RoomID = R.RoomID

text_es: Write a script that constructs three views for a comic book store. The first view manages pull lists by linking subscriber profiles, subscription preferences, comic series, and publisher catalogs, returning the subscriber name, series title, and publisher name for active pulls where the publisher is independent. The second view tracks special orders by combining customer requests, order shipments, distributor invoices, and receiving logs to show the request date, shipment tracking number, and receiving staff name for expedited orders. The third view analyzes back issue sales by joining physical bins, individual issues, grading conditions, and sales receipts to output the bin location, issue number, and sale price for items graded as mint condition. Only include records that have all associated details. Example input: an independent comic pulled for Dave, an expedited order received by staff Eve, a mint condition issue sold from bin three. Example output: Dave pulling hero quest by independent, monday request tracked as one two three received by Eve, bin three issue five sold for twenty.
text_nat:
CREATE VIEW ActivePullList AS
SELECT
    S.subscriber_name,
    CS.series_title,
    P.publisher_name
FROM Subscribers AS S
INNER JOIN Subscriptions AS SUB ON S.subscriber_id = SUB.subscriber_id
INNER JOIN ComicSeries AS CS ON SUB.series_id = CS.series_id
INNER JOIN Publishers AS P ON CS.publisher_id = P.publisher_id
WHERE SUB.is_active = 1
  AND P.is_independent = 1;

CREATE VIEW ExpeditedSpecialOrders AS
SELECT
    CR.request_date,
    OS.tracking_number,
    ST.staff_name
FROM CustomerRequests AS CR
INNER JOIN OrderShipments AS OS ON CR.request_id = OS.request_id
INNER JOIN DistributorInvoices AS DI ON OS.shipment_id = DI.shipment_id
INNER JOIN ReceivingLogs AS RL ON DI.invoice_id = RL.invoice_id
INNER JOIN Staff AS ST ON RL.received_by_staff_id = ST.staff_id
WHERE CR.is_expedited = 1;

CREATE VIEW MintBackIssueSales AS
SELECT
    B.bin_location,
    I.issue_number,
    SR.sale_price
FROM Bins AS B
INNER JOIN Issues AS I ON B.bin_id = I.bin_id
INNER JOIN GradingConditions AS GC ON I.grade_id = GC.grade_id
INNER JOIN SalesReceipts AS SR ON I.issue_id = SR.issue_id
WHERE GC.condition_name = 'Mint';

-- Pull volume per publisher, used when placing weekly distributor orders.
SELECT
    P.publisher_name,
    COUNT(*) AS pull_count
FROM Publishers AS P
INNER JOIN ComicSeries AS CS ON P.publisher_id = CS.publisher_id
INNER JOIN Subscriptions AS SUB ON CS.series_id = SUB.series_id
WHERE SUB.is_active = 1
GROUP BY P.publisher_name
ORDER BY pull_count DESC, P.publisher_name;

-- Receiving workload per staff member for expedited special orders.
SELECT
    ST.staff_name,
    COUNT(*) AS shipments_received
FROM Staff AS ST
INNER JOIN ReceivingLogs AS RL ON ST.staff_id = RL.received_by_staff_id
INNER JOIN DistributorInvoices AS DI ON RL.invoice_id = DI.invoice_id
INNER JOIN OrderShipments AS OS ON DI.shipment_id = OS.shipment_id
INNER JOIN CustomerRequests AS CR ON OS.request_id = CR.request_id
WHERE CR.is_expedited = 1
GROUP BY ST.staff_name
ORDER BY shipments_received DESC, ST.staff_name;

SELECT
    subscriber_name,
    series_title,
    publisher_name
FROM ActivePullList
ORDER BY subscriber_name, series_title;

SELECT
    request_date,
    tracking_number,
    staff_name
FROM ExpeditedSpecialOrders
ORDER BY request_date;

SELECT
    bin_location,
    issue_number,
    sale_price
FROM MintBackIssueSales
ORDER BY bin_location, issue_number;

text_es: Write a script that establishes three views for a surfing school. The first view details scheduled lessons by linking surfing instructors, lesson slots, beach locations, and ocean condition reports, returning the instructor name, lesson time, beach name, and wave height for days with offshore winds. The second view tracks student progression by combining student profiles, skill assessments, certificate levels, and grading examiners to show the student name, assessment date, and examiner name for students passing the intermediate level. The third view manages surfboard rentals by joining rental boards, board categories, customer waivers, and return inspections to output the board identifier, category name, and inspection result for boards categorized as longboards. Ensure only records with complete links across all tables are included. Example input: a morning lesson with offshore winds, a student passing the intermediate test with examiner Hal, a longboard returned without damage. Example output: instructor Ian at nine at south beach with two foot waves, student Jill on tuesday with Hal, board five longboard returned clean.
text_nat:
CREATE VIEW scheduled_lessons_offshore AS
SELECT
    i.instructor_name,
    s.lesson_time,
    b.beach_name,
    c.wave_height
FROM lesson_slots AS s
JOIN surf_instructors AS i ON s.instructor_id = i.instructor_id
JOIN beach_locations AS b ON s.beach_id = b.beach_id
JOIN ocean_conditions AS c ON c.beach_id = b.beach_id
    AND c.report_date = s.lesson_date
WHERE c.wind_direction = 'offshore';

CREATE VIEW student_intermediate_progress AS
SELECT
    st.student_name,
    a.assessment_date,
    e.examiner_name
FROM skill_assessments AS a
JOIN student_profiles AS st ON a.student_id = st.student_id
JOIN certificate_levels AS cl ON a.level_id = cl.level_id
JOIN grading_examiners AS e ON a.examiner_id = e.examiner_id
WHERE cl.level_name = 'intermediate'
  AND a.result = 'pass';

CREATE VIEW longboard_rental_returns AS
SELECT
    rb.board_code,
    bc.category_name,
    ri.inspection_result
FROM rental_boards AS rb
JOIN board_categories AS bc ON rb.category_id = bc.category_id
JOIN customer_waivers AS cw ON cw.board_id = rb.board_id
JOIN return_inspections AS ri ON ri.waiver_id = cw.waiver_id
WHERE bc.category_name = 'longboard';

SELECT
    l.instructor_name,
    l.lesson_time,
    l.beach_name,
    l.wave_height,
    b.beach_region
FROM scheduled_lessons_offshore AS l
JOIN beach_locations AS b ON l.beach_name = b.beach_name
ORDER BY l.lesson_time;

SELECT
    p.student_name,
    p.assessment_date,
    p.examiner_name,
    sp.home_break
FROM student_intermediate_progress AS p
JOIN student_profiles AS sp ON p.student_name = sp.student_name
ORDER BY p.assessment_date;

SELECT
    r.board_code,
    r.category_name,
    r.inspection_result,
    rb.length_feet
FROM longboard_rental_returns AS r
JOIN rental_boards AS rb ON r.board_code = rb.board_code
ORDER BY r.board_code;

text_es: Write a script generating three views for an escape room venue. The first view analyzes room schedules by linking puzzle rooms, booking slots, player groups, and game masters, returning the room theme, slot time, group name, and game master name for slots occurring on weekends. The second view tracks puzzle resets by combining room props, reset checklists, maintenance staff, and inspection logs to show the prop name, checklist item, staff name, and inspection time for items marked as fragile. The third view monitors promotional events by joining marketing campaigns, promo codes, applied transactions, and feedback surveys to output the campaign name, transaction date, and survey rating for campaigns targeting corporate teams. Include only records where all related entities exist. Example input: a weekend booking for the pirate room, a fragile prop reset by staff Ken, a corporate team using a summer promo code. Example output: pirate room at noon for team alpha with master Leo, glass vase reset by Ken at one, summer promo on friday rated five.
text_nat:
CREATE VIEW weekend_room_schedule AS
SELECT
    pr.theme            AS room_theme,
    bs.slot_time        AS slot_time,
    pg.group_name       AS group_name,
    gm.full_name        AS game_master_name
FROM puzzle_rooms AS pr
JOIN booking_slots AS bs ON bs.room_id = pr.room_id
JOIN player_groups AS pg ON pg.group_id = bs.group_id
JOIN game_masters AS gm ON gm.master_id = bs.master_id
WHERE DAYOFWEEK(bs.slot_date) IN (1, 7);

CREATE VIEW fragile_prop_resets AS
SELECT
    rp.prop_name            AS prop_name,
    rc.checklist_item       AS checklist_item,
    ms.full_name            AS staff_name,
    il.inspected_at         AS inspection_time
FROM room_props AS rp
JOIN reset_checklists AS rc ON rc.prop_id = rp.prop_id
JOIN maintenance_staff AS ms ON ms.staff_id = rc.staff_id
JOIN inspection_logs AS il ON il.checklist_id = rc.checklist_id
WHERE rp.is_fragile = 1;

CREATE VIEW corporate_promo_performance AS
SELECT
    mc.campaign_name        AS campaign_name,
    t.transaction_date      AS transaction_date,
    fs.rating               AS survey_rating
FROM marketing_campaigns AS mc
JOIN promo_codes AS pc ON pc.campaign_id = mc.campaign_id
JOIN transactions AS t ON t.promo_code_id = pc.promo_code_id
JOIN feedback_surveys AS fs ON fs.transaction_id = t.transaction_id
WHERE mc.target_segment = 'corporate teams';

SELECT
    ws.game_master_name     AS game_master_name,
    gm.contact_email        AS contact_email,
    COUNT(*)                AS weekend_slot_count
FROM weekend_room_schedule AS ws
JOIN game_masters AS gm ON gm.full_name = ws.game_master_name
GROUP BY ws.game_master_name, gm.contact_email
ORDER BY weekend_slot_count DESC;

SELECT
    fp.prop_name        AS prop_name,
    fp.checklist_item   AS checklist_item,
    pr.theme            AS room_theme,
    fp.inspection_time  AS inspection_time
FROM fragile_prop_resets AS fp
JOIN room_props AS rp ON rp.prop_name = fp.prop_name
JOIN puzzle_rooms AS pr ON pr.room_id = rp.room_id
ORDER BY pr.theme, fp.inspection_time;

SELECT
    cp.campaign_name        AS campaign_name,
    mc.budget               AS budget,
    AVG(cp.survey_rating)   AS average_rating
FROM corporate_promo_performance AS cp
JOIN marketing_campaigns AS mc ON mc.campaign_name = cp.campaign_name
GROUP BY cp.campaign_name, mc.budget

CREATE VIEW ConversationalSessionOverview AS
SELECT
    c.course_name,
    m.module_topic,
    s.student_name,
    t.tutor_name
FROM Courses AS c
JOIN Modules AS m ON m.course_id = c.course_id
JOIN Enrollments AS e ON e.course_id = c.course_id
JOIN Students AS s ON s.student_id = e.student_id
JOIN ModuleAssignments AS ma ON ma.module_id = m.module_id
JOIN Tutors AS t ON t.tutor_id = ma.tutor_id
WHERE m.skill_focus = 'Conversational';

CREATE VIEW PronunciationLabTickets AS
SELECT
    w.workstation_number,
    h.headset_model,
    st.staff_name
FROM Workstations AS w
JOIN Headsets AS h ON h.workstation_id = w.workstation_id
JOIN MaintenanceTickets AS mt ON mt.headset_id = h.headset_id
JOIN SupportStaff AS st ON st.staff_id = mt.staff_id
WHERE mt.issue_category = 'Microphone Failure';

CREATE VIEW EuropeanStudyAbroadApplications AS
SELECT
    a.applicant_name,
    u.university_name,
    ds.submission_date
FROM Applicants AS a
JOIN Applications AS ap ON ap.applicant_id = a.applicant_id
JOIN PartnerUniversities AS u ON u.university_id = ap.university_id
JOIN VisaRequirements AS vr ON vr.university_id = u.university_id
JOIN DocumentSubmissions AS ds ON ds.application_id = ap.application_id
WHERE u.region = 'Europe'
  AND ds.document_type = vr.required_document;
