CREATE TABLE Agents (agent_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, agent_name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL, agent_contact VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE Comedians (comedian_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, comedian_name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL, agent_id INTEGER REFERENCES Agents (agent_id));
CREATE TABLE Shows (show_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, show_date VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL, category VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE StageTimes (stage_time_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, show_id INTEGER REFERENCES Shows (show_id), comedian_id INTEGER REFERENCES Comedians (comedian_id), slot_minute INTEGER NOT NULL);

CREATE VIEW PerformanceLineups AS
SELECT S.show_date,
       C.comedian_name,
       A.agent_contact
FROM Shows AS S
INNER JOIN StageTimes AS ST ON S.show_id = ST.show_id
INNER JOIN Comedians AS C ON ST.comedian_id = C.comedian_id
INNER JOIN Agents AS A ON C.agent_id = A.agent_id
WHERE S.category = 'open mic night';

SELECT C.comedian_name,
       COUNT(*) AS sets_booked
FROM Comedians AS C
INNER JOIN StageTimes AS ST ON C.comedian_id = ST.comedian_id
GROUP BY C.comedian_name
ORDER BY sets_booked DESC, C.comedian_name;

CREATE TABLE Microphones (mic_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, brand VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL, model VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE Mixers (mixer_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, mixer_channel VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE Technicians (tech_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tech_name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE SoundcheckLogs (log_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, mic_id INTEGER REFERENCES Microphones (mic_id), mixer_id INTEGER REFERENCES Mixers (mixer_id), tech_id INTEGER REFERENCES Technicians (tech_id), issue_type VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL, resolved CHAR(1) NOT NULL);

CREATE VIEW SoundEngineeringChecks AS
SELECT M.brand AS microphone_brand,
       X.mixer_channel,
       T.tech_name
FROM SoundcheckLogs AS L
INNER JOIN Microphones AS M ON L.mic_id = M.mic_id
INNER JOIN Mixers AS X ON L.mixer_id = X.mixer_id
INNER JOIN Technicians AS T ON L.tech_id = T.tech_id
WHERE L.issue_type = 'static'
  AND L.resolved = 'Y';

SELECT T.tech_name,
       M.brand AS microphone_brand,
       L.issue_type
FROM SoundcheckLogs AS L
INNER JOIN Technicians AS T ON L.tech_id = T.tech_id
INNER JOIN Microphones AS M ON L.mic_id = M.mic_id
WHERE L.resolved = 'N'
ORDER BY T.tech_name;

CREATE TABLE FloorPlans (table_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, table_number VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL, section VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE GuestLists (guest_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, guest_name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE Servers (server_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, server_name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE TableReservations (reservation_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, table_id INTEGER REFERENCES FloorPlans (table_id), guest_id INTEGER REFERENCES GuestLists (guest_id), server_id INTEGER REFERENCES Servers (server_id), occasion VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL);

CREATE VIEW VipTableAssignments AS
SELECT F.table_number,
       G.guest_name,
       V.server_name
FROM FloorPlans AS F
INNER JOIN TableReservations AS R ON F.table_id = R.table_id
INNER JOIN GuestLists AS G ON R.guest_id = G.guest_id
INNER JOIN Servers AS V ON R.server_id = V.server_id
WHERE R.occasion = 'birthday celebration'
  AND F.section = 'vip';

SELECT V.server_name,
       COUNT(*) AS vip_tables_served
FROM Servers AS V
INNER JOIN TableReservations AS R ON V.server_id = R.server_id
INNER JOIN FloorPlans AS F ON R.table_id = F.table_id
WHERE F.section = 'vip'
GROUP BY V.server_name
ORDER BY vip_tables_served DESC, V.server_name;

The first view details styling appointments by linking salon chairs, appointment slots, customer profiles, and styling professionals, returning the chair number, slot time, customer name, and professional name for appointments booking a bridal package. The second view tracks hair color inventory by combining dye brands, color shades, mixing bowls, and inventory audits to show the brand name, shade name, and audit date for shades classified as vivid colors. The third view manages loyalty programs by joining reward tiers, point balances, redemption transactions, and checkout clerks to output the tier name, point value, and clerk name for redemptions applying a free haircut reward. Include only records with complete relational matches. Example input: a bridal package booked with professional Eve, a vivid color shade audited on tuesday, a free haircut reward redeemed with clerk Fay. Example output: chair three at noon customer Gina professional Eve, brand max vivid red tuesday audit, gold tier fifty points clerk Fay.
text_nat:
CREATE VIEW BridalStylingAppointments AS
SELECT
    ch.chair_number      AS chair_number,
    sl.slot_time         AS slot_time,
    cu.customer_name     AS customer_name,
    pr.professional_name AS professional_name
FROM Appointments AS ap
JOIN SalonChairs AS ch ON ch.chair_id = ap.chair_id
JOIN AppointmentSlots AS sl ON sl.slot_id = ap.slot_id
JOIN CustomerProfiles AS cu ON cu.customer_id = ap.customer_id
JOIN StylingProfessionals AS pr ON pr.professional_id = ap.professional_id
WHERE ap.package_type = 'bridal package';

CREATE VIEW VividColorInventory AS
SELECT
    db.brand_name  AS brand_name,
    cs.shade_name  AS shade_name,
    ia.audit_date  AS audit_date
FROM InventoryAudits AS ia
JOIN MixingBowls AS mb ON mb.bowl_id = ia.bowl_id
JOIN ColorShades AS cs ON cs.shade_id = mb.shade_id
JOIN DyeBrands AS db ON db.brand_id = cs.brand_id
WHERE cs.shade_class = 'vivid color';

CREATE VIEW FreeHaircutRedemptions AS
SELECT
    rt.tier_name    AS tier_name,
    pb.point_value  AS point_value,
    cl.clerk_name   AS clerk_name
FROM RedemptionTransactions AS rx
JOIN PointBalances AS pb ON pb.balance_id = rx.balance_id
JOIN RewardTiers AS rt ON rt.tier_id = pb.tier_id
JOIN CheckoutClerks AS cl ON cl.clerk_id = rx.clerk_id
WHERE rx.reward_type = 'free haircut';

SELECT chair_number, slot_time, customer_name, professional_name
FROM BridalStylingAppointments
ORDER BY slot_time, chair_number;

SELECT brand_name, shade_name, audit_date
FROM VividColorInventory
ORDER BY audit_date, brand_name;

SELECT tier_name, point_value, clerk_name
FROM FreeHaircutRedemptions
ORDER BY point_value DESC, tier_name;

SELECT
    pr.professional_name AS professional_name,
    COUNT(*)             AS bridal_bookings
FROM Appointments AS ap
JOIN StylingProfessionals AS pr ON pr.professional_id = ap.professional_id
WHERE ap.package_type = 'bridal package'
GROUP BY pr.professional_name
ORDER BY bridal_bookings DESC, pr.professional_name;

SELECT
    db.brand_name        AS brand_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT cs.shade_id) AS vivid_shades_audited
FROM InventoryAudits AS ia
JOIN MixingBowls AS mb ON mb.bowl_id = ia.bowl_id
JOIN ColorShades AS cs ON cs.shade_id = mb.shade_id
JOIN DyeBrands AS db ON db.brand_id = cs.brand_id
WHERE cs.shade_class = 'vivid color'
GROUP BY db.brand_name
ORDER BY vivid_shades_audited DESC, db.brand_name;

SELECT
    cl.clerk_name      AS clerk_name,
    SUM(pb.point_value) AS points_redeemed
FROM RedemptionTransactions AS rx
JOIN PointBalances AS pb ON pb.balance_id = rx.balance_id
JOIN CheckoutClerks AS cl ON cl.clerk_id = rx.clerk_id
WHERE rx.reward_type = 'free haircut'
GROUP BY cl.clerk_name
ORDER BY points_redeemed DESC, cl.clerk_name;

text_es: Design a stored procedure named `plan(month)` that builds two logistical planning tables for a given string month. The first table must show climber names, peak names, mountain range names, sherpa guide names, and permit authority names. To do this, connect climbers to expedition rosters, rosters to peak designations, peaks to mountain ranges, rosters to assigned sherpas, and expeditions to issued permits. The second table must list equipment types, basecamp locations, transport vehicle names, and driver names by connecting equipment items to basecamp manifests, manifests to transport schedules, schedules to vehicles, and vehicles to certified drivers. Ensure all returned data represents fully linked relationships, strictly excluding any partial associations. An example output row for May might be Jon Krakauer, Everest, Himalayas, Tenzing, Nepal Tourism Board.
text_nat:
DELIMITER $$

DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS plan $$
DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS plan_climber_manifest $$
DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS plan_equipment_movement $$
DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS plan_canonical_month $$
DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS plan_permitted_expeditions $$
DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS plan_scheduled_transports $$

CREATE FUNCTION plan_canonical_month(in_month VARCHAR(20))
RETURNS VARCHAR(20) READS SQL DATA
BEGIN
    DECLARE v_name VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT NULL;

    SELECT m.month_name INTO v_name
    FROM Months AS m
    INNER JOIN MonthAliases AS ma ON ma.month_id = m.month_id
    WHERE UPPER(ma.alias) = UPPER(TRIM(in_month))
    LIMIT 1;

    RETURN v_name;
END $$

CREATE FUNCTION plan_permitted_expeditions(in_month VARCHAR(20))
RETURNS INT READS SQL DATA
BEGIN
    DECLARE v_count INT DEFAULT 0;

    SELECT COUNT(*) INTO v_count
    FROM Expeditions AS e
    INNER JOIN Permits AS pm ON pm.expedition_id = e.expedition_id
    INNER JOIN PermitAuthorities AS pa ON pa.authority_id = pm.authority_id
    WHERE e.month = in_month;

    RETURN v_count;
END $$

CREATE FUNCTION plan_scheduled_transports(in_month VARCHAR(20))
RETURNS INT READS SQL DATA
BEGIN
    DECLARE v_count INT DEFAULT 0;

    SELECT COUNT(*) INTO v_count
    FROM TransportSchedules AS ts
    INNER JOIN Vehicles AS v ON v.vehicle_id = ts.vehicle_id
    INNER JOIN CertifiedDrivers AS d ON d.driver_id = v.driver_id
    WHERE ts.month = in_month;

    RETURN v_count;
END $$

CREATE PROCEDURE plan_climber_manifest(IN in_month VARCHAR(20))
BEGIN
    SELECT c.full_name AS climber_name,
           p.peak_name AS peak_name,
           mr.range_name AS range_name,
           s.full_name AS sherpa_name,
           pa.authority_name AS permit_authority
    FROM Climbers AS c
    INNER JOIN ExpeditionRosters AS r ON r.climber_id = c.climber_id
    INNER JOIN PeakDesignations AS pd ON pd.roster_id = r.roster_id
    INNER JOIN Peaks AS p ON p.peak_id = pd.peak_id
    INNER JOIN MountainRanges AS mr ON mr.range_id = p.range_id
    INNER JOIN Sherpas AS s ON s.sherpa_id = r.sherpa_id
    INNER JOIN Expeditions AS e ON e.expedition_id = r.expedition_id
    INNER JOIN Permits AS pm ON pm.expedition_id = e.expedition_id
    INNER JOIN PermitAuthorities AS pa ON pa.authority_id = pm.authority_id
    WHERE e.month = in_month
    ORDER BY mr.range_name, p.peak_name, c.full_name;
END $$

CREATE PROCEDURE plan_equipment_movement(IN in_month VARCHAR(20))
BEGIN
    SELECT eq.equipment_type AS equipment_type,
           bc.location_name AS basecamp_location,
           v.vehicle_name AS vehicle_name,
           d.full_name AS driver_name
    FROM Equipment AS eq
    INNER JOIN BasecampManifests AS bm ON bm.equipment_id = eq.equipment_id
    INNER JOIN Basecamps AS bc ON bc.basecamp_id = bm.basecamp_id
    INNER JOIN TransportSchedules AS ts ON ts.manifest_id = bm.manifest_id
    INNER JOIN Vehicles AS v ON v.vehicle_id = ts.vehicle_id
    INNER JOIN CertifiedDrivers AS d ON d.driver_id = v.driver_id
    WHERE ts.month = in_month
    ORDER BY bc.location_name, eq.equipment_type;
END $$

CREATE PROCEDURE plan(IN in_month VARCHAR(20))
BEGIN
    DECLARE v_month VARCHAR(20);

    SET v_month = plan_canonical_month(in_month);

    IF v_month IS NULL THEN
        SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000'
            SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'plan(month): unknown calendar month';
    END IF;

    IF plan_permitted_expeditions(v_month) = 0 THEN
        SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000'
            SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'plan(month): no permitted expeditions for that month';
    END IF;

    IF plan_scheduled_transports(v_month) = 0 THEN
        SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000'
            SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'plan(month): no transport scheduled with certified drivers';
    END IF;

    CALL plan_climber_manifest(v_month);
    CALL plan_equipment_movement(v_month);
END $$

DELIMITER ;

CALL plan('May');

DELIMITER $$

DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS plan $$
DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS plan_climber_manifest $$
DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS plan_equipment_movement $$
DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS plan_canonical_month $$
DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS plan_permitted_expeditions $$
DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS plan_scheduled_transports $$

CREATE FUNCTION plan_canonical_month(in_month VARCHAR(20))
RETURNS VARCHAR(20) READS SQL DATA
BEGIN
    DECLARE v_name VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT NULL;

    SELECT m.month_name INTO v_name
    FROM Months AS m, MonthAliases AS ma
    WHERE ma.month_id = m.month_id AND UPPER(ma.alias) = UPPER(TRIM(in_month))
    LIMIT 1;

    RETURN v_name;
END $$

CREATE FUNCTION plan_permitted_expeditions(in_month VARCHAR(20))
RETURNS INT READS SQL DATA
BEGIN
    DECLARE v_count INT DEFAULT 0;

    SELECT COUNT(*) INTO v_count
    FROM Expeditions AS e, Permits AS pm, PermitAuthorities AS pa
    WHERE pm.expedition_id = e.expedition_id AND pa.authority_id = pm.authority_id AND e.month = in_month;

    RETURN v_count;
END $$

CREATE FUNCTION plan_scheduled_transports(in_month VARCHAR(20))
RETURNS INT READS SQL DATA
BEGIN
    DECLARE v_count INT DEFAULT 0;

    SELECT COUNT(*) INTO v_count
    FROM TransportSchedules AS ts, Vehicles AS v, CertifiedDrivers AS d
    WHERE v.vehicle_id = ts.vehicle_id AND d.driver_id = v.driver_id AND ts.month = in_month;

    RETURN v_count;
END $$

CREATE PROCEDURE plan_climber_manifest(IN in_month VARCHAR(20))
BEGIN
    SELECT c.full_name AS climber_name,
           p.peak_name AS peak_name,
           mr.range_name AS range_name,
           s.full_name AS sherpa_name,
           pa.authority_name AS permit_authority
    FROM Climbers AS c, ExpeditionRosters AS r, PeakDesignations AS pd, Peaks AS p, MountainRanges AS mr, Sherpas AS s, Expeditions AS e, Permits AS pm, PermitAuthorities AS pa
    WHERE r.climber_id = c.climber_id AND pd.roster_id = r.roster_id AND p.peak_id = pd.peak_id AND mr.range_id = p.range_id AND s.sherpa_id = r.sherpa_id AND e.expedition_id = r.expedition_id AND pm.expedition_id = e.expedition_id AND pa.authority_id = pm.authority_id AND e.month = in_month
    ORDER BY mr.range_name, p.peak_name, c.full_name;

    ORDER BY bc.location_name, eq.equipment_type;
END $$

CREATE PROCEDURE plan(IN in_month VARCHAR(20))
BEGIN

BEGIN
    DECLARE cheese_rows INT;
    DECLARE milk_rows INT;

    SELECT COUNT(*) INTO cheese_rows
    FROM production_batches AS pb
    JOIN v_cave_sensors AS cs ON cs.cave_id = pb.cave_id

    SELECT COUNT(*) INTO milk_rows
    FROM farms AS f

text_es: Create a procedure named `schedule(network)` that outputs two broadcasting schedules for a given string network name. First, display producer names, show titles, network channel names, broadcast time slots, and advertiser brand names by linking producers to created shows, shows to network channels, shows to broadcast slots, and slots to purchased advertisements. Second, fetch actor names, episode titles, wardrobe designer names, and costume studio names by linking actors to episode appearances, appearances to wardrobe assignments, assignments to designers, and designers to their home studios. Only process entries that successfully bridge across all required categories, strictly ignoring unmatched data. For instance, providing Channel 4 might yield rows like John Doe, Morning News, Channel 4, 08:00 AM, SoapCorp.
text_nat:
DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS schedule;
DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS broadcast_schedule;
DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS wardrobe_schedule;
DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS network_summary;
DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS advertiser_roster;
DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS network_show_count;

DELIMITER //

CREATE FUNCTION network_show_count(network VARCHAR(100)) RETURNS INT
READS SQL DATA
BEGIN
    DECLARE total INT;
    SELECT COUNT(*) INTO total
    FROM shows AS s
    JOIN channels AS c ON c.channel_id = s.channel_id
    WHERE c.channel_name = network;
    RETURN total;
END //

CREATE PROCEDURE network_summary(IN network VARCHAR(100))
BEGIN
    SELECT c.channel_name,
           COUNT(DISTINCT s.show_id)    AS shows_aired,
           COUNT(DISTINCT b.slot_id)    AS slots_booked,
           COUNT(DISTINCT e.episode_id) AS episodes_taped
    FROM channels AS c
    JOIN shows AS s ON s.channel_id = c.channel_id
    JOIN broadcast_slots AS b ON b.show_id = s.show_id
    JOIN episodes AS e ON e.show_id = s.show_id
    WHERE c.channel_name = network
    GROUP BY c.channel_name;
END //

CREATE PROCEDURE broadcast_schedule(IN network VARCHAR(100))
BEGIN
    SELECT p.producer_name, s.show_title, c.channel_name, b.air_time, adv.brand_name
    FROM producers AS p
    JOIN shows AS s ON s.producer_id = p.producer_id
    JOIN channels AS c ON c.channel_id = s.channel_id
    JOIN broadcast_slots AS b ON b.show_id = s.show_id
    JOIN advertisements AS a ON a.slot_id = b.slot_id
    JOIN advertisers AS adv ON adv.advertiser_id = a.advertiser_id
    WHERE c.channel_name = network
    ORDER BY b.air_time, s.show_title;
END //

CREATE PROCEDURE wardrobe_schedule(IN network VARCHAR(100))
BEGIN
    SELECT ac.actor_name, e.episode_title, d.designer_name, st.studio_name
    FROM actors AS ac
    JOIN appearances AS ap ON ap.actor_id = ac.actor_id
    JOIN episodes AS e ON e.episode_id = ap.episode_id
    JOIN shows AS s ON s.show_id = e.show_id
    JOIN channels AS c ON c.channel_id = s.channel_id
    JOIN wardrobe_assignments AS w ON w.appearance_id = ap.appearance_id
    JOIN designers AS d ON d.designer_id = w.designer_id
    JOIN studios AS st ON st.studio_id = d.studio_id
    WHERE c.channel_name = network
    ORDER BY e.episode_title, ac.actor_name;
END //

CREATE PROCEDURE advertiser_roster(IN network VARCHAR(100))
BEGIN
    SELECT adv.brand_name, COUNT(*) AS spots_purchased
    FROM advertisers AS adv
    JOIN advertisements AS a ON a.advertiser_id = adv.advertiser_id
    JOIN broadcast_slots AS b ON b.slot_id = a.slot_id
    JOIN shows AS s ON s.show_id = b.show_id
    JOIN channels AS c ON c.channel_id = s.channel_id
    WHERE c.channel_name = network
    GROUP BY adv.brand_name
    ORDER BY spots_purchased DESC, adv.brand_name;
END //

CREATE PROCEDURE schedule(IN network VARCHAR(100))
BEGIN
    IF network_show_count(network) = 0 THEN
        SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000'
            SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'no shows are registered for the requested network';
    END IF;
    CALL network_summary(network);
    CALL broadcast_schedule(network);
    CALL wardrobe_schedule(network);
    CALL advertiser_roster(network);
END //

DELIMITER ;

CALL schedule('Channel 4');
text_alt:
DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS schedule;
DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS broadcast_schedule;
DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS wardrobe_schedule;
DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS network_summary;
DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS advertiser_roster;
DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS network_show_count;

DELIMITER //

CREATE FUNCTION network_show_count(network VARCHAR(100)) RETURNS INT
READS SQL DATA
BEGIN
    DECLARE total INT;
    SELECT COUNT(*) INTO total
    FROM shows AS s, channels AS c
    WHERE c.channel_id = s.channel_id
      AND c.channel_name = network;
    RETURN total;
END //

CREATE PROCEDURE network_summary(IN network VARCHAR(100))
BEGIN
    SELECT c.channel_name,
           COUNT(DISTINCT s.show_id)    AS shows_aired,
           COUNT(DISTINCT b.slot_id)    AS slots_booked,
           COUNT(DISTINCT e.episode_id) AS episodes_taped
    FROM channels AS c, shows AS s, broadcast_slots AS b, episodes AS e
    WHERE s.channel_id = c.channel_id
      AND b.show_id = s.show_id
      AND e.show_id = s.show_id
      AND c.channel_name = network
    GROUP BY c.channel_name;
END //

CREATE PROCEDURE broadcast_schedule(IN network VARCHAR(100))
BEGIN
    SELECT p.producer_name, s.show_title, c.channel_name, b.air_time, adv.brand_name
    FROM producers AS p, shows AS s, channels AS c, broadcast_slots AS b, advertisements AS a, advertisers AS adv
    WHERE s.producer_id = p.producer_id
      AND c.channel_id = s.channel_id
      AND b.show_id = s.show_id
      AND a.slot_id = b.slot_id
      AND adv.advertiser_id = a.advertiser_id
      AND c.channel_name = network
    ORDER BY b.air_time, s.show_title;
END //

CREATE PROCEDURE wardrobe_schedule(IN network VARCHAR(100))
BEGIN
    SELECT ac.actor_name, e.episode_title, d.designer_name, st.studio_name
    FROM actors AS ac, appearances AS ap, episodes AS e, shows AS s, channels AS c, wardrobe_assignments AS w, designers AS d, studios AS st
    WHERE ap.actor_id = ac.actor_id
      AND e.episode_id = ap.episode_id
      AND s.show_id = e.show_id
      AND c.channel_id = s.channel_id
      AND w.appearance_id = ap.appearance_id
      AND d.designer_id = w.designer_id
      AND st.studio_id = d.studio_id
      AND c.channel_name = network
    ORDER BY e.episode_title, ac.actor_name;
END //

CREATE PROCEDURE advertiser_roster(IN network VARCHAR(100))
BEGIN
    SELECT adv.brand_name, COUNT(*) AS spots_purchased
    FROM advertisers AS adv, advertisements AS a, broadcast_slots AS b, shows AS s, channels AS c
    WHERE a.advertiser_id = adv.advertiser_id
      AND b.slot_id = a.slot_id
      AND s.show_id = b.show_id
      AND c.channel_id = s.channel_id
      AND c.channel_name = network
    GROUP BY adv.brand_name
    ORDER BY spots_purchased DESC, adv.brand_name;
END //

CREATE PROCEDURE schedule(IN network VARCHAR(100))
BEGIN
    IF network_show_count(network) = 0 THEN
        SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000'
            SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'no shows are registered for the requested network';
    END IF;
    CALL network_summary(network);
    CALL broadcast_schedule(network);
    CALL wardrobe_schedule(network);
    CALL advertiser_roster(network);
END //

DELIMITER ;

CALL schedule('Channel 4');

text_es: Develop a routine named `assess(district)` that generates two arboriculture reports for a given string district. The first query must return arborist names, tree species names, neighborhood park names, soil type descriptions, and treatment plan names by linking arborists to tree assessments, assessments to planted trees, trees to species, trees to neighborhood parks, parks to soil types, and assessments to treatment plans. The second query must list pruning equipment names, maintenance crew names, depot locations, and supervisor names by linking equipment to usage logs, logs to crews, crews to home depots, and depots to supervisors. All data points must be strictly interconnected with no missing associations. For example, entering Downtown might produce rows like Sarah, Red Oak, Central Park, Clay, Nitrogen Fertilizer.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE SoilTypes (soil_id INT PRIMARY KEY, soil_description VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE NeighborhoodParks (park_id INT PRIMARY KEY, park_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL, district VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL, soil_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES SoilTypes(soil_id));
CREATE TABLE TreeSpecies (species_id INT PRIMARY KEY, species_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE PlantedTrees (tree_id INT PRIMARY KEY, species_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES TreeSpecies(species_id), park_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES NeighborhoodParks(park_id), planted_on DATE NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE TreatmentPlans (plan_id INT PRIMARY KEY, plan_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE Arborists (arborist_id INT PRIMARY KEY, arborist_name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL, certification VARCHAR(40));
CREATE TABLE TreeAssessments (assessment_id INT PRIMARY KEY, arborist_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES Arborists(arborist_id), tree_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES PlantedTrees(tree_id), plan_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES TreatmentPlans(plan_id), assessed_on DATE NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE Supervisors (supervisor_id INT PRIMARY KEY, supervisor_name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE Depots (depot_id INT PRIMARY KEY, depot_location VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL, district VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL, supervisor_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES Supervisors(supervisor_id));
CREATE TABLE MaintenanceCrews (crew_id INT PRIMARY KEY, crew_name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL, depot_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES Depots(depot_id));
CREATE TABLE PruningEquipment (equipment_id INT PRIMARY KEY, equipment_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE EquipmentUsageLogs (log_id INT PRIMARY KEY, equipment_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES PruningEquipment(equipment_id), crew_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES MaintenanceCrews(crew_id), used_on DATE NOT NULL);

DELIMITER //

CREATE PROCEDURE assess(IN district VARCHAR(60))
BEGIN
    SELECT A.arborist_name, S.species_name, P.park_name, ST.soil_description, TP.plan_name
    FROM Arborists AS A
    INNER JOIN TreeAssessments AS TA ON A.arborist_id = TA.arborist_id
    INNER JOIN PlantedTrees AS T ON TA.tree_id = T.tree_id
    INNER JOIN TreeSpecies AS S ON T.species_id = S.species_id
    INNER JOIN NeighborhoodParks AS P ON T.park_id = P.park_id
    INNER JOIN SoilTypes AS ST ON P.soil_id = ST.soil_id
    INNER JOIN TreatmentPlans AS TP ON TA.plan_id = TP.plan_id
    WHERE P.district = district
    ORDER BY A.arborist_name, P.park_name, S.species_name;

    SELECT E.equipment_name, C.crew_name, D.depot_location, SV.supervisor_name
    FROM PruningEquipment AS E
    INNER JOIN EquipmentUsageLogs AS L ON E.equipment_id = L.equipment_id
    INNER JOIN MaintenanceCrews AS C ON L.crew_id = C.crew_id
    INNER JOIN Depots AS D ON C.depot_id = D.depot_id
    INNER JOIN Supervisors AS SV ON D.supervisor_id = SV.supervisor_id
    WHERE D.district = district
    ORDER BY E.equipment_name, C.crew_name;
END //

CREATE PROCEDURE species_soil_profile(IN district VARCHAR(60))
BEGIN
    SELECT S.species_name, ST.soil_description, COUNT(T.tree_id) AS tree_count
    FROM TreeSpecies AS S
    INNER JOIN PlantedTrees AS T ON S.species_id = T.species_id
    INNER JOIN NeighborhoodParks AS P ON T.park_id = P.park_id
    INNER JOIN SoilTypes AS ST ON P.soil_id = ST.soil_id
    WHERE P.district = district
    GROUP BY S.species_name, ST.soil_description
    ORDER BY tree_count DESC, S.species_name;
END //

CREATE PROCEDURE plan_workload(IN district VARCHAR(60))
BEGIN
    SELECT TP.plan_name, COUNT(TA.assessment_id) AS assessments, MAX(TA.assessed_on) AS latest_assessment
    FROM TreatmentPlans AS TP
    INNER JOIN TreeAssessments AS TA ON TP.plan_id = TA.plan_id
    INNER JOIN PlantedTrees AS T ON TA.tree_id = T.tree_id
    INNER JOIN NeighborhoodParks AS P ON T.park_id = P.park_id
    WHERE P.district = district
    GROUP BY TP.plan_name
    ORDER BY assessments DESC, TP.plan_name;
END //

CREATE PROCEDURE crew_utilisation(IN district VARCHAR(60))
BEGIN
    SELECT SV.supervisor_name, D.depot_location, C.crew_name, COUNT(L.log_id) AS usage_events
    FROM Supervisors AS SV
    INNER JOIN Depots AS D ON SV.supervisor_id = D.supervisor_id
    INNER JOIN MaintenanceCrews AS C ON D.depot_id = C.depot_id
    INNER JOIN EquipmentUsageLogs AS L ON C.crew_id = L.crew_id
    WHERE D.district = district
    GROUP BY SV.supervisor_name, D.depot_location, C.crew_name
    ORDER BY usage_events DESC, C.crew_name;
END //

CREATE PROCEDURE district_coverage()
BEGIN
    SELECT P.district, COUNT(DISTINCT TA.tree_id) AS assessed_trees, COUNT(DISTINCT C.crew_id) AS available_crews
    FROM NeighborhoodParks AS P
    INNER JOIN PlantedTrees AS T ON P.park_id = T.park_id
    INNER JOIN TreeAssessments AS TA ON T.tree_id = TA.tree_id
    INNER JOIN Depots AS D ON P.district = D.district
    INNER JOIN MaintenanceCrews AS C ON D.depot_id = C.depot_id
    GROUP BY P.district
    ORDER BY P.district;
END //

DELIMITER ;

CALL assess('Downtown');
CALL species_soil_profile('Downtown');
CALL plan_workload('Downtown');
CALL crew_utilisation('Downtown');
CALL assess('Riverside');
CALL district_coverage();

text_es: Implement a procedure named `rank(division)` that retrieves two athletic performance datasets for a string division. First, return rower names, boat class names, racing club names, regatta event names, and river location names by linking rowers to crew assignments, assignments to boats, boats to clubs, crews to regatta entries, and regattas to river locations. Second, output coach names, training plan names, nutrition sponsor names, and physical therapist names by linking coaches to training plans, plans to crews, crews to nutrition sponsorships, and crews to physical therapy sessions. Retrieve only records where every link in the chain exists, discarding rows with incomplete associations. A valid output row for the first query might be James, Eights, River City Club, Spring Sprints, Thames.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Rowers (rower_id INT PRIMARY KEY, rower_name VARCHAR(60));
CREATE TABLE Clubs (club_id INT PRIMARY KEY, club_name VARCHAR(60));
CREATE TABLE Boats (boat_id INT PRIMARY KEY, boat_class VARCHAR(40), club_id INT);
CREATE TABLE Crews (crew_id INT PRIMARY KEY, division VARCHAR(30));
CREATE TABLE CrewAssignments (assignment_id INT PRIMARY KEY, rower_id INT, crew_id INT, boat_id INT);
CREATE TABLE RiverLocations (river_id INT PRIMARY KEY, river_name VARCHAR(60));
CREATE TABLE Regattas (regatta_id INT PRIMARY KEY, event_name VARCHAR(60), river_id INT);
CREATE TABLE RegattaEntries (entry_id INT PRIMARY KEY, crew_id INT, regatta_id INT);
CREATE TABLE Coaches (coach_id INT PRIMARY KEY, coach_name VARCHAR(60));
CREATE TABLE TrainingPlans (plan_id INT PRIMARY KEY, plan_name VARCHAR(60), coach_id INT, crew_id INT);
CREATE TABLE NutritionSponsorships (sponsorship_id INT PRIMARY KEY, crew_id INT, sponsor_name VARCHAR(60));
CREATE TABLE PhysicalTherapySessions (session_id INT PRIMARY KEY, crew_id INT, therapist_name VARCHAR(60));
DELIMITER $$

CREATE PROCEDURE `rank`(IN division VARCHAR(30))
BEGIN
    DECLARE v_division VARCHAR(30) DEFAULT division;

    SELECT R.rower_name, B.boat_class, CL.club_name, RG.event_name, RL.river_name
    FROM Rowers AS R
    JOIN CrewAssignments AS CA ON CA.rower_id = R.rower_id
    JOIN Boats AS B ON B.boat_id = CA.boat_id
    JOIN Clubs AS CL ON CL.club_id = B.club_id
    JOIN Crews AS C ON C.crew_id = CA.crew_id
    JOIN RegattaEntries AS RE ON RE.crew_id = C.crew_id

CREATE PROCEDURE division_report(IN p_division VARCHAR(30))

    FROM Clubs AS CL

DELIMITER //

CREATE PROCEDURE train_validate_status(IN p_status VARCHAR(50))
BEGIN
    DECLARE v_known INT;
    SELECT COUNT(*) INTO v_known FROM DogStatuses WHERE status_code = p_status;
    IF v_known = 0 THEN
        SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000' SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'Unknown training status requested';
    END IF;
END//

CREATE PROCEDURE train_placement_roster(IN p_status VARCHAR(50))
BEGIN
    SELECT tr.trainer_name, br.breed_name, ce.certificate_name, cl.client_name, ci.city_name
      FROM Trainers AS tr
      JOIN Cohorts AS co ON co.trainer_id = tr.trainer_id
      JOIN Dogs AS dg ON dg.cohort_id = co.cohort_id
      JOIN Breeds AS br ON br.breed_id = dg.breed_id
      JOIN Certificates AS ce ON ce.dog_id = dg.dog_id
      JOIN Matches AS ma ON ma.dog_id = dg.dog_id
      JOIN Clients AS cl ON cl.client_id = ma.client_id
      JOIN Cities AS ci ON ci.city_id = cl.city_id
     WHERE dg.training_status = p_status
     ORDER BY tr.trainer_name, cl.client_name;
END//

CREATE PROCEDURE train_care_roster(IN p_status VARCHAR(50))
BEGIN
    SELECT vc.clinic_name, va.vaccine_name, dp.plan_name, sp.family_name
      FROM Dogs AS dg
      JOIN VetVisits AS vv ON vv.dog_id = dg.dog_id
      JOIN VetClinics AS vc ON vc.clinic_id = vv.clinic_id
      JOIN Vaccines AS va ON va.vaccine_id = vv.vaccine_id
      JOIN DietPlans AS dp ON dp.dog_id = dg.dog_id
      JOIN Sponsors AS sp ON sp.dog_id = dg.dog_id
     WHERE dg.training_status = p_status
     ORDER BY vc.clinic_name, va.vaccine_name;
END//

CREATE PROCEDURE train_cohort_summary(IN p_status VARCHAR(50))
BEGIN
    SELECT tr.trainer_name, co.cohort_name, COUNT(*) AS dogs_in_status
      FROM Trainers AS tr
      JOIN Cohorts AS co ON co.trainer_id = tr.trainer_id
      JOIN Dogs AS dg ON dg.cohort_id = co.cohort_id
     WHERE dg.training_status = p_status
     GROUP BY tr.trainer_name, co.cohort_name
     ORDER BY tr.trainer_name, co.cohort_name;
END//

CREATE PROCEDURE train_awaiting_placement(IN p_status VARCHAR(50))
BEGIN
    SELECT dg.dog_id, br.breed_name, ce.certificate_name
      FROM Dogs AS dg
      JOIN Breeds AS br ON br.breed_id = dg.breed_id
      JOIN Certificates AS ce ON ce.dog_id = dg.dog_id
     WHERE dg.training_status = p_status
       AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Matches AS ma WHERE ma.dog_id = dg.dog_id)
     ORDER BY br.breed_name, dg.dog_id;
END//

CREATE PROCEDURE train_care_gaps(IN p_status VARCHAR(50))
BEGIN
    SELECT dg.dog_id, tr.trainer_name
      FROM Dogs AS dg
      JOIN Cohorts AS co ON co.cohort_id = dg.cohort_id
      JOIN Trainers AS tr ON tr.trainer_id = co.trainer_id
     WHERE dg.training_status = p_status
       AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM DietPlans AS dp WHERE dp.dog_id = dg.dog_id)
     ORDER BY tr.trainer_name, dg.dog_id;
END//

CREATE PROCEDURE train(IN status VARCHAR(50))
BEGIN
    CALL train_validate_status(status);
    CALL train_placement_roster(status);
    CALL train_care_roster(status);
    CALL train_cohort_summary(status);
    CALL train_awaiting_placement(status);
    CALL train_care_gaps(status);
END//

DELIMITER ;

CALL train('Graduated');

    asteroid_id  INT PRIMARY KEY,
    composition  VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    sector       VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,

The third query joins wealthy collectors, antique clocks, replacement gears, clockmaker artisans, and polishing compounds to list collectors whose clocks are fully restored, returning the collector name, clock style, gear material, artisan name, and compound type. All combinations must exclusively return records where the connections between entities are fully intact. Example input era victorian outputs three lists of related restoration details.

CREATE TABLE Collectors (
    collector_id   INT PRIMARY KEY,
    collector_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE Artisans (
    artisan_id   INT PRIMARY KEY,
    artisan_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE Clocks (
    clock_id     INT PRIMARY KEY,
    clock_style  VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    era          VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    collector_id INT,
    artisan_id   INT
);

CREATE TABLE Gears (
    gear_id       INT PRIMARY KEY,
    gear_material VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    clock_id      INT
);

CREATE TABLE Compounds (
    compound_id   INT PRIMARY KEY,
    compound_type VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    clock_id      INT,
    artisan_id    INT
);

CREATE VIEW GearedClocks AS
SELECT K.clock_id, K.clock_style, K.era, K.collector_id, K.artisan_id, G.gear_material
FROM Clocks AS K
JOIN Gears AS G ON G.clock_id = K.clock_id;

CREATE VIEW PolishedClocks AS
SELECT K.clock_id, P.compound_type, P.artisan_id
FROM Clocks AS K
JOIN Compounds AS P ON P.clock_id = K.clock_id
  AND P.artisan_id = K.artisan_id;

DELIMITER //

CREATE PROCEDURE restore(IN era VARCHAR(50))
BEGIN
    SELECT C.collector_name, K.clock_style, K.gear_material, A.artisan_name
    FROM GearedClocks AS K
    JOIN Collectors AS C ON C.collector_id = K.collector_id
    JOIN Artisans AS A ON A.artisan_id = K.artisan_id
    WHERE K.era = era
    ORDER BY C.collector_name, K.clock_style;

    SELECT K.clock_style, K.gear_material, P.compound_type, A.artisan_name
    FROM GearedClocks AS K
    JOIN PolishedClocks AS P ON P.clock_id = K.clock_id
    JOIN Artisans AS A ON A.artisan_id = P.artisan_id
    WHERE K.era = era
    ORDER BY K.clock_style, P.compound_type;

    SELECT C.collector_name,
           K.clock_style,
           K.gear_material,
           A.artisan_name,
           P.compound_type
    FROM GearedClocks AS K
    JOIN Collectors AS C ON C.collector_id = K.collector_id
    JOIN Artisans AS A ON A.artisan_id = K.artisan_id
    JOIN PolishedClocks AS P ON P.clock_id = K.clock_id
      AND P.artisan_id = A.artisan_id
    WHERE K.era = era
    ORDER BY C.collector_name, A.artisan_name;
END //

DELIMITER ;

CALL restore('victorian');

CREATE TABLE ballet_companies (company_id INT PRIMARY KEY, company_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    theater_id INT NOT NULL, period VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE stage_theaters (theater_id INT PRIMARY KEY, theater_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    capacity INT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE principal_dancers (dancer_id INT PRIMARY KEY, dancer_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    company_id INT NOT NULL, is_lead BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE);
CREATE TABLE tailored_tutus (tutu_id INT PRIMARY KEY, dancer_id INT NOT NULL,
    tutu_color VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL, is_fitted BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE);
CREATE TABLE orchestral_conductors (conductor_id INT PRIMARY KEY, conductor_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    company_id INT NOT NULL, theater_id INT NOT NULL);

DELIMITER //

CREATE FUNCTION lead_dancer_count(p_period VARCHAR(20)) RETURNS INT
READS SQL DATA
BEGIN
    DECLARE v_count INT;
    SELECT COUNT(*) INTO v_count
    FROM principal_dancers AS pd
    JOIN ballet_companies AS bc ON bc.company_id = pd.company_id
    JOIN tailored_tutus AS tt ON tt.dancer_id = pd.dancer_id
    WHERE bc.period = p_period AND pd.is_lead AND tt.is_fitted;
    RETURN v_count;
END //

CREATE PROCEDURE perform(IN p_period VARCHAR(20))
BEGIN
    SELECT bc.company_name, st.capacity, pd.dancer_name, tt.tutu_color
    FROM ballet_companies AS bc
    JOIN stage_theaters AS st ON st.theater_id = bc.theater_id
    JOIN principal_dancers AS pd ON pd.company_id = bc.company_id
    JOIN tailored_tutus AS tt ON tt.dancer_id = pd.dancer_id
    WHERE bc.period = p_period AND pd.is_lead AND tt.is_fitted
    ORDER BY bc.company_name, pd.dancer_name;

    SELECT st.capacity, pd.dancer_name, oc.conductor_name, bc.company_name
    FROM stage_theaters AS st
    JOIN ballet_companies AS bc ON bc.theater_id = st.theater_id
    JOIN principal_dancers AS pd ON pd.company_id = bc.company_id
    JOIN orchestral_conductors AS oc ON oc.company_id = bc.company_id AND oc.theater_id = st.theater_id
    WHERE bc.period = p_period
    ORDER BY st.capacity DESC, oc.conductor_name;

    SELECT bc.company_name, st.capacity, pd.dancer_name, tt.tutu_color, oc.conductor_name
    FROM ballet_companies AS bc
    JOIN stage_theaters AS st ON st.theater_id = bc.theater_id
    JOIN principal_dancers AS pd ON pd.company_id = bc.company_id
    JOIN tailored_tutus AS tt ON tt.dancer_id = pd.dancer_id
    JOIN orchestral_conductors AS oc ON oc.company_id = bc.company_id AND oc.theater_id = st.theater_id
    WHERE bc.period = p_period AND pd.is_lead AND tt.is_fitted
    ORDER BY bc.company_name, pd.dancer_name, oc.conductor_name;
END //

CREATE PROCEDURE costume_audit(IN p_period VARCHAR(20))
BEGIN
    SELECT bc.company_name, pd.dancer_name, tt.tutu_color
    FROM tailored_tutus AS tt
    JOIN principal_dancers AS pd ON pd.dancer_id = tt.dancer_id
    JOIN ballet_companies AS bc ON bc.company_id = pd.company_id
    WHERE bc.period = p_period AND pd.is_lead AND NOT tt.is_fitted
    ORDER BY bc.company_name, pd.dancer_name;
END //

CREATE PROCEDURE period_overview(IN p_period VARCHAR(20))
BEGIN
    SELECT st.theater_name, st.capacity, COUNT(DISTINCT bc.company_id) AS companies,
           COUNT(DISTINCT oc.conductor_id) AS conductors
    FROM stage_theaters AS st
    JOIN ballet_companies AS bc ON bc.theater_id = st.theater_id
    JOIN orchestral_conductors AS oc ON oc.company_id = bc.company_id AND oc.theater_id = st.theater_id
    WHERE bc.period = p_period
    GROUP BY st.theater_name, st.capacity
    ORDER BY st.capacity DESC;
END //

DELIMITER ;

The database includes tables for ink chemists, liquid dyes, mixing beakers, glass bottles, and quality blotters. The first result set connects ink chemists, liquid dyes, mixing beakers, and glass bottles to show the chemist name, dye pigment, beaker volume, and bottle shape, strictly for inks aiming for the given shade that have dyes, beakers, and bottles assigned. The second query joins mixing beakers, glass bottles, quality blotters, and ink chemists to display the beaker volume, bottle shape, blotter absorbency, and chemist name, including only inks that underwent quality testing on blotters by a chemist. The third query links ink chemists, liquid dyes, mixing beakers, glass bottles, and quality blotters to list inks successfully mixed and bottled, returning the chemist name, dye pigment, beaker volume, bottle shape, and blotter absorbency. The logic demands that all queries only include records with complete matching data across the linked tables. Example input shade azure returns three production summaries.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE InkChemists (
    chemist_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    chemist_name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE Inks (
    ink_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    shade VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL,
    chemist_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES InkChemists(chemist_id)
);

CREATE TABLE LiquidDyes (
    dye_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    ink_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES Inks(ink_id),
    pigment VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE MixingBeakers (
    beaker_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    ink_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES Inks(ink_id),
    volume_ml DECIMAL(7,2) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE GlassBottles (
    bottle_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    ink_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES Inks(ink_id),
    shape VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE QualityBlotters (
    blotter_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    ink_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES Inks(ink_id),
    chemist_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES InkChemists(chemist_id),
    absorbency VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL
);

CREATE VIEW MixedInks AS
SELECT i.ink_id, i.shade, i.chemist_id, d.pigment, b.volume_ml
FROM Inks AS i
JOIN LiquidDyes AS d ON d.ink_id = i.ink_id
JOIN MixingBeakers AS b ON b.ink_id = i.ink_id;

CREATE VIEW BottledInks AS
SELECT b.ink_id, b.volume_ml, g.shape
FROM MixingBeakers AS b
JOIN GlassBottles AS g ON g.ink_id = b.ink_id;

CREATE VIEW BlotterTests AS
SELECT q.ink_id, q.chemist_id, q.absorbency, c.chemist_name
FROM QualityBlotters AS q
JOIN InkChemists AS c ON c.chemist_id = q.chemist_id;

DELIMITER //

CREATE PROCEDURE mix(IN p_shade VARCHAR(40))
BEGIN
    SELECT c.chemist_name, m.pigment, m.volume_ml, g.shape
    FROM MixedInks AS m
    JOIN InkChemists AS c ON c.chemist_id = m.chemist_id
    JOIN GlassBottles AS g ON g.ink_id = m.ink_id
    WHERE m.shade = p_shade
    ORDER BY c.chemist_name, m.pigment;

    SELECT bi.volume_ml, bi.shape, t.absorbency, t.chemist_name
    FROM BottledInks AS bi
    JOIN Inks AS i ON i.ink_id = bi.ink_id
    JOIN BlotterTests AS t ON t.ink_id = bi.ink_id
    WHERE i.shade = p_shade
    ORDER BY bi.volume_ml, t.absorbency;

    SELECT c.chemist_name, m.pigment, m.volume_ml, g.shape, q.absorbency
    FROM MixedInks AS m
    JOIN InkChemists AS c ON c.chemist_id = m.chemist_id
    JOIN GlassBottles AS g ON g.ink_id = m.ink_id
    JOIN QualityBlotters AS q ON q.ink_id = m.ink_id AND q.chemist_id = m.chemist_id
    WHERE m.shade = p_shade
    ORDER BY c.chemist_name, g.shape;
END //

DELIMITER ;

CALL mix('azure');

text_es: Create a stored procedure `sequence(organism)` that takes an organism strain string and produces three biological analysis reports. The lab database contains tables for research projects, organism strains, genetic sequences, physical assays, and laboratory technicians. The first query joins research projects, organism strains, genetic sequences, and physical assays to list the project title, strain mutation, sequence length, and assay result, focusing only on the specified organism where sequences are fully mapped and assayed. The second query links genetic sequences, physical assays, laboratory technicians, and organism strains to output the sequence identifier, assay result, technician name, and strain mutation, keeping only assays completed by active technicians on known strains. The third query connects research projects, organism strains, physical assays, laboratory technicians, and genetic sequences to summarize project progress, returning the project title, strain mutation, assay date, technician specialty, and sequence length. All joins must rigidly require matching rows in every connected table. Input organism yeast returns three biological data tables.
text_nat:
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE sequence(IN p_organism VARCHAR(255))
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
DECLARE
    v_strain_count  INTEGER;
    v_mapped_count  INTEGER;
BEGIN

    SELECT COUNT(*) INTO v_strain_count
    FROM organism_strains os
    JOIN research_projects rp ON os.project_id = rp.project_id
    WHERE os.organism = p_organism;

    IF v_strain_count = 0 THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'organism % is not registered on any research project', p_organism;
    END IF;

    SELECT COUNT(*) INTO v_mapped_count
    FROM organism_strains os
    JOIN genetic_sequences gs ON os.strain_id = gs.strain_id
    WHERE os.organism = p_organism
      AND gs.fully_mapped = TRUE;

    IF v_mapped_count = 0 THEN
        RAISE NOTICE 'organism % has no fully mapped sequences yet', p_organism;
    END IF;

    DROP TABLE IF EXISTS report_one;
    CREATE TEMP TABLE report_one AS
    SELECT rp.title,
           os.mutation,
           gs.sequence_length,
           pa.result
    FROM organism_strains os
    JOIN research_projects rp ON os.project_id = rp.project_id
    JOIN genetic_sequences gs ON os.strain_id = gs.strain_id
    JOIN physical_assays pa ON gs.sequence_id = pa.sequence_id
    WHERE os.organism = p_organism
      AND gs.fully_mapped = TRUE
      AND pa.completed = TRUE;

    DROP TABLE IF EXISTS report_two;
    CREATE TEMP TABLE report_two AS
    SELECT gs.sequence_id,
           pa.result,
           lt.name AS technician_name,
           os.mutation
    FROM genetic_sequences gs
    JOIN physical_assays pa ON gs.sequence_id = pa.sequence_id
    JOIN laboratory_technicians lt ON pa.tech_id = lt.tech_id
    JOIN organism_strains os ON gs.strain_id = os.strain_id
    WHERE os.organism = p_organism
      AND pa.completed = TRUE
      AND lt.active = TRUE;

    DROP TABLE IF EXISTS report_three;
    CREATE TEMP TABLE report_three AS
    SELECT rp.title,
           os.mutation,
           pa.assay_date,
           lt.specialty,
           gs.sequence_length
    FROM research_projects rp
    JOIN organism_strains os ON rp.project_id = os.project_id
    JOIN physical_assays pa ON os.strain_id = pa.strain_id
    JOIN laboratory_technicians lt ON pa.tech_id = lt.tech_id
    JOIN genetic_sequences gs ON pa.sequence_id = gs.sequence_id
    WHERE os.organism = p_organism;

END;
$$;

CALL sequence('yeast');
SELECT * FROM report_one;
SELECT * FROM report_two;
SELECT * FROM report_three;

text_es: Write a stored procedure `dive(trench)` that takes a trench name and generates three result sets regarding underwater exploration. The system manages tables for oceanographic institutes, submersible vehicles, robotic arms, collected samples, and marine pilots. The first query combines oceanographic institutes, submersible vehicles, robotic arms, and collected samples to list the institute name, vehicle class, arm span, and sample mineral, strictly for vehicles exploring the given trench that have collected samples using robotic arms. The second query links submersible vehicles, collected samples, marine pilots, and robotic arms to display the vehicle class, sample mineral, pilot name, and arm span, including only vehicles that collected a sample, used an arm, and have a pilot. The third query joins oceanographic institutes, submersible vehicles, robotic arms, collected samples, and marine pilots to find the most successful expeditions, returning the institute name, vehicle class, arm span, sample mineral, and pilot name. Only fully intersecting data sets with matching records everywhere can be included. Example input trench mariana outputs three exploration reports.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE institutes (
    institute_id   INT PRIMARY KEY,
    institute_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    country        VARCHAR(60)
);

CREATE TABLE vehicles (
    vehicle_id    INT PRIMARY KEY,
    institute_id  INT NOT NULL,
    vehicle_class VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    trench        VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (institute_id) REFERENCES institutes(institute_id)
);

CREATE TABLE arms (
    arm_id      INT PRIMARY KEY,
    vehicle_id  INT NOT NULL,
    arm_span_cm DECIMAL(6,2) NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (vehicle_id) REFERENCES vehicles(vehicle_id)
);

CREATE TABLE samples (
    sample_id  INT PRIMARY KEY,
    vehicle_id INT NOT NULL,
    arm_id     INT,
    mineral    VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    mass_g     DECIMAL(8,2),
    FOREIGN KEY (vehicle_id) REFERENCES vehicles(vehicle_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (arm_id) REFERENCES arms(arm_id)
);

CREATE TABLE pilots (
    pilot_id   INT PRIMARY KEY,
    vehicle_id INT NOT NULL,
    pilot_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (vehicle_id) REFERENCES vehicles(vehicle_id)
);

CREATE VIEW fleet AS
SELECT i.institute_name, v.vehicle_id, v.vehicle_class, v.trench
FROM institutes AS i
JOIN vehicles AS v ON v.institute_id = i.institute_id;

CREATE VIEW arm_samples AS
SELECT s.vehicle_id, s.mineral, s.mass_g, a.arm_id, a.arm_span_cm
FROM samples AS s
JOIN arms AS a ON a.arm_id = s.arm_id AND a.vehicle_id = s.vehicle_id;

CREATE VIEW crews AS
SELECT p.pilot_name, v.vehicle_id, v.vehicle_class, v.trench
FROM pilots AS p
JOIN vehicles AS v ON v.vehicle_id = p.vehicle_id;

DELIMITER //

CREATE PROCEDURE dive(IN trench VARCHAR(80))
BEGIN
    DECLARE target VARCHAR(80);
    SET target = trench;

    SELECT f.institute_name, f.vehicle_class, s.arm_span_cm, s.mineral
    FROM fleet AS f
    JOIN arm_samples AS s ON s.vehicle_id = f.vehicle_id
    WHERE f.trench = target
    ORDER BY f.institute_name, f.vehicle_class, s.mineral;

    SELECT c.vehicle_class, s.mineral, c.pilot_name, s.arm_span_cm
    FROM crews AS c
    JOIN arm_samples AS s ON s.vehicle_id = c.vehicle_id
    WHERE c.trench = target
    ORDER BY c.vehicle_class, c.pilot_name;

    SELECT f.institute_name, f.vehicle_class, s.arm_span_cm, s.mineral, c.pilot_name
    FROM fleet AS f
    JOIN arm_samples AS s ON s.vehicle_id = f.vehicle_id
    JOIN crews AS c ON c.vehicle_id = f.vehicle_id
    WHERE f.trench = target
    ORDER BY s.mass_g DESC, f.institute_name;
END //

DELIMITER ;

CALL dive('mariana');

text_es: Implement a stored procedure `maintain(coast)` that takes a coastline name and provides three result sets on lighthouse upkeep. The database has tables for maritime regions, lighthouses, beacon lamps, power generators, and maintenance crews. The first query links maritime regions, lighthouses, beacon lamps, and power generators to show the region name, lighthouse elevation, lamp intensity, and generator capacity, restricted to the specified coast for lighthouses with installed lamps and generators. The second query connects lighthouses, power generators, maintenance crews, and maritime regions to output the lighthouse name, generator fuel type, crew supervisor, and region name, strictly for lighthouses actively assigned to a crew in a known region. The third query combines maritime regions, lighthouses, beacon lamps, power generators, and maintenance crews to catalog the full technical stack of coastal beacons, returning the region name, lighthouse name, lamp type, generator capacity, and crew supervisor. Ensure all queries purely select records that successfully match across all combined tables. Input coast western returns three maintenance tables.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE maritime_regions (
    region_id    INT PRIMARY KEY,
    region_name  VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    coast        VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE lighthouses (
    lighthouse_id   INT PRIMARY KEY,
    region_id       INT NOT NULL,
    lighthouse_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    elevation_m     DECIMAL(6,2) NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (region_id) REFERENCES maritime_regions(region_id)
);
CREATE TABLE beacon_lamps (
    lamp_id       INT PRIMARY KEY,
    lighthouse_id INT NOT NULL,
    lamp_type     VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    intensity_cd  INT NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (lighthouse_id) REFERENCES lighthouses(lighthouse_id)
);
CREATE TABLE power_generators (
    generator_id  INT PRIMARY KEY,
    lighthouse_id INT NOT NULL,
    capacity_kw   DECIMAL(6,2) NOT NULL,
    fuel_type     VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (lighthouse_id) REFERENCES lighthouses(lighthouse_id)
);
CREATE TABLE maintenance_crews (
    crew_id       INT PRIMARY KEY,
    lighthouse_id INT NOT NULL,
    supervisor    VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (lighthouse_id) REFERENCES lighthouses(lighthouse_id)
);

CREATE VIEW coastal_lighthouses AS
SELECT r.coast, r.region_name, l.lighthouse_id, l.lighthouse_name, l.elevation_m
FROM maritime_regions AS r
JOIN lighthouses AS l ON l.region_id = r.region_id;

CREATE VIEW powered_lighthouses AS
SELECT l.lighthouse_id, l.lighthouse_name, l.region_id, g.fuel_type, g.capacity_kw
FROM lighthouses AS l
JOIN power_generators AS g ON g.lighthouse_id = l.lighthouse_id;

CREATE VIEW crewed_lighthouses AS
SELECT l.lighthouse_id, c.supervisor
FROM lighthouses AS l
JOIN maintenance_crews AS c ON c.lighthouse_id = l.lighthouse_id;

DELIMITER //

CREATE PROCEDURE maintain(IN coast VARCHAR(40))
BEGIN
    DECLARE target_coast VARCHAR(40);
    SET target_coast = TRIM(LOWER(coast));

    SELECT cl.region_name, cl.elevation_m, b.intensity_cd, g.capacity_kw
    FROM coastal_lighthouses AS cl
    JOIN beacon_lamps AS b ON b.lighthouse_id = cl.lighthouse_id
    JOIN power_generators AS g ON g.lighthouse_id = cl.lighthouse_id
    WHERE LOWER(cl.coast) = target_coast
    ORDER BY cl.region_name, cl.elevation_m DESC;

    SELECT pl.lighthouse_name, pl.fuel_type, c.supervisor, r.region_name
    FROM powered_lighthouses AS pl
    JOIN maintenance_crews AS c ON c.lighthouse_id = pl.lighthouse_id
    JOIN maritime_regions AS r ON r.region_id = pl.region_id
    WHERE LOWER(r.coast) = target_coast
    ORDER BY c.supervisor, pl.lighthouse_name;

    SELECT cl.region_name, cl.lighthouse_name, b.lamp_type, g.capacity_kw, k.supervisor
    FROM coastal_lighthouses AS cl
    JOIN beacon_lamps AS b ON b.lighthouse_id = cl.lighthouse_id
    JOIN power_generators AS g ON g.lighthouse_id = cl.lighthouse_id
    JOIN crewed_lighthouses AS k ON k.lighthouse_id = cl.lighthouse_id
    WHERE LOWER(cl.coast) = target_coast
    ORDER BY cl.region_name, cl.lighthouse_name;
END //

DELIMITER ;

CALL maintain('western');

text_es: Develop a stored procedure `fabricate(style)` that takes a motorcycle style and generates three result sets for workshop builds. The database features tables for client orders, motorcycle frames, lead mechanics, and engine blocks. The first result set connects client orders, motorcycle frames, lead mechanics, and engine blocks to show the order date, frame material, mechanic name, and engine displacement, including only orders for the specified style that have started frame fabrication and engine assignment. The second query links motorcycle frames, engine blocks, custom fairings, and client orders to output the frame serial, engine displacement, fairing color, and order date, strictly for frames that have engines, fairings installed, and a valid order. The third query joins client orders, motorcycle frames, engine blocks, lead mechanics, and custom fairings to detail completed drivetrains, returning the order deadline, frame material, engine type, mechanic name, and fairing color. All combinations must enforce that corresponding rows exist in every joined table. Input style chopper returns three fabrication summaries.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE lead_mechanics (
    mechanic_id INT PRIMARY KEY, mechanic_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL, certification VARCHAR(40));

CREATE TABLE client_orders (
    order_id INT PRIMARY KEY, client_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL, style VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL,
    order_date DATE NOT NULL, deadline DATE NOT NULL,
    mechanic_id INT REFERENCES lead_mechanics(mechanic_id));

CREATE TABLE motorcycle_frames (
    frame_id INT PRIMARY KEY, order_id INT REFERENCES client_orders(order_id),
    frame_serial VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL, material VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL);

CREATE TABLE engine_blocks (
    engine_id INT PRIMARY KEY, frame_id INT REFERENCES motorcycle_frames(frame_id),
    displacement INT NOT NULL, engine_type VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL);

CREATE TABLE custom_fairings (
    fairing_id INT PRIMARY KEY, frame_id INT REFERENCES motorcycle_frames(frame_id),
    color VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL, installed BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE);

CREATE VIEW frame_build_state AS
SELECT mf.frame_id, mf.order_id, mf.frame_serial, mf.material,
       eb.displacement, eb.engine_type, cf.color, cf.installed
FROM motorcycle_frames AS mf
INNER JOIN engine_blocks AS eb ON eb.frame_id = mf.frame_id
INNER JOIN custom_fairings AS cf ON cf.frame_id = mf.frame_id;

CREATE VIEW order_crew AS
SELECT co.order_id, co.client_name, co.style, co.order_date, co.deadline, lm.mechanic_name
FROM client_orders AS co
INNER JOIN lead_mechanics AS lm ON lm.mechanic_id = co.mechanic_id;

DELIMITER //

CREATE PROCEDURE style_progress(IN style VARCHAR(40))
BEGIN
    SELECT oc.mechanic_name, COUNT(*) AS frames_in_build, SUM(fbs.installed) AS fairings_done
    FROM order_crew AS oc
    INNER JOIN frame_build_state AS fbs ON fbs.order_id = oc.order_id
    WHERE oc.style = style
    GROUP BY oc.mechanic_name
    ORDER BY frames_in_build DESC;
END //

CREATE PROCEDURE fabricate(IN style VARCHAR(40))
BEGIN
    SELECT co.order_date, mf.material, lm.mechanic_name, eb.displacement
    FROM client_orders AS co
    INNER JOIN motorcycle_frames AS mf ON mf.order_id = co.order_id
    INNER JOIN lead_mechanics AS lm ON lm.mechanic_id = co.mechanic_id
    INNER JOIN engine_blocks AS eb ON eb.frame_id = mf.frame_id
    WHERE co.style = style
    ORDER BY co.order_date;

    SELECT mf.frame_serial, eb.displacement, cf.color, co.order_date
    FROM motorcycle_frames AS mf
    INNER JOIN engine_blocks AS eb ON eb.frame_id = mf.frame_id
    INNER JOIN custom_fairings AS cf ON cf.frame_id = mf.frame_id
    INNER JOIN client_orders AS co ON co.order_id = mf.order_id
    WHERE co.style = style AND cf.installed = TRUE
    ORDER BY mf.frame_serial;

    SELECT co.deadline, mf.material, eb.engine_type, lm.mechanic_name, cf.color
    FROM client_orders AS co
    INNER JOIN motorcycle_frames AS mf ON mf.order_id = co.order_id
    INNER JOIN engine_blocks AS eb ON eb.frame_id = mf.frame_id
    INNER JOIN lead_mechanics AS lm ON lm.mechanic_id = co.mechanic_id
    INNER JOIN custom_fairings AS cf ON cf.frame_id = mf.frame_id
    WHERE co.style = style AND cf.installed = TRUE
    ORDER BY co.deadline;
END //

DELIMITER ;

CALL fabricate('chopper');
CALL style_progress('chopper');

CREATE TABLE motorcycle_frames (
    frame_id INT PRIMARY KEY, order_id INT REFERENCES client_orders(order_id),
    frame_serial VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL, material VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL);

CREATE TABLE engine_blocks (
    engine_id INT PRIMARY KEY, frame_id INT REFERENCES motorcycle_frames(frame_id),
    displacement INT NOT NULL, engine_type VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL);

CREATE TABLE custom_fairings (
    fairing_id INT PRIMARY KEY, frame_id INT REFERENCES motorcycle_frames(frame_id),
    color VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL, installed BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE);

CREATE VIEW frame_build_state AS
SELECT mf.frame_id, mf.order_id, mf.frame_serial, mf.material,
       eb.displacement, eb.engine_type, cf.color, cf.installed
FROM motorcycle_frames AS mf, engine_blocks AS eb, custom_fairings AS cf
WHERE eb.frame_id = mf.frame_id AND cf.frame_id = mf.frame_id;

CREATE VIEW order_crew AS
SELECT co.order_id, co.client_name, co.style, co.order_date, co.deadline, lm.mechanic_name
FROM client_orders AS co, lead_mechanics AS lm
WHERE lm.mechanic_id = co.mechanic_id;

DELIMITER //

CREATE PROCEDURE style_progress(IN style VARCHAR(40))
BEGIN
    SELECT oc.mechanic_name, COUNT(*) AS frames_in_build, SUM(fbs.installed) AS fairings_done
    FROM order_crew AS oc, frame_build_state AS fbs
    WHERE fbs.order_id = oc.order_id
    AND oc.style = style
    GROUP BY oc.mechanic_name
    ORDER BY frames_in_build DESC;
END //

CREATE PROCEDURE fabricate(IN style VARCHAR(40))
BEGIN
    SELECT co.order_date, mf.material, lm.mechanic_name, eb.displacement
    FROM client_orders AS co, motorcycle_frames AS mf, lead_mechanics AS lm, engine_blocks AS eb
    WHERE mf.order_id = co.order_id
    AND lm.mechanic_id = co.mechanic_id
    AND eb.frame_id = mf.frame_id
    AND co.style = style
    ORDER BY co.order_date;

    SELECT mf.frame_serial, eb.displacement, cf.color, co.order_date
    FROM motorcycle_frames AS mf, engine_blocks AS eb, custom_fairings AS cf, client_orders AS co
    WHERE eb.frame_id = mf.frame_id
    AND cf.frame_id = mf.frame_id
    AND co.order_id = mf.order_id
    AND co.style = style AND cf.installed = TRUE
    ORDER BY mf.frame_serial;

    SELECT co.deadline, mf.material, eb.engine_type, lm.mechanic_name, cf.color
    FROM client_orders AS co, motorcycle_frames AS mf, engine_blocks AS eb, lead_mechanics AS lm, custom_fairings AS cf
    WHERE mf.order_id = co.order_id
    AND eb.frame_id = mf.frame_id
    AND lm.mechanic_id = co.mechanic_id
    AND cf.frame_id = mf.frame_id
    AND co.style = style AND cf.installed = TRUE
    ORDER BY co.deadline;
END //

DELIMITER ;

CALL style_progress('chopper');

The first result set links booking agents, tour groups, flight itineraries, and helicopters to list the agent agency, group size, itinerary departure time, and helicopter registration, strictly for groups flying the specified route with an assigned helicopter. The second query connects helicopters, flight itineraries, tour guides, and tour groups to display the helicopter registration, flight duration, guide name, and group size, including only flights that have assigned helicopters, guides, and groups. The third query joins booking agents, tour groups, flight itineraries, tour guides, and helicopters to trace the guided groups back to their agents, returning the agent agency, group size, itinerary date, guide name, and helicopter registration. text_es: Develop a stored procedure `repair(metal)` that takes a metal type and outputs three result sets on instrument restorations. The records are divided into tables for musicians, broken instruments, repair tickets, replacement valves, and master technicians. The first query joins musicians, broken instruments, repair tickets, and replacement valves to show the musician name, instrument type, ticket estimate, and valve size, strictly for instruments made of the specified metal that have active tickets and allocated valves. The second query links repair tickets, replacement valves, master technicians, and broken instruments to output the ticket issue, valve size, technician name, and instrument type, keeping only tickets where replacement parts are allocated, a technician is assigned, and an instrument is linked. The third query connects musicians, broken instruments, repair tickets, replacement valves, and master technicians to list instruments undergoing valve replacement, returning the musician name, instrument type, ticket date, valve size, and technician name. Every combination must completely omit any rows lacking matches in the joined tables. Input metal silver returns three repair logs.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Musicians (
    musician_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    musician_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE MasterTechnicians (
    technician_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    technician_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE BrokenInstruments (
    instrument_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    musician_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES Musicians (musician_id),
    instrument_type VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL,
    metal VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE RepairTickets (
    ticket_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    instrument_id INT REFERENCES BrokenInstruments (instrument_id),
    technician_id INT REFERENCES MasterTechnicians (technician_id),
    issue VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    estimate DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,
    ticket_date DATE NOT NULL,
    status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE ReplacementValves (
    valve_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    ticket_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES RepairTickets (ticket_id),
    valve_size VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    allocated TINYINT NOT NULL
);

CREATE VIEW InstrumentOwners AS
SELECT m.musician_name, b.instrument_id, b.instrument_type, b.metal
FROM Musicians AS m
INNER JOIN BrokenInstruments AS b ON b.musician_id = m.musician_id;

CREATE VIEW AssignedTickets AS
SELECT t.ticket_id, t.instrument_id, t.issue, t.ticket_date, tech.technician_name
FROM RepairTickets AS t
INNER JOIN MasterTechnicians AS tech ON tech.technician_id = t.technician_id;

CREATE VIEW ValveWork AS
SELECT t.ticket_id, t.instrument_id, t.estimate, t.ticket_date, t.status, v.valve_size
FROM RepairTickets AS t
INNER JOIN ReplacementValves AS v ON v.ticket_id = t.ticket_id
WHERE v.allocated = 1;

DELIMITER //

CREATE PROCEDURE repair(IN p_metal VARCHAR(40))
BEGIN
    SELECT o.musician_name, o.instrument_type, w.estimate, w.valve_size
    FROM InstrumentOwners AS o
    INNER JOIN ValveWork AS w ON w.instrument_id = o.instrument_id
    WHERE o.metal = p_metal AND w.status = 'active'
    ORDER BY o.musician_name, w.valve_size;

    SELECT a.issue, w.valve_size, a.technician_name, b.instrument_type
    FROM AssignedTickets AS a
    INNER JOIN ValveWork AS w ON w.ticket_id = a.ticket_id
    INNER JOIN BrokenInstruments AS b ON b.instrument_id = a.instrument_id
    WHERE b.metal = p_metal
    ORDER BY a.technician_name, a.ticket_id;

    SELECT o.musician_name, o.instrument_type, a.ticket_date, w.valve_size, a.technician_name
    FROM InstrumentOwners AS o
    INNER JOIN AssignedTickets AS a ON a.instrument_id = o.instrument_id
    INNER JOIN ValveWork AS w ON w.ticket_id = a.ticket_id
    WHERE o.metal = p_metal
    ORDER BY a.ticket_date, o.musician_name;
END //

DELIMITER ;

CALL repair('silver');

text_es: Write a stored procedure `launch(weather)` that takes a weather condition string and returns three result sets for festival flights. The system comprises tables for festival days, balloon teams, balloon envelopes, burner systems, and safety inspectors. The first query links festival days, balloon teams, balloon envelopes, and burner systems to list the day date, team sponsor, envelope volume, and burner output, including only teams scheduled on days matching the given weather condition with burners attached. The second query connects balloon envelopes, burner systems, safety inspectors, and balloon teams to display the envelope color, burner output, inspector name, and team sponsor, strictly for balloons that have both burners attached, passed inspection, and belong to a team. The third query joins festival days, balloon teams, balloon envelopes, safety inspectors, and burner systems to identify cleared flights, returning the day date, team sponsor, envelope color, inspector name, and burner output. Only data that successfully links across all the combined entities can be included in the outputs. Example input weather clear yields three launch reports.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE FestivalDays (
    day_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    day_date DATE NOT NULL,
    weather VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE BalloonTeams (
    team_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    sponsor VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    day_id INT REFERENCES FestivalDays(day_id)
);

CREATE TABLE BalloonEnvelopes (
    envelope_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    color VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL,
    volume_m3 INT NOT NULL,
    team_id INT REFERENCES BalloonTeams(team_id)
);

CREATE TABLE BurnerSystems (
    burner_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    output_mw DECIMAL(5,2) NOT NULL,
    envelope_id INT REFERENCES BalloonEnvelopes(envelope_id)
);

CREATE TABLE SafetyInspectors (
    inspector_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    inspector_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    envelope_id INT REFERENCES BalloonEnvelopes(envelope_id),
    passed BOOLEAN NOT NULL
);

CREATE VIEW v_day_roster AS
SELECT FD.day_id, FD.day_date, FD.weather, BT.team_id, BT.sponsor,
       BE.envelope_id, BE.color, BE.volume_m3
FROM FestivalDays AS FD
INNER JOIN BalloonTeams AS BT ON BT.day_id = FD.day_id
INNER JOIN BalloonEnvelopes AS BE ON BE.team_id = BT.team_id;

CREATE VIEW v_equipped_balloons AS
SELECT BE.envelope_id, BE.color, BE.team_id, BS.output_mw
FROM BalloonEnvelopes AS BE
INNER JOIN BurnerSystems AS BS ON BS.envelope_id = BE.envelope_id;

CREATE VIEW v_cleared_balloons AS
SELECT EB.envelope_id, EB.color, EB.output_mw, SI.inspector_name
FROM v_equipped_balloons AS EB
INNER JOIN SafetyInspectors AS SI ON SI.envelope_id = EB.envelope_id
WHERE SI.passed = TRUE;

CREATE PROCEDURE launch(IN in_weather VARCHAR(30))
BEGIN
    SELECT DR.day_date, DR.sponsor, DR.volume_m3, EB.output_mw
    FROM v_day_roster AS DR
    INNER JOIN v_equipped_balloons AS EB ON EB.envelope_id = DR.envelope_id
    WHERE DR.weather = in_weather
    ORDER BY DR.day_date, DR.sponsor;

    SELECT CB.color, CB.output_mw, CB.inspector_name, BT.sponsor
    FROM v_cleared_balloons AS CB
    INNER JOIN BalloonEnvelopes AS BE ON BE.envelope_id = CB.envelope_id
    INNER JOIN BalloonTeams AS BT ON BT.team_id = BE.team_id
    ORDER BY CB.color;

    SELECT DR.day_date, DR.sponsor, DR.color, CB.inspector_name, CB.output_mw
    FROM v_day_roster AS DR
    INNER JOIN v_cleared_balloons AS CB ON CB.envelope_id = DR.envelope_id
    WHERE DR.weather = in_weather
    ORDER BY DR.day_date, DR.color;
END;

CALL launch('clear');

text_es: Create a stored procedure `press(variety)` that takes an olive variety string and generates three result sets for oil production. The data is held in tables for olive groves, harvest bins, washing stations, mechanical presses, and quality tasters. The first result set connects olive groves, harvest bins, washing stations, and mechanical presses to list the grove location, bin weight, station identifier, and press pressure, strictly for bins containing the specified variety that have reached a washing station and a mechanical press. The second query links harvest bins, mechanical presses, quality tasters, and olive groves to output the bin weight, press pressure, taster name, and grove location, including only pressed batches that have been assigned a taster and originate from a grove. The third query joins olive groves, harvest bins, mechanical presses, quality tasters, and washing stations to summarize tasted oils, returning the grove location, bin weight, press pressure, taster score, and station identifier. Ensure that only records fully linked across all the related entities are returned by the queries. Example input variety kalamata outputs three oil production reports.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE olive_groves (grove_id INT PRIMARY KEY, location VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL, variety VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE harvest_bins (bin_id INT PRIMARY KEY, grove_id INT, variety VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL, weight_kg DECIMAL(8,2) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE washing_stations (station_id INT PRIMARY KEY, bin_id INT, station_code VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE mechanical_presses (press_id INT PRIMARY KEY, bin_id INT, pressure_bar DECIMAL(6,2) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE quality_tasters (taster_id INT PRIMARY KEY, press_id INT, taster_name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL, score DECIMAL(4,1) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE press_runs (run_id INT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY, variety VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL, batches INT NOT NULL,
    total_weight DECIMAL(12,2), avg_score DECIMAL(5,2), run_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP);

DELIMITER $$

CREATE FUNCTION fully_linked_count(v_variety VARCHAR(40)) RETURNS INT
READS SQL DATA
BEGIN
    DECLARE n INT;
    SELECT COUNT(*) INTO n
    FROM olive_groves AS g
    INNER JOIN harvest_bins AS b ON b.grove_id = g.grove_id
    INNER JOIN washing_stations AS w ON w.bin_id = b.bin_id
    INNER JOIN mechanical_presses AS p ON p.bin_id = b.bin_id
    INNER JOIN quality_tasters AS t ON t.press_id = p.press_id
    WHERE b.variety = v_variety;
    RETURN n;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE press_wash_report(IN v_variety VARCHAR(40))
BEGIN
    SELECT g.location, b.weight_kg, w.station_code, p.pressure_bar
    FROM olive_groves AS g
    INNER JOIN harvest_bins AS b ON b.grove_id = g.grove_id
    INNER JOIN washing_stations AS w ON w.bin_id = b.bin_id
    INNER JOIN mechanical_presses AS p ON p.bin_id = b.bin_id
    WHERE b.variety = v_variety
    ORDER BY g.location, b.bin_id;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE press_taster_report(IN v_variety VARCHAR(40))
BEGIN
    SELECT b.weight_kg, p.pressure_bar, t.taster_name, g.location
    FROM harvest_bins AS b
    INNER JOIN mechanical_presses AS p ON p.bin_id = b.bin_id
    INNER JOIN quality_tasters AS t ON t.press_id = p.press_id
    INNER JOIN olive_groves AS g ON g.grove_id = b.grove_id
    WHERE b.variety = v_variety
    ORDER BY t.taster_name, b.weight_kg DESC;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE press_tasting_report(IN v_variety VARCHAR(40))
BEGIN
    SELECT g.location, b.weight_kg, p.pressure_bar, t.score, w.station_code
    FROM olive_groves AS g
    INNER JOIN harvest_bins AS b ON b.grove_id = g.grove_id
    INNER JOIN mechanical_presses AS p ON p.bin_id = b.bin_id
    INNER JOIN quality_tasters AS t ON t.press_id = p.press_id
    INNER JOIN washing_stations AS w ON w.bin_id = b.bin_id
    WHERE b.variety = v_variety
    ORDER BY t.score DESC, g.location;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE press_log_run(IN v_variety VARCHAR(40))
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO press_runs (variety, batches, total_weight, avg_score)
    SELECT v_variety, COUNT(*), SUM(b.weight_kg), AVG(t.score)
    FROM olive_groves AS g
    INNER JOIN harvest_bins AS b ON b.grove_id = g.grove_id
    INNER JOIN washing_stations AS w ON w.bin_id = b.bin_id
    INNER JOIN mechanical_presses AS p ON p.bin_id = b.bin_id
    INNER JOIN quality_tasters AS t ON t.press_id = p.press_id
    WHERE b.variety = v_variety;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE press(IN variety VARCHAR(40))
BEGIN
    IF fully_linked_count(variety) = 0 THEN
        SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000' SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'no fully linked batches for the requested variety';
    END IF;
    CALL press_wash_report(variety);
    CALL press_taster_report(variety);
    CALL press_tasting_report(variety);
    CALL press_log_run(variety);
END$$

DELIMITER ;

CALL press('kalamata');

text_es: Develop a stored procedure `animate(genre)` that takes a story genre and returns three result sets on theater operations. text_es: Write a stored procedure named `audit(month)` that builds three maintenance reports based on exact record matches. The operational database stores cabinets, boards, technicians, parts, suppliers, and logs. It is essential to only select records that have complete associations across all specified tables. The first report must fetch the cabinet title, board serial, technician name, and log notes by linking cabinets, boards, technicians, and logs for the given month. The second report should display the board serial, part name, supplier company, and log date by joining the boards, parts, suppliers, and logs where the part cost is above fifty. The third report must surface the technician name, part name, and supplier company by combining technicians, logs, parts, and suppliers. The procedure should return these three sets sequentially. For example, the first report could return Pac Man, serial one two three, Dave, and replaced capacitor.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE cabinets (cabinet_id INT PRIMARY KEY, title VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE boards (board_id INT PRIMARY KEY, cabinet_id INT NOT NULL, serial VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE technicians (technician_id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE suppliers (supplier_id INT PRIMARY KEY, company VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE parts (part_id INT PRIMARY KEY, supplier_id INT NOT NULL, name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    cost DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE logs (log_id INT PRIMARY KEY, board_id INT NOT NULL, technician_id INT NOT NULL,
    part_id INT NOT NULL, log_date DATE NOT NULL, notes VARCHAR(255));
CREATE TABLE audit_runs (run_id INT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY, audit_month INT NOT NULL, logged_jobs INT NOT NULL,
    part_spend DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL, busiest_technician VARCHAR(100), run_at DATETIME NOT NULL);
DELIMITER $$

CREATE FUNCTION busiest_technician(p_month INT) RETURNS VARCHAR(100) READS SQL DATA
BEGIN
    DECLARE v_name VARCHAR(100);
    SELECT t.name INTO v_name
    FROM logs AS l
    JOIN technicians AS t ON t.technician_id = l.technician_id
    WHERE MONTH(l.log_date) = p_month
    GROUP BY t.name
    ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
    LIMIT 1;
    RETURN v_name;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE record_audit_run(IN p_month INT)
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO audit_runs (audit_month, logged_jobs, part_spend, busiest_technician, run_at)
    SELECT p_month, COUNT(*), COALESCE(SUM(p.cost), 0), busiest_technician(p_month), NOW()
    FROM logs AS l
    JOIN boards AS b ON b.board_id = l.board_id
    JOIN cabinets AS c ON c.cabinet_id = b.cabinet_id
    JOIN technicians AS t ON t.technician_id = l.technician_id
    JOIN parts AS p ON p.part_id = l.part_id
    JOIN suppliers AS s ON s.supplier_id = p.supplier_id
    WHERE MONTH(l.log_date) = p_month;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE report_cabinet_logs(IN p_month INT)
BEGIN
    SELECT c.title AS cabinet_title, b.serial AS board_serial,
           t.name AS technician_name, l.notes AS log_notes
    FROM cabinets AS c
    JOIN boards AS b ON b.cabinet_id = c.cabinet_id
    JOIN logs AS l ON l.board_id = b.board_id
    JOIN technicians AS t ON t.technician_id = l.technician_id
    WHERE MONTH(l.log_date) = p_month
    ORDER BY c.title, b.serial;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE report_part_usage(IN p_month INT)
BEGIN
    SELECT b.serial AS board_serial, p.name AS part_name,
           s.company AS supplier_company, l.log_date
    FROM boards AS b
    JOIN logs AS l ON l.board_id = b.board_id
    JOIN parts AS p ON p.part_id = l.part_id
    JOIN suppliers AS s ON s.supplier_id = p.supplier_id
    WHERE p.cost > 50.00
      AND MONTH(l.log_date) = p_month
    ORDER BY l.log_date, b.serial;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE report_technician_parts(IN p_month INT)
BEGIN
    SELECT t.name AS technician_name, p.name AS part_name, s.company AS supplier_company
    FROM technicians AS t
    JOIN logs AS l ON l.technician_id = t.technician_id
    JOIN parts AS p ON p.part_id = l.part_id
    JOIN suppliers AS s ON s.supplier_id = p.supplier_id
    WHERE MONTH(l.log_date) = p_month
    ORDER BY t.name, p.name;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE audit(IN p_month INT)
BEGIN
    IF p_month < 1 OR p_month > 12 THEN
        SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000' SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'month must be between 1 and 12';
    END IF;
    CALL record_audit_run(p_month);
    CALL report_cabinet_logs(p_month);
    CALL report_part_usage(p_month);
    CALL report_technician_parts(p_month);
END$$
DELIMITER ;
CALL audit(3);
