text_es: Implement a script `formulate(quarter)` to summarize essential oil production. The tables include partner farms, crop harvests, distillation runs, copper stills, essential oil batches, chemical lab tests, and fragrance product lines. The first query must link partner farms, crop harvests, distillation runs, copper stills, and essential oil batches to trace all batches produced from a specific farm, showing harvest date, still capacity, and final batch volume. The second query connects essential oil batches, chemical lab tests, lab technicians, and fragrance product lines to find any batch rejected for impurities, displaying the farm origin, distillation temperature, lab technician name, and the affected product line. The third query joins fragrance product lines, essential oil batches, distillation runs, crop harvests, partner farms, and agricultural regions to map out the geographic source of all premium grade fragrances. An example output for the first query is (2023-08-15, 500, 25.5). The second query returns (Valley Farm, 100, Alice, Floral Mist).
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE agricultural_regions (region_id INT PRIMARY KEY, region_name VARCHAR(60), country VARCHAR(60));
CREATE TABLE partner_farms (farm_id INT PRIMARY KEY, farm_name VARCHAR(60), region_id INT);
CREATE TABLE crop_harvests (harvest_id INT PRIMARY KEY, farm_id INT, harvest_date DATE, crop_kg DECIMAL(10,2));
CREATE TABLE copper_stills (still_id INT PRIMARY KEY, still_name VARCHAR(60), capacity_l INT);
CREATE TABLE distillation_runs (run_id INT PRIMARY KEY, harvest_id INT, still_id INT, run_quarter CHAR(7), temperature_c INT);
CREATE TABLE fragrance_product_lines (line_id INT PRIMARY KEY, line_name VARCHAR(60), grade VARCHAR(20));
CREATE TABLE essential_oil_batches (batch_id INT PRIMARY KEY, run_id INT, line_id INT, volume_l DECIMAL(8,2));
CREATE TABLE lab_technicians (tech_id INT PRIMARY KEY, tech_name VARCHAR(60));
CREATE TABLE chemical_lab_tests (test_id INT PRIMARY KEY, batch_id INT, tech_id INT, verdict VARCHAR(20), defect VARCHAR(40));
DELIMITER $$
CREATE PROCEDURE top_harvest_farm(IN p_quarter CHAR(7), OUT p_farm VARCHAR(60))
BEGIN
  SELECT f.farm_name INTO p_farm
  FROM partner_farms AS f
  JOIN crop_harvests AS h ON h.farm_id = f.farm_id
  JOIN distillation_runs AS r ON r.harvest_id = h.harvest_id
  WHERE r.run_quarter = p_quarter
  GROUP BY f.farm_name
  ORDER BY SUM(h.crop_kg) DESC LIMIT 1;
END$$
CREATE PROCEDURE trace_farm_batches(IN p_quarter CHAR(7), IN p_farm VARCHAR(60))
BEGIN
  SELECT h.harvest_date, s.capacity_l, b.volume_l
  FROM partner_farms AS f
  JOIN crop_harvests AS h ON h.farm_id = f.farm_id
  JOIN distillation_runs AS r ON r.harvest_id = h.harvest_id
  JOIN copper_stills AS s ON s.still_id = r.still_id
  JOIN essential_oil_batches AS b ON b.run_id = r.run_id
  WHERE f.farm_name = p_farm AND r.run_quarter = p_quarter
  ORDER BY h.harvest_date, b.batch_id;
END$$
CREATE PROCEDURE impurity_rejections(IN p_quarter CHAR(7))
BEGIN
  SELECT f.farm_name, r.temperature_c, t.tech_name, l.line_name
  FROM essential_oil_batches AS b
  JOIN chemical_lab_tests AS c ON c.batch_id = b.batch_id
  JOIN lab_technicians AS t ON t.tech_id = c.tech_id
  JOIN fragrance_product_lines AS l ON l.line_id = b.line_id
  JOIN distillation_runs AS r ON r.run_id = b.run_id
  JOIN crop_harvests AS h ON h.harvest_id = r.harvest_id
  JOIN partner_farms AS f ON f.farm_id = h.farm_id
  WHERE c.verdict = 'REJECTED' AND c.defect = 'impurities'
    AND r.run_quarter = p_quarter
  ORDER BY f.farm_name, l.line_name;
END$$
CREATE PROCEDURE still_utilization(IN p_quarter CHAR(7))
BEGIN
  SELECT s.still_name, s.capacity_l, COUNT(r.run_id) AS runs, SUM(h.crop_kg) AS crop_kg
  FROM copper_stills AS s
  JOIN distillation_runs AS r ON r.still_id = s.still_id
  JOIN crop_harvests AS h ON h.harvest_id = r.harvest_id
  JOIN partner_farms AS f ON f.farm_id = h.farm_id
  WHERE r.run_quarter = p_quarter
  GROUP BY s.still_name, s.capacity_l
  ORDER BY crop_kg DESC;
END$$
CREATE PROCEDURE premium_origin_map(IN p_quarter CHAR(7))
BEGIN
  SELECT l.line_name, g.region_name, g.country, f.farm_name, SUM(b.volume_l) AS total_volume_l
  FROM fragrance_product_lines AS l
  JOIN essential_oil_batches AS b ON b.line_id = l.line_id
  JOIN distillation_runs AS r ON r.run_id = b.run_id
  JOIN crop_harvests AS h ON h.harvest_id = r.harvest_id
  JOIN partner_farms AS f ON f.farm_id = h.farm_id
  JOIN agricultural_regions AS g ON g.region_id = f.region_id
  WHERE l.grade = 'premium' AND r.run_quarter = p_quarter
  GROUP BY l.line_name, g.region_name, g.country, f.farm_name
  ORDER BY l.line_name, total_volume_l DESC;
END$$
CREATE PROCEDURE formulate(IN quarter CHAR(7))
BEGIN
  DECLARE v_farm VARCHAR(60);
  CALL top_harvest_farm(quarter, v_farm);
  CALL trace_farm_batches(quarter, v_farm);
  CALL impurity_rejections(quarter);
  CALL still_utilization(quarter);
  CALL premium_origin_map(quarter);
END$$
DELIMITER ;
CALL formulate('2023-Q3');

BEGIN

  FROM fragrance_product_lines AS l, essential_oil_batches AS b, distillation_runs AS r, crop_harvests AS h, partner_farms AS f, agricultural_regions AS g
  WHERE b.line_id = l.line_id

BEGIN

text_es: Create a procedure `score(tournament)` that outputs the final standings and analyses for a trampoline event. The database contains gymnastics clubs, athletes, routine elements, element difficulties, execution scores, judging panels, and final rankings. The first query links gymnastics clubs, athletes, routine elements, element difficulties, and execution scores to calculate the total difficulty value attempted by each club. The second query connects athletes, routine elements, execution scores, judging panels, and final rankings to display every instance where a judge awarded a perfect execution score, detailing the athlete name, club affiliation, element description, and judge name. The third query joins final rankings, athletes, gymnastics clubs, routine elements, element difficulties, and execution scores to find all medalists whose routine included a triple somersault, showing their final score and club location. For example, the first query outputs (Sky High Club, 45.2). The second query yields (John Doe, Flip City, Double Pike, Jane Smith).
text_nat:
CREATE PROCEDURE score(IN tournament VARCHAR(100))
BEGIN
    SELECT c.club_name, SUM(d.difficulty_value) AS total_difficulty
    FROM clubs AS c
    JOIN athletes AS a ON a.club_id = c.club_id
    JOIN routine_elements AS r ON r.athlete_id = a.athlete_id
    JOIN element_difficulties AS d ON d.element_id = r.element_id
    JOIN execution_scores AS e ON e.routine_element_id = r.routine_element_id
    WHERE r.tournament = tournament
    GROUP BY c.club_id, c.club_name
    ORDER BY total_difficulty DESC;

    SELECT a.athlete_name, c.club_name,
           r.element_description, p.judge_name
    FROM athletes AS a
    JOIN clubs AS c ON c.club_id = a.club_id
    JOIN routine_elements AS r ON r.athlete_id = a.athlete_id
    JOIN execution_scores AS e ON e.routine_element_id = r.routine_element_id
    JOIN judging_panels AS p ON p.judge_id = e.judge_id
    JOIN final_rankings AS f ON f.athlete_id = a.athlete_id
    WHERE r.tournament = tournament AND f.tournament = tournament
      AND e.execution_score = 10.0
    ORDER BY a.athlete_name, r.element_description;

    SELECT DISTINCT a.athlete_name, f.rank_position,
           f.final_score, c.club_location
    FROM final_rankings AS f
    JOIN athletes AS a ON a.athlete_id = f.athlete_id
    JOIN clubs AS c ON c.club_id = a.club_id
    JOIN routine_elements AS r ON r.athlete_id = a.athlete_id
    JOIN element_difficulties AS d ON d.element_id = r.element_id
    JOIN execution_scores AS e ON e.routine_element_id = r.routine_element_id
    WHERE f.tournament = tournament AND r.tournament = tournament
      AND f.rank_position <= 3
      AND r.element_description LIKE '%Triple Somersault%'
    ORDER BY f.rank_position;
END;

CREATE PROCEDURE club_execution_average(IN tournament VARCHAR(100))
BEGIN
    SELECT c.club_name, AVG(e.execution_score) AS mean_execution,
           COUNT(DISTINCT r.routine_element_id) AS elements_judged
    FROM clubs AS c
    JOIN athletes AS a ON a.club_id = c.club_id
    JOIN routine_elements AS r ON r.athlete_id = a.athlete_id
    JOIN execution_scores AS e ON e.routine_element_id = r.routine_element_id
    JOIN judging_panels AS p ON p.judge_id = e.judge_id
    WHERE r.tournament = tournament AND p.panel_role = 'Execution'
    GROUP BY c.club_id, c.club_name
    ORDER BY mean_execution DESC;
END;

CREATE PROCEDURE judge_workload(IN tournament VARCHAR(100))
BEGIN
    SELECT p.judge_name, COUNT(e.execution_score_id) AS scores_awarded,
           MIN(e.execution_score) AS lowest, MAX(e.execution_score) AS highest
    FROM judging_panels AS p
    JOIN execution_scores AS e ON e.judge_id = p.judge_id
    JOIN routine_elements AS r ON r.routine_element_id = e.routine_element_id
    JOIN athletes AS a ON a.athlete_id = r.athlete_id
    JOIN clubs AS c ON c.club_id = a.club_id
    WHERE r.tournament = tournament
    GROUP BY p.judge_id, p.judge_name
    ORDER BY scores_awarded DESC, p.judge_name;
END;

CREATE PROCEDURE run_event_report(IN tournament VARCHAR(100))
BEGIN
    CALL score(tournament);
    CALL club_execution_average(tournament);
    CALL judge_workload(tournament);
END;

CALL run_event_report('World Trampoline Final 2026');

text_es: Implement a stored procedure `harvest(week)` that schedules greenhouse operations. The tables include greenhouse sectors, nutrient mixing vats, irrigation pumps, floating grow rafts, plant growth cycles, harvest logs, and grocery distributors. The first query links greenhouse sectors, nutrient mixing vats, irrigation pumps, floating grow rafts, and plant growth cycles to identify any rafts currently receiving suboptimal nutrient levels, showing the sector name, vat chemical balance, pump status, and planted crop variety. The second query connects floating grow rafts, plant growth cycles, harvest logs, grocery distributors, and delivery trucks to create a shipping manifest for mature lettuces, detailing the harvest weight, distributor name, and truck license plate. The third query joins greenhouse sectors, irrigation pumps, floating grow rafts, plant growth cycles, harvest logs, and nutrient mixing vats to calculate the total yield per sector for a specific month. For example, the second query outputs rows like (500, Fresh Foods, ABC 123). The third query returns (Sector Seven, 4500).
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE sectors (sector_id INT PRIMARY KEY, sector_name VARCHAR(40));
CREATE TABLE vats (vat_id INT PRIMARY KEY, sector_id INT, chemical_balance DECIMAL(5,2), nutrient_ppm INT, vat_active TINYINT);
CREATE TABLE pumps (pump_id INT PRIMARY KEY, sector_id INT, vat_id INT, pump_status VARCHAR(20));
CREATE TABLE rafts (raft_id INT PRIMARY KEY, sector_id INT, pump_id INT, raft_slots INT);
CREATE TABLE cycles (cycle_id INT PRIMARY KEY, raft_id INT, crop_variety VARCHAR(30), growth_stage VARCHAR(20), plant_week INT);
CREATE TABLE distributors (distributor_id INT PRIMARY KEY, distributor_name VARCHAR(40));
CREATE TABLE trucks (truck_id INT PRIMARY KEY, distributor_id INT, license_plate VARCHAR(12));
CREATE TABLE harvest_logs (log_id INT PRIMARY KEY, cycle_id INT, distributor_id INT, truck_id INT,
    weight_kg INT, harvest_week INT, harvest_month INT);

DELIMITER $$

CREATE PROCEDURE pump_alerts(IN week INT)
BEGIN
    SELECT s.sector_name, p.pump_status, v.chemical_balance, COUNT(DISTINCT r.raft_id) AS stalled_rafts
    FROM sectors AS s
    JOIN pumps AS p ON p.sector_id = s.sector_id
    JOIN vats AS v ON v.vat_id = p.vat_id
    JOIN rafts AS r ON r.pump_id = p.pump_id
    JOIN cycles AS c ON c.raft_id = r.raft_id AND c.plant_week <= week
    WHERE p.pump_status <> 'running'
      AND c.growth_stage <> 'harvested'
    GROUP BY s.sector_id, s.sector_name, p.pump_status, v.chemical_balance
    ORDER BY stalled_rafts DESC;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE distributor_capacity(IN week INT)
BEGIN
    SELECT d.distributor_name, t.license_plate, SUM(h.weight_kg) AS booked_kg
    FROM distributors AS d
    JOIN trucks AS t ON t.distributor_id = d.distributor_id
    JOIN harvest_logs AS h ON h.truck_id = t.truck_id
    JOIN cycles AS c ON c.cycle_id = h.cycle_id
    WHERE h.harvest_week = week
      AND c.growth_stage = 'mature'
    GROUP BY d.distributor_id, d.distributor_name, t.truck_id, t.license_plate
    ORDER BY d.distributor_name, booked_kg DESC;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE harvest(IN week INT)
BEGIN
    DECLARE target_month INT;
    SET target_month = ((week - 1) DIV 4) + 1;

    SELECT s.sector_name, v.chemical_balance, p.pump_status, c.crop_variety
    FROM sectors AS s
    JOIN vats AS v ON v.sector_id = s.sector_id
    JOIN pumps AS p ON p.vat_id = v.vat_id
    JOIN rafts AS r ON r.pump_id = p.pump_id
    JOIN cycles AS c ON c.raft_id = r.raft_id
    WHERE v.nutrient_ppm < 800
      AND v.vat_active = 1
      AND c.plant_week <= week
      AND c.growth_stage <> 'harvested'
    ORDER BY s.sector_name, c.crop_variety;

    SELECT h.weight_kg, d.distributor_name, t.license_plate
    FROM rafts AS r
    JOIN cycles AS c ON c.raft_id = r.raft_id
    JOIN harvest_logs AS h ON h.cycle_id = c.cycle_id
    JOIN distributors AS d ON d.distributor_id = h.distributor_id
    JOIN trucks AS t ON t.truck_id = h.truck_id AND t.distributor_id = d.distributor_id
    WHERE c.crop_variety = 'lettuce'
      AND c.growth_stage = 'mature'
      AND h.harvest_week = week
    ORDER BY d.distributor_name, h.weight_kg DESC;

    SELECT s.sector_name, SUM(h.weight_kg) AS total_yield
    FROM sectors AS s
    JOIN pumps AS p ON p.sector_id = s.sector_id
    JOIN rafts AS r ON r.pump_id = p.pump_id
    JOIN cycles AS c ON c.raft_id = r.raft_id
    JOIN harvest_logs AS h ON h.cycle_id = c.cycle_id
    JOIN vats AS v ON v.vat_id = p.vat_id
    WHERE h.harvest_month = target_month
      AND v.vat_active = 1
    GROUP BY s.sector_id, s.sector_name
    HAVING SUM(h.weight_kg) > 0
    ORDER BY total_yield DESC;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE weekly_briefing(IN week INT)
BEGIN
    SELECT s.sector_name, COUNT(DISTINCT r.raft_id) AS active_rafts, SUM(r.raft_slots) AS planted_slots
    FROM sectors AS s
    JOIN rafts AS r ON r.sector_id = s.sector_id
    JOIN cycles AS c ON c.raft_id = r.raft_id
    WHERE c.plant_week <= week
      AND c.growth_stage IN ('seedling', 'growing', 'mature')
    GROUP BY s.sector_id, s.sector_name
    ORDER BY s.sector_name;

    CALL pump_alerts(week);
    CALL distributor_capacity(week);
    CALL harvest(week);
END$$

DELIMITER ;

CALL weekly_briefing(12);

      AND d.distributor_id = h.distributor_id
      AND t.truck_id = h.truck_id AND t.distributor_id = d.distributor_id
      AND c.crop_variety = 'lettuce'

    ORDER BY d.distributor_name, h.weight_kg DESC;

    SELECT s.sector_name, SUM(h.weight_kg) AS total_yield
    FROM sectors AS s, pumps AS p, rafts AS r, cycles AS c, harvest_logs AS h, vats AS v
    WHERE p.sector_id = s.sector_id
      AND r.pump_id = p.pump_id
      AND c.raft_id = r.raft_id
      AND h.cycle_id = c.cycle_id
      AND v.vat_id = p.vat_id
      AND h.harvest_month = target_month
      AND v.vat_active = 1
    GROUP BY s.sector_id, s.sector_name
    HAVING SUM(h.weight_kg) > 0

END$$

text_es: A laboratory system tracks synthesis reactors, chemical precursors, supply vendors, batch production runs, quality control scans, electron microscope images, purification centrifuges, technician shifts, and safety incident reports. Implement a procedure `report(reactor)` that outputs the full history of a specific machine. Combine the batch runs with the precursors used and the vendors that supplied them. Link quality control scans to the electron microscope images and the specific technician who authorized the batch. Connect the purification centrifuges used for each batch to their maintenance records and the safety incidents associated with that shift. Produce an overview showing the purity percentage of each batch, the associated vendor reliability, and the incident count. Example input: reactor serial 7. Output: 98 percent purity, 2 safety incidents.
text_nat:
CREATE PROCEDURE report(IN target_reactor_serial INT)
BEGIN
    CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE BatchBase AS
    SELECT 
        b.batch_id,
        b.purity_percentage,
        b.shift_id,
        r.serial
    FROM BatchRuns b
    JOIN Reactors r 
        ON b.reactor_id = r.reactor_id
    WHERE r.serial = target_reactor_serial;

    CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE VendorData AS
    SELECT 
        bb.batch_id,
        AVG(v.reliability_score) AS avg_reliability
    FROM BatchBase bb
    JOIN Precursors p 
        ON bb.batch_id = p.batch_id
    JOIN Vendors v 
        ON p.vendor_id = v.vendor_id
    GROUP BY bb.batch_id;

    CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE QualityData AS
    SELECT 
        bb.batch_id,
        t.name AS technician_name,
        COUNT(mi.image_id) AS image_count
    FROM BatchBase bb
    JOIN QualityScans qs 
        ON bb.batch_id = qs.batch_id
    JOIN MicroscopeImages mi 
        ON qs.scan_id = mi.scan_id
    JOIN Technicians t 
        ON qs.technician_id = t.technician_id
    GROUP BY bb.batch_id, t.name;

    CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE IncidentData AS
    SELECT 
        bb.batch_id,
        COUNT(DISTINCT mr.record_id) AS maintenance_count,
        COUNT(DISTINCT si.incident_id) AS incident_count
    FROM BatchBase bb
    JOIN Centrifuges c 
        ON bb.batch_id = c.batch_id
    JOIN MaintenanceRecords mr 
        ON c.centrifuge_id = mr.centrifuge_id
    JOIN SafetyIncidents si 
        ON bb.shift_id = si.shift_id
    GROUP BY bb.batch_id;

    SELECT 
        bb.batch_id,
        bb.purity_percentage,
        vd.avg_reliability,
        qd.technician_name,
        qd.image_count,
        id.maintenance_count,
        id.incident_count
    FROM BatchBase bb
    JOIN VendorData vd 
        ON bb.batch_id = vd.batch_id
    JOIN QualityData qd 
        ON bb.batch_id = qd.batch_id
    JOIN IncidentData id 
        ON bb.batch_id = id.batch_id;

    DROP TEMPORARY TABLE IF EXISTS BatchBase;
    DROP TEMPORARY TABLE IF EXISTS VendorData;
    DROP TEMPORARY TABLE IF EXISTS QualityData;
    DROP TEMPORARY TABLE IF EXISTS IncidentData;
END;

CREATE PROCEDURE report(IN target_reactor_serial INT)
BEGIN

    WHERE bb.batch_id = p.batch_id

    CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE QualityData AS

        t.name AS technician_name,

    FROM BatchBase bb, QualityScans qs, MicroscopeImages mi, Technicians t
    WHERE bb.batch_id = qs.batch_id
      AND qs.scan_id = mi.scan_id
      AND qs.technician_id = t.technician_id
    GROUP BY bb.batch_id, t.name;

    CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE IncidentData AS
    SELECT 
        bb.batch_id,
        COUNT(DISTINCT mr.record_id) AS maintenance_count,
        COUNT(DISTINCT si.incident_id) AS incident_count
    FROM BatchBase bb, Centrifuges c, MaintenanceRecords mr, SafetyIncidents si
    WHERE bb.batch_id = c.batch_id
      AND c.centrifuge_id = mr.centrifuge_id

text_es: A skyscraper management system tracks elevator cabins, vertical shafts, horizontal transit corridors, passenger call requests, magnetic rail segments, power substation feeds, emergency braking tests, maintenance technicians, and vendor warranties. Create a procedure `inspect(building)` that details transit efficiency and safety. Link the passenger calls to the elevator cabins and the horizontal corridors used. Match magnetic rail segments with the power substation feeds and the daily voltage fluctuations. Connect emergency braking tests to the maintenance technicians and the vendor warranties for the replaced parts. Output the average wait time per cabin, the total horizontal distance traveled, and the count of successful braking tests. Example input: building number 12. Output: 45 seconds average wait, 1200 meters horizontal travel.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE buildings (building_id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(80));
CREATE TABLE shafts (shaft_id INT PRIMARY KEY, building_id INT, orientation VARCHAR(20));
CREATE TABLE cabins (cabin_id INT PRIMARY KEY, shaft_id INT, code VARCHAR(20));
CREATE TABLE corridors (corridor_id INT PRIMARY KEY, building_id INT, length_m DECIMAL(8,2));
CREATE TABLE calls (call_id INT PRIMARY KEY, cabin_id INT, corridor_id INT, wait_seconds INT, requested_at DATETIME);
CREATE TABLE substation_feeds (feed_id INT PRIMARY KEY, building_id INT, nominal_voltage INT);
CREATE TABLE rail_segments (segment_id INT PRIMARY KEY, shaft_id INT, feed_id INT, length_m DECIMAL(8,2));
CREATE TABLE voltage_readings (reading_id INT PRIMARY KEY, feed_id INT, reading_day DATE, fluctuation_pct DECIMAL(5,2));
CREATE TABLE technicians (technician_id INT PRIMARY KEY, full_name VARCHAR(80));
CREATE TABLE warranties (warranty_id INT PRIMARY KEY, vendor_name VARCHAR(80), part_name VARCHAR(80), expires_on DATE);
CREATE TABLE braking_tests (test_id INT PRIMARY KEY, cabin_id INT, technician_id INT, warranty_id INT, result VARCHAR(16), tested_on DATE);

DELIMITER $$

CREATE PROCEDURE inspect(IN building INT)
BEGIN
    SELECT b.building_id, b.name, COUNT(DISTINCT s.shaft_id) AS shafts, COUNT(c.cabin_id) AS cabins
    FROM buildings AS b
    JOIN shafts AS s ON s.building_id = b.building_id
    JOIN cabins AS c ON c.shaft_id = s.shaft_id
    WHERE b.building_id = building
    GROUP BY b.building_id, b.name;

    SELECT c.code AS cabin, ROUND(AVG(cl.wait_seconds)) AS avg_wait_seconds, SUM(co.length_m) AS horizontal_m
    FROM cabins AS c
    JOIN shafts AS s ON c.shaft_id = s.shaft_id
    JOIN calls AS cl ON cl.cabin_id = c.cabin_id
    JOIN corridors AS co ON cl.corridor_id = co.corridor_id
    WHERE s.building_id = building
    GROUP BY c.code
    ORDER BY c.code;

    SELECT co.corridor_id, co.length_m, COUNT(cl.call_id) AS transits, SUM(co.length_m) AS distance_m
    FROM corridors AS co
    JOIN calls AS cl ON cl.corridor_id = co.corridor_id
    JOIN cabins AS c ON cl.cabin_id = c.cabin_id
    WHERE co.building_id = building
    GROUP BY co.corridor_id, co.length_m
    ORDER BY distance_m DESC;

    SELECT r.segment_id, r.length_m, f.nominal_voltage,
           ROUND(AVG(v.fluctuation_pct), 2) AS avg_daily_fluctuation_pct,
           MAX(v.fluctuation_pct) AS worst_fluctuation_pct
    FROM rail_segments AS r
    JOIN substation_feeds AS f ON r.feed_id = f.feed_id
    JOIN voltage_readings AS v ON v.feed_id = f.feed_id
    JOIN shafts AS s ON r.shaft_id = s.shaft_id
    WHERE s.building_id = building
    GROUP BY r.segment_id, r.length_m, f.nominal_voltage
    ORDER BY worst_fluctuation_pct DESC;

    SELECT bt.test_id, c.code AS cabin, t.full_name AS technician,
           w.vendor_name, w.part_name, w.expires_on, bt.result
    FROM braking_tests AS bt
    JOIN technicians AS t ON bt.technician_id = t.technician_id
    JOIN warranties AS w ON bt.warranty_id = w.warranty_id
    JOIN cabins AS c ON bt.cabin_id = c.cabin_id
    JOIN shafts AS s ON c.shaft_id = s.shaft_id
    WHERE s.building_id = building
    ORDER BY bt.tested_on DESC;

    SELECT (SELECT ROUND(AVG(cl.wait_seconds))
            FROM calls AS cl
            JOIN cabins AS c ON cl.cabin_id = c.cabin_id
            JOIN shafts AS s ON c.shaft_id = s.shaft_id
            WHERE s.building_id = building) AS avg_wait_seconds,
           (SELECT SUM(co.length_m)
            FROM calls AS cl
            JOIN corridors AS co ON cl.corridor_id = co.corridor_id
            JOIN cabins AS c ON cl.cabin_id = c.cabin_id
            JOIN shafts AS s ON c.shaft_id = s.shaft_id
            WHERE s.building_id = building) AS total_horizontal_m,
           (SELECT COUNT(*)
            FROM braking_tests AS bt
            JOIN cabins AS c ON bt.cabin_id = c.cabin_id
            JOIN shafts AS s ON c.shaft_id = s.shaft_id
            WHERE s.building_id = building
              AND bt.result = 'PASS') AS successful_braking_tests;
END$$

text_alt:
CREATE TABLE buildings (building_id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(80));
CREATE TABLE shafts (shaft_id INT PRIMARY KEY, building_id INT, orientation VARCHAR(20));
CREATE TABLE cabins (cabin_id INT PRIMARY KEY, shaft_id INT, code VARCHAR(20));
CREATE TABLE corridors (corridor_id INT PRIMARY KEY, building_id INT, length_m DECIMAL(8,2));
CREATE TABLE calls (call_id INT PRIMARY KEY, cabin_id INT, corridor_id INT, wait_seconds INT, requested_at DATETIME);
CREATE TABLE substation_feeds (feed_id INT PRIMARY KEY, building_id INT, nominal_voltage INT);
CREATE TABLE rail_segments (segment_id INT PRIMARY KEY, shaft_id INT, feed_id INT, length_m DECIMAL(8,2));
CREATE TABLE voltage_readings (reading_id INT PRIMARY KEY, feed_id INT, reading_day DATE, fluctuation_pct DECIMAL(5,2));
CREATE TABLE technicians (technician_id INT PRIMARY KEY, full_name VARCHAR(80));
CREATE TABLE warranties (warranty_id INT PRIMARY KEY, vendor_name VARCHAR(80), part_name VARCHAR(80), expires_on DATE);
CREATE TABLE braking_tests (test_id INT PRIMARY KEY, cabin_id INT, technician_id INT, warranty_id INT, result VARCHAR(16), tested_on DATE);

DELIMITER $$

CREATE PROCEDURE inspect(IN building INT)
BEGIN
    SELECT b.building_id, b.name, COUNT(DISTINCT s.shaft_id) AS shafts, COUNT(c.cabin_id) AS cabins
    FROM buildings AS b,
    shafts AS s,
    cabins AS c
    WHERE s.building_id = b.building_id AND c.shaft_id = s.shaft_id AND b.building_id = building
    GROUP BY b.building_id, b.name;

    SELECT c.code AS cabin, ROUND(AVG(cl.wait_seconds)) AS avg_wait_seconds, SUM(co.length_m) AS horizontal_m
    FROM cabins AS c,
    shafts AS s,
    calls AS cl,
    corridors AS co
    WHERE c.shaft_id = s.shaft_id AND cl.cabin_id = c.cabin_id AND cl.corridor_id = co.corridor_id AND s.building_id = building
    GROUP BY c.code
    ORDER BY c.code;

    SELECT co.corridor_id, co.length_m, COUNT(cl.call_id) AS transits, SUM(co.length_m) AS distance_m
    FROM corridors AS co,
    calls AS cl,
    cabins AS c
    WHERE cl.corridor_id = co.corridor_id AND cl.cabin_id = c.cabin_id AND co.building_id = building
    GROUP BY co.corridor_id, co.length_m
    ORDER BY distance_m DESC;

    SELECT r.segment_id, r.length_m, f.nominal_voltage,
           ROUND(AVG(v.fluctuation_pct), 2) AS avg_daily_fluctuation_pct,
           MAX(v.fluctuation_pct) AS worst_fluctuation_pct
    FROM rail_segments AS r,
    substation_feeds AS f,
    voltage_readings AS v,
    shafts AS s
    WHERE r.feed_id = f.feed_id AND v.feed_id = f.feed_id AND r.shaft_id = s.shaft_id AND s.building_id = building
    GROUP BY r.segment_id, r.length_m, f.nominal_voltage
    ORDER BY worst_fluctuation_pct DESC;

    SELECT bt.test_id, c.code AS cabin, t.full_name AS technician,
           w.vendor_name, w.part_name, w.expires_on, bt.result
    FROM braking_tests AS bt,
    technicians AS t,
    warranties AS w,
    cabins AS c,
    shafts AS s
    WHERE bt.technician_id = t.technician_id AND bt.warranty_id = w.warranty_id AND bt.cabin_id = c.cabin_id AND c.shaft_id = s.shaft_id AND s.building_id = building
    ORDER BY bt.tested_on DESC;

    SELECT (SELECT ROUND(AVG(cl.wait_seconds))
            FROM calls AS cl,
            cabins AS c,
            shafts AS s
            WHERE cl.cabin_id = c.cabin_id AND c.shaft_id = s.shaft_id AND s.building_id = building) AS avg_wait_seconds,
           (SELECT SUM(co.length_m)
            FROM calls AS cl,
            corridors AS co,
            cabins AS c,
            shafts AS s
            WHERE cl.corridor_id = co.corridor_id AND cl.cabin_id = c.cabin_id AND c.shaft_id = s.shaft_id AND s.building_id = building) AS total_horizontal_m,
           (SELECT COUNT(*)
            FROM braking_tests AS bt,
            cabins AS c,
            shafts AS s
            WHERE bt.cabin_id = c.cabin_id AND c.shaft_id = s.shaft_id AND s.building_id = building
              AND bt.result = 'PASS') AS successful_braking_tests;
END$$

DELIMITER ;

Write a procedure `assess(patient)` that compiles a therapy progress report. Combine patient therapy plans with the exoskeleton suits, joint motor actuators, and the clinical therapists assigned. Link session progress metrics to the balance sensor pads and the software firmware versions active on the suit. Connect maintenance diagnostics to the specific actuators and the repair technicians. Tie the therapy plans to the insurance authorization forms and the billing codes. Output the total steps taken, the average balance score, and the number of maintenance faults. Example input: patient number 88. Output: 2000 steps taken, 92 percent balance score.
text_nat:
DELIMITER $$

CREATE FUNCTION total_steps(p_patient INT) RETURNS INT DETERMINISTIC
BEGIN
  DECLARE v_steps INT;
  SELECT IFNULL(SUM(sm.steps), 0) INTO v_steps
    FROM therapy_plans AS tp
    JOIN session_metrics AS sm ON sm.plan_id = tp.plan_id
   WHERE tp.patient_id = p_patient;
  RETURN v_steps;
END$$

CREATE FUNCTION avg_balance(p_patient INT) RETURNS DECIMAL(5,2) DETERMINISTIC
BEGIN
  DECLARE v_score DECIMAL(5,2);
  SELECT IFNULL(ROUND(AVG(sm.balance_score), 2), 0) INTO v_score
    FROM therapy_plans AS tp
    JOIN session_metrics AS sm ON sm.plan_id = tp.plan_id
    JOIN sensor_pads AS sp ON sp.pad_id = sm.pad_id
   WHERE tp.patient_id = p_patient
     AND sp.calibrated = 1;
  RETURN v_score;
END$$

CREATE FUNCTION fault_count(p_patient INT) RETURNS INT DETERMINISTIC
BEGIN
  DECLARE v_faults INT;
  SELECT COUNT(*) INTO v_faults
    FROM therapy_plans AS tp
    JOIN actuators AS ac ON ac.suit_id = tp.suit_id
    JOIN maintenance_diagnostics AS md ON md.actuator_id = ac.actuator_id
   WHERE tp.patient_id = p_patient
     AND md.fault_code IS NOT NULL;
  RETURN v_faults;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE assess(IN patient INT)
BEGIN
  SELECT tp.plan_id, s.model AS suit_model, ac.joint_name, th.full_name AS therapist
    FROM therapy_plans AS tp
    JOIN suits AS s ON s.suit_id = tp.suit_id
    JOIN actuators AS ac ON ac.suit_id = s.suit_id
    JOIN therapists AS th ON th.therapist_id = tp.therapist_id
   WHERE tp.patient_id = patient
   ORDER BY tp.plan_id, ac.joint_name;

  SELECT sm.session_date, sp.pad_label, fw.version AS firmware, sm.steps, sm.balance_score
    FROM therapy_plans AS tp
    JOIN session_metrics AS sm ON sm.plan_id = tp.plan_id
    JOIN sensor_pads AS sp ON sp.pad_id = sm.pad_id
    JOIN firmware_versions AS fw ON fw.firmware_id = sm.firmware_id
   WHERE tp.patient_id = patient
   ORDER BY sm.session_date;

  SELECT ac.joint_name, md.fault_code, md.severity, tc.full_name AS technician
    FROM therapy_plans AS tp
    JOIN actuators AS ac ON ac.suit_id = tp.suit_id
    JOIN maintenance_diagnostics AS md ON md.actuator_id = ac.actuator_id
    JOIN technicians AS tc ON tc.technician_id = md.technician_id
   WHERE tp.patient_id = patient
   ORDER BY md.severity DESC;

  SELECT ia.form_number, ia.valid_until, bc.billing_code, bc.description
    FROM therapy_plans AS tp
    JOIN insurance_authorizations AS ia ON ia.auth_id = tp.auth_id
    JOIN billing_codes AS bc ON bc.billing_code_id = ia.billing_code_id
   WHERE tp.patient_id = patient;

  SELECT CONCAT(total_steps(patient), ' steps taken') AS steps_summary,
         CONCAT(avg_balance(patient), ' percent balance score') AS balance_summary,
         fault_count(patient) AS maintenance_faults;
END$$

text_es: A material science database tracks battery cells, charge cycle testers, thermal imaging cameras, internal resistance probes, degradation models, laboratory safety enclosures, material synthesis batches, principal investigators, and consumer electronics partners. Create a procedure `review(cell)` that determines the longevity of the battery. Combine battery cells with the charge cycle testers, thermal imaging cameras, and the internal resistance probes. Link degradation models to the material synthesis batches and the laboratory safety enclosures used. Connect principal investigators to the testing phases and the consumer electronics partners reviewing the data. Return the total charge cycles completed, the peak thermal output, and the estimated lifespan. Example input: cell number 10. Output: 5000 charge cycles, 45 degrees peak thermal output.
text_nat:
DELIMITER $$

CREATE TABLE battery_cells (cell_id INT PRIMARY KEY, batch_id INT, enclosure_id INT, model_id INT, phase_id INT)$$
CREATE TABLE cycle_testers (tester_id INT PRIMARY KEY, cell_id INT, cycles_completed INT)$$
CREATE TABLE thermal_cameras (camera_id INT PRIMARY KEY, cell_id INT, peak_temp_c DECIMAL(6,2))$$
CREATE TABLE resistance_probes (probe_id INT PRIMARY KEY, cell_id INT, milliohms DECIMAL(6,2))$$
CREATE TABLE synthesis_batches (batch_id INT PRIMARY KEY, material VARCHAR(40), capacity_mah INT)$$
CREATE TABLE safety_enclosures (enclosure_id INT PRIMARY KEY, max_temp_c DECIMAL(6,2))$$
CREATE TABLE degradation_models (model_id INT PRIMARY KEY, batch_id INT, enclosure_id INT, fade_per_kcycle DECIMAL(6,3))$$
CREATE TABLE testing_phases (phase_id INT PRIMARY KEY, investigator_id INT, phase_name VARCHAR(40))$$
CREATE TABLE investigators (investigator_id INT PRIMARY KEY, inv_name VARCHAR(60))$$
CREATE TABLE partners (partner_id INT PRIMARY KEY, investigator_id INT, company VARCHAR(60))$$

CREATE FUNCTION fn_total_cycles(p_cell INT) RETURNS INT DETERMINISTIC
BEGIN
  DECLARE v_cycles INT;
  SELECT COALESCE(SUM(t.cycles_completed), 0) INTO v_cycles
    FROM battery_cells AS c
    JOIN cycle_testers AS t ON t.cell_id = c.cell_id
   WHERE c.cell_id = p_cell;
  RETURN v_cycles;
END$$

CREATE FUNCTION fn_peak_thermal(p_cell INT) RETURNS DECIMAL(6,2) DETERMINISTIC
BEGIN
  DECLARE v_peak DECIMAL(6,2);
  SELECT MAX(LEAST(cam.peak_temp_c, enc.max_temp_c)) INTO v_peak
    FROM battery_cells AS c
    JOIN thermal_cameras AS cam ON cam.cell_id = c.cell_id
    JOIN safety_enclosures AS enc ON enc.enclosure_id = c.enclosure_id
   WHERE c.cell_id = p_cell;
  RETURN v_peak;
END$$

CREATE FUNCTION fn_avg_resistance(p_cell INT) RETURNS DECIMAL(6,2) DETERMINISTIC
BEGIN
  DECLARE v_ohms DECIMAL(6,2);
  SELECT COALESCE(AVG(rp.milliohms), 0) INTO v_ohms
    FROM battery_cells AS c
    JOIN resistance_probes AS rp ON rp.cell_id = c.cell_id
   WHERE c.cell_id = p_cell;
  RETURN v_ohms;
END$$

CREATE VIEW v_model_limits AS
  SELECT dm.model_id, dm.fade_per_kcycle, sb.material, sb.capacity_mah, enc.max_temp_c
    FROM degradation_models AS dm
    JOIN synthesis_batches AS sb ON sb.batch_id = dm.batch_id
    JOIN safety_enclosures AS enc ON enc.enclosure_id = dm.enclosure_id$$

CREATE FUNCTION fn_estimated_lifespan(p_cell INT) RETURNS INT DETERMINISTIC
BEGIN
  DECLARE v_life INT;
  SELECT FLOOR(20.0 / (m.fade_per_kcycle * (1 + fn_avg_resistance(p_cell) / 100))
               * 1000 * (m.capacity_mah / 2500)) INTO v_life
    FROM battery_cells AS c
    JOIN v_model_limits AS m ON m.model_id = c.model_id
   WHERE c.cell_id = p_cell;
  RETURN v_life;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE review(IN cell INT)
BEGIN
  SELECT c.cell_id, i.inv_name, tp.phase_name,
         GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT p.company ORDER BY p.company) AS reviewers,
         fn_total_cycles(c.cell_id) AS total_charge_cycles,
         fn_peak_thermal(c.cell_id) AS peak_thermal_output_c,
         fn_estimated_lifespan(c.cell_id) AS estimated_lifespan_cycles
    FROM battery_cells AS c
    JOIN testing_phases AS tp ON tp.phase_id = c.phase_id
    JOIN investigators AS i ON i.investigator_id = tp.investigator_id
    JOIN partners AS p ON p.investigator_id = i.investigator_id
   WHERE c.cell_id = cell
   GROUP BY c.cell_id, i.inv_name, tp.phase_name;
END$$

DELIMITER ;

CALL review(10);

First, generate a leaderboard by combining event runs, dogs, handlers, and competition rings to list the handler name, dog name, ring location, and total time. Second, analyze errors by connecting obstacle faults, event runs, dogs, and obstacle types to count the most common obstacle failures for each dog. Third, summarize participation by linking dogs, breed registries, and handlers to count how many distinct handlers are registered per breed category. Fourth, calculate ring utilization by joining competition rings, event runs, judges, and handlers to display the judge name, ring location, and number of unique handlers evaluated. The main entry point must invoke these four queries and return their aggregated results as a four element tuple.

Implement a function named `calculate(database)` to aggregate astronomical data for a pulsar tracking observatory. The database contains tables for radio telescopes, observed pulsars, timing residuals, observation shifts, astronomer schedules, and calibration sources. Draft four scientific queries. The first combines timing residuals, observed pulsars, radio telescopes, and observation shifts to calculate the average timing error for each pulsar across different telescopes. The second joins astronomer schedules, observation shifts, radio telescopes, and observed pulsars to list the lead astronomer for every observation of a specific pulsar. The third links calibration sources, radio telescopes, and timing residuals to identify which calibration source was active during periods of high residual noise. The fourth connects observed pulsars, celestial coordinates, and radio telescopes to map which telescopes have line of sight to which pulsars during the current epoch. The main routine must return all four query results grouped in a tuple.
text_nat:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION avg_timing_error(p_database text)
RETURNS TABLE (pulsar text, telescope text, mean_error_us numeric)
AS $$
    SELECT p.designation, t.name, ROUND(AVG(ABS(r.residual_us)), 3)
    FROM timing_residuals AS r
    JOIN observed_pulsars AS p ON r.pulsar_id = p.pulsar_id
    JOIN observation_shifts AS s ON r.shift_id = s.shift_id
    JOIN radio_telescopes AS t ON s.telescope_id = t.telescope_id
    WHERE t.archive_database = p_database
    GROUP BY p.designation, t.name
    ORDER BY p.designation, t.name;
$$ LANGUAGE sql STABLE;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION lead_astronomers(p_database text, p_pulsar text)
RETURNS TABLE (shift_id integer, started timestamp, telescope text, lead_name text)
AS $$
    SELECT s.shift_id, s.start_time, t.name, a.astronomer_name
    FROM astronomer_schedules AS a
    JOIN observation_shifts AS s ON a.shift_id = s.shift_id
    JOIN radio_telescopes AS t ON s.telescope_id = t.telescope_id
    JOIN observed_pulsars AS p ON s.pulsar_id = p.pulsar_id
    WHERE a.role = 'LEAD'
      AND p.designation = p_pulsar
      AND t.archive_database = p_database
    ORDER BY s.start_time;
$$ LANGUAGE sql STABLE;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION noisy_calibration_sources(p_database text, p_threshold numeric)
RETURNS TABLE (telescope text, source_name text, noisy_samples bigint, peak_residual_us numeric)
AS $$
    SELECT t.name, c.source_name, COUNT(*), MAX(ABS(r.residual_us))
    FROM calibration_sources AS c
    JOIN radio_telescopes AS t ON c.telescope_id = t.telescope_id
    JOIN observation_shifts AS s ON s.telescope_id = t.telescope_id
    JOIN timing_residuals AS r ON r.shift_id = s.shift_id
    WHERE ABS(r.residual_us) > p_threshold
      AND s.start_time >= c.active_from
      AND s.start_time < c.active_to
      AND t.archive_database = p_database
    GROUP BY t.name, c.source_name
    ORDER BY 4 DESC;
$$ LANGUAGE sql STABLE;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION visibility_map(p_database text, p_epoch text)
RETURNS TABLE (telescope text, pulsar text, right_ascension numeric, declination numeric)
AS $$
    SELECT t.name, p.designation, k.right_ascension, k.declination
    FROM observed_pulsars AS p
    JOIN celestial_coordinates AS k ON p.coord_id = k.coord_id
    JOIN radio_telescopes AS t ON k.declination BETWEEN t.dec_min AND t.dec_max
    WHERE k.epoch = p_epoch
      AND t.archive_database = p_database
    ORDER BY t.name, p.designation;
$$ LANGUAGE sql STABLE;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION calculate(database text)
RETURNS TABLE (timing_errors refcursor, leads refcursor, calibration refcursor, visibility refcursor)
AS $$
DECLARE
    v_target text;
    v_epoch  text;
BEGIN
    SELECT p.designation
    INTO v_target
    FROM timing_residuals AS r
    JOIN observed_pulsars AS p ON r.pulsar_id = p.pulsar_id
    JOIN observation_shifts AS s ON r.shift_id = s.shift_id
    JOIN radio_telescopes AS t ON s.telescope_id = t.telescope_id
    WHERE t.archive_database = database
    GROUP BY p.designation
    ORDER BY AVG(ABS(r.residual_us)) DESC
    LIMIT 1;
    SELECT MAX(k.epoch) INTO v_epoch FROM celestial_coordinates AS k;
    OPEN timing_errors FOR SELECT * FROM avg_timing_error(database);
    OPEN leads FOR SELECT * FROM lead_astronomers(database, v_target);
    OPEN calibration FOR SELECT * FROM noisy_calibration_sources(database, 25.0);
    OPEN visibility FOR SELECT * FROM visibility_map(database, v_epoch);
    RETURN NEXT;
    RETURN;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

text_es: Write a function named `navigate(db)` to process flight logistics for an urban air mobility startup. The relational database holds tables for passenger drones, landing pads, flight itineraries, pilot supervisors, weather advisories, and battery swap stations. Construct four flight operations queries. The first joins flight itineraries, passenger drones, landing pads, and pilot supervisors to generate a daily flight manifest showing the departure pad, drone registration, and overseeing pilot. The second connects weather advisories, landing pads, flight itineraries, and passenger drones to identify which upcoming flights are scheduled to land at pads currently under high wind warnings. The third links battery swap stations, passenger drones, maintenance logs, and flight itineraries to find drones that completed long distance flights and need immediate cell replacements. The fourth joins pilot supervisors, training certifications, passenger drones, and drone models to verify that all supervisors are legally certified to oversee the specific drone models currently in the air. Return all four query lists in one tuple.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE fleets (fleet_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, db_name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE drone_models (model_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, model_name TEXT NOT NULL, max_range_km NUMERIC(6,1) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE passenger_drones (drone_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, registration TEXT NOT NULL, model_id INTEGER REFERENCES drone_models, fleet_id INTEGER REFERENCES fleets);
CREATE TABLE landing_pads (pad_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, pad_name TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE pilot_supervisors (pilot_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, pilot_name TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE flight_itineraries (flight_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, drone_id INTEGER REFERENCES passenger_drones, dep_pad_id INTEGER REFERENCES landing_pads,
    arr_pad_id INTEGER REFERENCES landing_pads, pilot_id INTEGER REFERENCES pilot_supervisors, flight_date DATE NOT NULL, distance_km NUMERIC(6,1) NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE weather_advisories (advisory_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, pad_id INTEGER REFERENCES landing_pads, advisory_type TEXT NOT NULL, wind_kph NUMERIC(5,1) NOT NULL, valid_until TIMESTAMP NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE battery_swap_stations (station_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, pad_id INTEGER REFERENCES landing_pads, cells_in_stock INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE maintenance_logs (log_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, drone_id INTEGER REFERENCES passenger_drones, cell_cycles INTEGER NOT NULL, logged_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE training_certifications (cert_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, pilot_id INTEGER REFERENCES pilot_supervisors, model_id INTEGER REFERENCES drone_models, expires_on DATE NOT NULL);

CREATE FUNCTION pad_readiness(db TEXT)
RETURNS TABLE (pad_name TEXT, cells_in_stock INTEGER, inbound_flights BIGINT) AS $$
    SELECT p.pad_name, b.cells_in_stock, count(f.flight_id)
    FROM landing_pads AS p
    JOIN battery_swap_stations AS b ON b.pad_id = p.pad_id
    JOIN flight_itineraries AS f ON f.arr_pad_id = p.pad_id
    JOIN passenger_drones AS d ON d.drone_id = f.drone_id
    JOIN fleets AS fl ON fl.fleet_id = d.fleet_id
    WHERE fl.db_name = db AND f.status = 'SCHEDULED'
    GROUP BY p.pad_name, b.cells_in_stock ORDER BY p.pad_name;
$$ LANGUAGE sql;

CREATE FUNCTION expiring_certs(db TEXT, horizon INTEGER)
RETURNS TABLE (pilot_name TEXT, model_name TEXT, expires_on DATE) AS $$
    SELECT DISTINCT s.pilot_name, mo.model_name, c.expires_on
    FROM training_certifications AS c
    JOIN pilot_supervisors AS s ON s.pilot_id = c.pilot_id
    JOIN drone_models AS mo ON mo.model_id = c.model_id
    JOIN passenger_drones AS d ON d.model_id = mo.model_id
    JOIN fleets AS fl ON fl.fleet_id = d.fleet_id
    WHERE fl.db_name = db
      AND c.expires_on BETWEEN CURRENT_DATE AND CURRENT_DATE + horizon
    ORDER BY c.expires_on;
$$ LANGUAGE sql;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION navigate(db TEXT, OUT manifest JSONB, OUT wind_risk JSONB,
                                    OUT cell_swaps JSONB, OUT cert_gaps JSONB) AS $$
BEGIN
    SELECT jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(q)) INTO manifest FROM (
        SELECT f.flight_id, p.pad_name AS departure_pad, d.registration, s.pilot_name
        FROM flight_itineraries AS f
        JOIN passenger_drones AS d ON d.drone_id = f.drone_id
        JOIN fleets AS fl ON fl.fleet_id = d.fleet_id
        JOIN landing_pads AS p ON p.pad_id = f.dep_pad_id
        JOIN pilot_supervisors AS s ON s.pilot_id = f.pilot_id
        WHERE fl.db_name = db AND f.flight_date = CURRENT_DATE ORDER BY f.flight_id) AS q;
    SELECT jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(q)) INTO wind_risk FROM (
        SELECT f.flight_id, p.pad_name AS arrival_pad, d.registration, w.wind_kph
        FROM weather_advisories AS w
        JOIN landing_pads AS p ON p.pad_id = w.pad_id
        JOIN flight_itineraries AS f ON f.arr_pad_id = p.pad_id
        JOIN passenger_drones AS d ON d.drone_id = f.drone_id
        JOIN fleets AS fl ON fl.fleet_id = d.fleet_id
        WHERE fl.db_name = db AND w.advisory_type = 'HIGH_WIND' AND w.valid_until > NOW() AND f.status = 'SCHEDULED' ORDER BY w.wind_kph DESC) AS q;
    SELECT jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(q)) INTO cell_swaps FROM (
        SELECT d.registration, b.station_id, b.cells_in_stock, m.cell_cycles, f.distance_km
        FROM battery_swap_stations AS b
        JOIN flight_itineraries AS f ON f.arr_pad_id = b.pad_id
        JOIN passenger_drones AS d ON d.drone_id = f.drone_id
        JOIN maintenance_logs AS m ON m.drone_id = d.drone_id
        JOIN fleets AS fl ON fl.fleet_id = d.fleet_id
        WHERE fl.db_name = db AND f.status = 'COMPLETED' AND f.distance_km >= 120 AND m.cell_cycles >= 400 ORDER BY m.cell_cycles DESC) AS q;
    SELECT jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(q)) INTO cert_gaps FROM (
        SELECT s.pilot_name, mo.model_name, d.registration,
               (SELECT max(c.expires_on) FROM training_certifications AS c
                 WHERE c.pilot_id = s.pilot_id AND c.model_id = mo.model_id) AS latest_expiry
        FROM pilot_supervisors AS s
        JOIN flight_itineraries AS f ON f.pilot_id = s.pilot_id
        JOIN passenger_drones AS d ON d.drone_id = f.drone_id
        JOIN drone_models AS mo ON mo.model_id = d.model_id
        JOIN fleets AS fl ON fl.fleet_id = d.fleet_id
        WHERE fl.db_name = db AND f.status = 'IN_FLIGHT'
          AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM training_certifications AS c
                           WHERE c.pilot_id = s.pilot_id AND c.model_id = mo.model_id
                             AND c.expires_on >= CURRENT_DATE)
        ORDER BY s.pilot_name) AS q;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

text_es: Implement a data extraction tool featuring the function compile(database) to analyze extreme sports metrics. The database holds tables for surfing beaches, athletes, kite models, surfboard designs, wind conditions, competition events, and corporate sponsors. The first query must link surfing beaches, competition events, and wind conditions to find locations with optimal gales during events. The second query connects athletes, corporate sponsors, kite models, and surfboard designs to match riders with their primary equipment providers. The third query associates competition events, athletes, kite models, and wind conditions to determine which equipment performs best in heavy storms. The fourth query combines surfing beaches, competition events, athletes, corporate sponsors, and surfboard designs to calculate the total sponsor investment per event location. Return a tuple of lists containing the rows from these four relational queries, providing a complete overview of the surfing circuit.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE beaches (beach_id INT PRIMARY KEY, beach_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL, country VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE sponsors (sponsor_id INT PRIMARY KEY, sponsor_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL, annual_budget DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE kites (kite_id INT PRIMARY KEY, kite_model VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL, size_m2 DECIMAL(4,1) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE boards (board_id INT PRIMARY KEY, board_model VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL, length_cm INT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE athletes (
    athlete_id   INT PRIMARY KEY,
    athlete_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    sponsor_id   INT REFERENCES sponsors(sponsor_id),
    kite_id      INT REFERENCES kites(kite_id),
    board_id     INT REFERENCES boards(board_id)
);
CREATE TABLE events (
    event_id    INT PRIMARY KEY,
    event_name  VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    beach_id    INT REFERENCES beaches(beach_id),
    prize_money DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE winds (wind_id INT PRIMARY KEY, event_id INT REFERENCES events(event_id), speed_knots DECIMAL(5,2) NOT NULL, gust_knots DECIMAL(5,2) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE results (
    event_id   INT REFERENCES events(event_id),
    athlete_id INT REFERENCES athletes(athlete_id),
    score      DECIMAL(6,2) NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (event_id, athlete_id)
);

CREATE VIEW event_entries AS
SELECT e.event_id, e.event_name, e.beach_id, e.prize_money, r.score,
       a.athlete_id, a.athlete_name, a.sponsor_id, a.kite_id, a.board_id
FROM events AS e
JOIN results AS r ON r.event_id = e.event_id
JOIN athletes AS a ON a.athlete_id = r.athlete_id;

CREATE VIEW rider_sponsors AS
SELECT a.athlete_id, a.athlete_name, a.kite_id, a.board_id,
       s.sponsor_id, s.sponsor_name, s.annual_budget
FROM athletes AS a
JOIN sponsors AS s ON s.sponsor_id = a.sponsor_id;

DELIMITER $$
CREATE PROCEDURE compile(IN `database` VARCHAR(64))
BEGIN
    IF `database` IS NULL OR `database` <> DATABASE() THEN
        SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000' SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'compile: requested database is not the active surfing circuit schema';
    END IF;

    SELECT b.beach_name, b.country, e.event_name, w.speed_knots, w.gust_knots
    FROM beaches AS b
    JOIN events AS e ON e.beach_id = b.beach_id
    JOIN winds AS w ON w.event_id = e.event_id
    WHERE w.speed_knots >= 25
    ORDER BY w.gust_knots DESC;

    SELECT rs.athlete_name, rs.sponsor_name, k.kite_model, k.size_m2, bd.board_model
    FROM rider_sponsors AS rs
    JOIN kites AS k ON k.kite_id = rs.kite_id
    JOIN boards AS bd ON bd.board_id = rs.board_id
    ORDER BY rs.sponsor_name, rs.athlete_name;

    SELECT k.kite_model, k.size_m2, AVG(ee.score) AS avg_storm_score, COUNT(*) AS runs
    FROM event_entries AS ee
    JOIN winds AS w ON w.event_id = ee.event_id
    JOIN kites AS k ON k.kite_id = ee.kite_id
    WHERE w.gust_knots >= 35
    GROUP BY k.kite_id, k.kite_model, k.size_m2
    ORDER BY avg_storm_score DESC;

    SELECT b.beach_name, ee.event_name,
           SUM(rs.annual_budget) AS sponsor_investment,
           COUNT(DISTINCT bd.board_id) AS board_designs
    FROM beaches AS b
    JOIN event_entries AS ee ON ee.beach_id = b.beach_id
    JOIN rider_sponsors AS rs ON rs.athlete_id = ee.athlete_id
    JOIN boards AS bd ON bd.board_id = rs.board_id
    GROUP BY b.beach_id, b.beach_name, ee.event_id, ee.event_name
    ORDER BY sponsor_investment DESC;
END$$
DELIMITER ;

CALL compile(DATABASE());

text_es: Write a database script containing a single function analyze(threshold) that returns three summarization lists for an independent podcast network. First, list the top performing programs by matching the programs to their current hosts, the individual broadcasts released this year, the advertising sponsors for those broadcasts, and the demographic profiles of the listeners, filtering for programs exceeding the provided threshold of total listeners. Second, calculate the total advertising revenue by connecting the promotional reads to their respective broadcasts, the sponsors who bought them, the financial contracts for those reads, and the programs they aired on. Finally, track regional audience distribution by linking the programs to listener demographics, listening platforms, and geographic regions. Example input: ten thousand. Example output: a list of top programs, a list of revenue totals, and a list of region counts.
text_alt:
CREATE TABLE programs (program_id int PRIMARY KEY, title text NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE hosts (host_id int PRIMARY KEY, host_name text NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE program_hosts (program_id int, host_id int, is_current boolean NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE episodes (episode_id int PRIMARY KEY, program_id int, release_date date NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE sponsors (sponsor_id int PRIMARY KEY, sponsor_name text NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE contracts (contract_id int PRIMARY KEY, sponsor_id int, rate_per_read numeric(10,2) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE ad_reads (read_id int PRIMARY KEY, episode_id int, sponsor_id int, contract_id int);
CREATE TABLE regions (region_id int PRIMARY KEY, region_name text NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE platforms (platform_id int PRIMARY KEY, platform_name text NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE listeners (listener_id int PRIMARY KEY, age_bracket text, region_id int, platform_id int);
CREATE TABLE plays (play_id int PRIMARY KEY, episode_id int, listener_id int);

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION program_age_profile(p_program_id integer) RETURNS jsonb AS $$
    SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_object_agg(age_bracket, listener_total), '{}'::jsonb)
      FROM (SELECT COALESCE(l.age_bracket, 'unknown') AS age_bracket,
                   COUNT(DISTINCT l.listener_id) AS listener_total
              FROM episodes AS e,
                   plays AS pl,
                   listeners AS l
             WHERE pl.episode_id = e.episode_id
               AND l.listener_id = pl.listener_id
               AND e.program_id = p_program_id
             GROUP BY 1) AS profile;
$$ LANGUAGE sql STABLE;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION network_listener_total() RETURNS bigint AS $$
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT pl.listener_id)
      FROM episodes AS e,
           plays AS pl
     WHERE pl.episode_id = e.episode_id
       AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM e.release_date) = EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CURRENT_DATE);
$$ LANGUAGE sql STABLE;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION mismatched_read_count() RETURNS bigint AS $$
    SELECT COUNT(*)
      FROM ad_reads AS ar,
           contracts AS c
     WHERE c.contract_id = ar.contract_id
       AND c.sponsor_id <> ar.sponsor_id;
$$ LANGUAGE sql STABLE;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "analyze"(threshold integer) RETURNS jsonb AS $$
DECLARE
    net bigint := network_listener_total();
    top_programs jsonb;
    revenue_totals jsonb;
    region_counts jsonb;
BEGIN
    SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('program', title, 'host', host_name,
                                        'listeners', listener_total, 'sponsors', sponsor_total,
                                        'share_pct', ROUND(100.0 * listener_total / NULLIF(net, 0), 2),
                                        'age_profile', program_age_profile(program_id))
                     ORDER BY listener_total DESC)
      INTO top_programs
      FROM (SELECT p.program_id, p.title, h.host_name,
                   COUNT(DISTINCT l.listener_id) AS listener_total,
                   COUNT(DISTINCT s.sponsor_id) AS sponsor_total
              FROM programs AS p,
                   program_hosts AS ph,
                   hosts AS h,
                   episodes AS e,
                   ad_reads AS ar,
                   sponsors AS s,
                   plays AS pl,
                   listeners AS l
             WHERE ph.program_id = p.program_id
               AND h.host_id = ph.host_id
               AND e.program_id = p.program_id
               AND ar.episode_id = e.episode_id
               AND s.sponsor_id = ar.sponsor_id
               AND pl.episode_id = e.episode_id
               AND l.listener_id = pl.listener_id
               AND ph.is_current
               AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM e.release_date) = EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CURRENT_DATE)
             GROUP BY p.program_id, p.title, h.host_name
            HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT l.listener_id) > threshold) AS ranked;

    SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('program', title, 'sponsor', sponsor_name,
                                        'reads', read_count, 'revenue', gross)
                     ORDER BY gross DESC)
      INTO revenue_totals
      FROM (SELECT p.title, s.sponsor_name,
                   COUNT(ar.read_id) AS read_count,
                   SUM(c.rate_per_read) AS gross
              FROM ad_reads AS ar,
                   episodes AS e,
                   sponsors AS s,
                   contracts AS c,
                   programs AS p
             WHERE e.episode_id = ar.episode_id
               AND s.sponsor_id = ar.sponsor_id
               AND c.contract_id = ar.contract_id AND c.sponsor_id = s.sponsor_id
               AND p.program_id = e.program_id
             GROUP BY p.program_id, p.title, s.sponsor_name) AS billed;

    SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('program', p.title, 'region', r.region_name,
                                        'platform', pf.platform_name,
                                        'listeners', COUNT(DISTINCT l.listener_id))
                     ORDER BY p.title, r.region_name, pf.platform_name)
      INTO region_counts
      FROM programs AS p,
           episodes AS e,
           plays AS pl,
           listeners AS l,
           platforms AS pf,
           regions AS r
     WHERE e.program_id = p.program_id
       AND pl.episode_id = e.episode_id
       AND l.listener_id = pl.listener_id
       AND pf.platform_id = l.platform_id
       AND r.region_id = l.region_id
     GROUP BY p.program_id, p.title, r.region_name, pf.platform_name;

    RETURN jsonb_build_object('top_programs', COALESCE(top_programs, '[]'::jsonb),
                              'revenue_totals', COALESCE(revenue_totals, '[]'::jsonb),
                              'region_counts', COALESCE(region_counts, '[]'::jsonb),
                              'unbilled_reads', mismatched_read_count());
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

SELECT "analyze"(10000) AS network_summary;

text_es: Draft a set of database queries wrapped in the function inspect(decade) to generate three progress reports for architectural preservation. Detail the stonework progress by linking the master stonemasons to their assigned scaffolding zones, the specific architectural sculptures they restored, the original historical blueprints, and the material suppliers who provided the new stone during the specified decade. Next, summarize the project finances by connecting the scaffolding zones to the structural inspection reports, the conservation grants awarded, the philanthropic donors, and the expense ledgers. Lastly, monitor the stained glass preservation by matching the sculptures and windows to the glass artisans, the protective glazing installations, and the weather monitoring sensors. text_nat:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION grant_spend(d1 DATE, d2 DATE)
RETURNS TABLE (grant_id INTEGER, report_id INTEGER, grant_title TEXT,
               donor_name TEXT, awarded NUMERIC, spent NUMERIC)
AS $$
    SELECT g.grant_id, g.report_id, g.grant_title, d.donor_name, g.amount_awarded,
           (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(e.amount_spent), 0)
            FROM expense_ledgers AS e
            WHERE e.grant_id = g.grant_id)
    FROM conservation_grants AS g
    JOIN donors AS d ON d.donor_id = g.donor_id
    WHERE g.awarded_on >= d1
      AND g.awarded_on < d2;
$$ LANGUAGE sql STABLE;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION sensor_climate(d1 DATE, d2 DATE)
RETURNS TABLE (zone_id INTEGER, sensor_code TEXT, mean_humidity NUMERIC)
AS $$
    SELECT z.zone_id, ws.sensor_code, AVG(sr.humidity)
    FROM weather_sensors AS ws
    JOIN scaffold_zones AS z ON z.zone_id = ws.zone_id
    JOIN sensor_readings AS sr ON sr.sensor_id = ws.sensor_id
    WHERE sr.recorded_on >= d1
      AND sr.recorded_on < d2
    GROUP BY z.zone_id, ws.sensor_code;
$$ LANGUAGE sql STABLE;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION mason_stonework(d1 DATE, d2 DATE)
RETURNS TABLE (mason_name TEXT, zone_name TEXT, sculpture_name TEXT,
               archive_ref TEXT, supplier_name TEXT,
               stone_volume_m3 NUMERIC, restoration_count BIGINT)
AS $$
    SELECT m.mason_name, z.zone_name, s.sculpture_name, b.archive_ref,
           sup.supplier_name, SUM(r.stone_volume), COUNT(*)
    FROM restorations AS r
    JOIN stonemasons AS m ON m.mason_id = r.mason_id
    JOIN scaffold_zones AS z ON z.zone_id = m.zone_id
    JOIN sculptures AS s ON s.sculpture_id = r.sculpture_id
    JOIN blueprints AS b ON b.blueprint_id = s.blueprint_id
    JOIN suppliers AS sup ON sup.supplier_id = r.supplier_id
    WHERE r.restored_on >= d1
      AND r.restored_on < d2
    GROUP BY m.mason_name, z.zone_name, s.sculpture_name, b.archive_ref, sup.supplier_name
    ORDER BY m.mason_name, s.sculpture_name;
$$ LANGUAGE sql STABLE;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION zone_finances(d1 DATE, d2 DATE)
RETURNS TABLE (zone_name TEXT, structural_rating TEXT, donor_name TEXT,
               grant_title TEXT, awarded NUMERIC, spent NUMERIC, balance NUMERIC)
AS $$
    SELECT z.zone_name, i.structural_rating, gs.donor_name, gs.grant_title,
           gs.awarded, gs.spent, gs.awarded - gs.spent
    FROM grant_spend(d1, d2) AS gs
    JOIN inspection_reports AS i ON i.report_id = gs.report_id
    JOIN scaffold_zones AS z ON z.zone_id = i.zone_id
    ORDER BY gs.awarded - gs.spent ASC;
$$ LANGUAGE sql STABLE;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION glass_status(d1 DATE, d2 DATE)
RETURNS TABLE (sculpture_name TEXT, window_name TEXT, artisan_name TEXT,
               glazing_type TEXT, installed_on DATE,
               sensor_code TEXT, mean_humidity NUMERIC)
AS $$
    SELECT s.sculpture_name, w.window_name, a.artisan_name, gi.glazing_type,
           gi.installed_on, sc.sensor_code, sc.mean_humidity
    FROM windows AS w
    JOIN sculptures AS s ON s.sculpture_id = w.sculpture_id
    JOIN glass_artisans AS a ON a.artisan_id = w.artisan_id
    JOIN glazing_installations AS gi ON gi.window_id = w.window_id
    JOIN sensor_climate(d1, d2) AS sc ON sc.zone_id = s.zone_id
    WHERE gi.installed_on >= d1
      AND gi.installed_on < d2
    ORDER BY sc.mean_humidity DESC, w.window_name;
$$ LANGUAGE sql STABLE;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION inspect(decade INTEGER,
                                   OUT stonework REFCURSOR,
                                   OUT finances REFCURSOR,
                                   OUT glass REFCURSOR)
AS $$
DECLARE
    d1 DATE := make_date(decade, 1, 1);
    d2 DATE := make_date(decade + 10, 1, 1);
BEGIN
    IF decade % 10 <> 0 THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'inspect() expects the first year of a decade, got %', decade;
    END IF;

    stonework := 'stonework_cur';
    OPEN stonework FOR SELECT * FROM mason_stonework(d1, d2);

    finances := 'finances_cur';
    OPEN finances FOR SELECT * FROM zone_finances(d1, d2);

    glass := 'glass_cur';
    OPEN glass FOR SELECT * FROM glass_status(d1, d2);
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

BEGIN;
SELECT inspect(1990);
FETCH ALL FROM stonework_cur;
FETCH ALL FROM finances_cur;
FETCH ALL FROM glass_cur;
COMMIT;

text_es: Create a tournament management script using the entry function compile(level) to return three result summaries for a competitive educational organization. First, identify the top spellers by associating the individual contestants with their sponsoring schools, the vocabulary words they attempted, the judges who scored them, and the specific tournament rounds they advanced through at the given competition level. Second, analyze word difficulty by connecting the vocabulary words to their linguistic origin dictionaries, the pronunciation audio files, the contestants who misspelled them, and the districts those contestants represent. Third, summarize school performance by linking the sponsoring schools to their district coordinators, the regional trophies won, and the transportation buses chartered for the event. Example input: state championship. Example output: lists of top contestants, word difficulty rankings, and school achievements.

CREATE TABLE Coordinators (coordinator_id INT PRIMARY KEY, full_name VARCHAR(80));
CREATE TABLE Districts (district_id INT PRIMARY KEY, district_name VARCHAR(80), coordinator_id INT);
CREATE TABLE Schools (school_id INT PRIMARY KEY, school_name VARCHAR(80), district_id INT);
CREATE TABLE Contestants (contestant_id INT PRIMARY KEY, contestant_name VARCHAR(80), grade INT, school_id INT);
CREATE TABLE OriginDictionaries (origin_id INT PRIMARY KEY, language VARCHAR(40), dictionary_name VARCHAR(80));
CREATE TABLE Words (word_id INT PRIMARY KEY, spelling VARCHAR(60), origin_id INT, difficulty_tier INT);
CREATE TABLE Pronunciations (pron_id INT PRIMARY KEY, word_id INT, audio_file VARCHAR(120), duration_ms INT);
CREATE TABLE Judges (judge_id INT PRIMARY KEY, judge_name VARCHAR(80), certification VARCHAR(40));
CREATE TABLE Rounds (round_id INT PRIMARY KEY, round_number INT, competition_level VARCHAR(60));
CREATE TABLE Attempts (attempt_id INT PRIMARY KEY, contestant_id INT, word_id INT, round_id INT,
                       judge_id INT, spelled_correctly TINYINT, points DECIMAL(5,2));
CREATE TABLE Trophies (trophy_id INT PRIMARY KEY, school_id INT, title VARCHAR(80), region VARCHAR(60));
CREATE TABLE Buses (bus_id INT PRIMARY KEY, school_id INT, charter_code VARCHAR(30), seat_count INT);

CREATE VIEW ScoredAttempts AS
SELECT A.attempt_id, A.word_id, A.judge_id, A.points, A.spelled_correctly,
       R.round_number, R.competition_level,
       C.contestant_id, C.contestant_name, S.school_id, S.school_name, D.district_id, D.district_name
FROM Attempts AS A
JOIN Rounds AS R ON R.round_id = A.round_id
JOIN Contestants AS C ON C.contestant_id = A.contestant_id
JOIN Schools AS S ON S.school_id = C.school_id
JOIN Districts AS D ON D.district_id = S.district_id;

CREATE VIEW WordProfiles AS
SELECT W.word_id, W.spelling, W.difficulty_tier, O.language, O.dictionary_name, P.audio_file, P.duration_ms
FROM Words AS W
JOIN OriginDictionaries AS O ON O.origin_id = W.origin_id
JOIN Pronunciations AS P ON P.word_id = W.word_id;

CREATE VIEW SchoolSupport AS
SELECT S.school_id, S.school_name, D.district_name, K.full_name AS coordinator
FROM Schools AS S
JOIN Districts AS D ON D.district_id = S.district_id
JOIN Coordinators AS K ON K.coordinator_id = D.coordinator_id;

DELIMITER //

CREATE PROCEDURE compile(IN level VARCHAR(60))
BEGIN
    SELECT SA.contestant_name,
           SA.school_name,
           MAX(SA.round_number) AS furthest_round,
           COUNT(DISTINCT W.word_id) AS words_attempted,
           COUNT(DISTINCT J.judge_id) AS judges_scoring,
           SUM(SA.points) AS total_points
    FROM ScoredAttempts AS SA
    JOIN Words AS W ON W.word_id = SA.word_id
    JOIN Judges AS J ON J.judge_id = SA.judge_id
    WHERE SA.competition_level = level
    GROUP BY SA.contestant_id, SA.contestant_name, SA.school_name
    ORDER BY total_points DESC, furthest_round DESC
    LIMIT 10;

    SELECT WP.spelling, WP.difficulty_tier, WP.language, WP.dictionary_name, WP.audio_file,
           COUNT(DISTINCT SA.contestant_id) AS spellers_missing_it,
           COUNT(DISTINCT SA.district_id) AS districts_affected
    FROM WordProfiles AS WP
    JOIN ScoredAttempts AS SA ON SA.word_id = WP.word_id
    WHERE SA.spelled_correctly = 0
      AND SA.competition_level = level
    GROUP BY WP.word_id, WP.spelling, WP.difficulty_tier, WP.language, WP.dictionary_name, WP.audio_file
    ORDER BY spellers_missing_it DESC, WP.difficulty_tier DESC;

    SELECT SS.school_name, SS.district_name, SS.coordinator,
           (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Trophies AS T WHERE T.school_id = SS.school_id) AS trophies_won,
           (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Buses AS B WHERE B.school_id = SS.school_id) AS buses_chartered,
           (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(B.seat_count), 0) FROM Buses AS B WHERE B.school_id = SS.school_id) AS seats_reserved
    FROM SchoolSupport AS SS
    JOIN ScoredAttempts AS SA ON SA.school_id = SS.school_id
    WHERE SA.competition_level = level
    GROUP BY SS.school_id, SS.school_name, SS.district_name, SS.coordinator
    ORDER BY trophies_won DESC, SS.school_name;
END //

DELIMITER ;

CALL compile('state championship');

text_es: Provide a production tracking script with the function trace(status) to generate three manufacturing reports for a luxury footwear atelier. Detail the client order progress by associating the wealthy clients with their specific foot molds, the master cobblers assigned to them, the premium leather suppliers, and the distinct assembly stages, filtering for orders matching the provided status. Evaluate quality control by connecting the assembly stages to the final quality checks, the rejected material batches, the senior inspectors, and the client return shipping logs. Monitor material sourcing by linking the premium leather suppliers to the exotic animal import permits, the tannery inspection reports, and the international shipping couriers. Example input: awaiting assembly. Example output: lists of order timelines, quality rejection rates, and material shipping delays.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE clients (client_id INT PRIMARY KEY, full_name VARCHAR(80), city VARCHAR(40));
CREATE TABLE foot_molds (mold_id INT PRIMARY KEY, client_id INT, last_shape VARCHAR(40), carved_on DATE);
CREATE TABLE cobblers (cobbler_id INT PRIMARY KEY, master_name VARCHAR(80), bench_no INT);
CREATE TABLE suppliers (supplier_id INT PRIMARY KEY, house_name VARCHAR(80), country VARCHAR(40));
CREATE TABLE orders (order_id INT PRIMARY KEY, client_id INT, mold_id INT, cobbler_id INT, supplier_id INT, status VARCHAR(30), placed_on DATE, due_on DATE);
CREATE TABLE assembly_stages (stage_id INT PRIMARY KEY, order_id INT, stage_name VARCHAR(40), started_on DATE, finished_on DATE);
CREATE TABLE inspectors (inspector_id INT PRIMARY KEY, inspector_name VARCHAR(80), seniority VARCHAR(20));
CREATE TABLE quality_checks (check_id INT PRIMARY KEY, stage_id INT, inspector_id INT, verdict VARCHAR(20), checked_on DATE);
CREATE TABLE rejected_batches (batch_id INT PRIMARY KEY, check_id INT, supplier_id INT, hide_grade VARCHAR(20), rejected_on DATE);
CREATE TABLE couriers (courier_id INT PRIMARY KEY, courier_name VARCHAR(80), service_level VARCHAR(20));
CREATE TABLE return_shipments (return_id INT PRIMARY KEY, order_id INT, courier_id INT, shipped_on DATE, received_on DATE);
CREATE TABLE import_permits (permit_id INT PRIMARY KEY, supplier_id INT, species VARCHAR(40), valid_until DATE);
CREATE TABLE tannery_reports (report_id INT PRIMARY KEY, supplier_id INT, hygiene_score INT, inspected_on DATE);
CREATE TABLE material_shipments (shipment_id INT PRIMARY KEY, supplier_id INT, courier_id INT, permit_id INT, dispatched_on DATE, promised_on DATE, arrived_on DATE);

DELIMITER $$

CREATE PROCEDURE order_progress(IN p_status VARCHAR(30))
BEGIN
  SELECT o.order_id, c.full_name AS client, fm.last_shape AS mold,
         mc.master_name AS cobbler, s.house_name AS leather_house,
         GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT st.stage_name ORDER BY st.started_on) AS stage_path,
         MIN(st.started_on) AS work_began,
         DATEDIFF(o.due_on, COALESCE(MAX(st.finished_on), CURRENT_DATE)) AS days_of_slack
  FROM orders AS o
  JOIN clients AS c ON c.client_id = o.client_id
  JOIN foot_molds AS fm ON fm.mold_id = o.mold_id
  JOIN cobblers AS mc ON mc.cobbler_id = o.cobbler_id
  JOIN suppliers AS s ON s.supplier_id = o.supplier_id
  JOIN assembly_stages AS st ON st.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE o.status = p_status
  GROUP BY o.order_id, c.full_name, fm.last_shape, mc.master_name, s.house_name, o.due_on
  ORDER BY days_of_slack;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE stage_timeline(IN p_status VARCHAR(30))
BEGIN
  SELECT o.order_id, c.full_name AS client, st.stage_name, st.started_on,
         DATEDIFF(COALESCE(st.finished_on, CURRENT_DATE), st.started_on) AS days_in_stage
  FROM assembly_stages AS st
  JOIN orders AS o ON o.order_id = st.order_id
  JOIN clients AS c ON c.client_id = o.client_id
  WHERE o.status = p_status
  ORDER BY o.order_id, st.started_on;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE quality_control(IN p_status VARCHAR(30))
BEGIN
  SELECT st.stage_name, i.inspector_name, i.seniority,
         COUNT(qc.check_id) AS checks_made,
         SUM(CASE WHEN qc.verdict = 'rejected' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failed_checks,
         ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN qc.verdict = 'rejected' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
               / COUNT(qc.check_id), 1) AS rejection_rate_pct
  FROM assembly_stages AS st
  JOIN quality_checks AS qc ON qc.stage_id = st.stage_id
  JOIN inspectors AS i ON i.inspector_id = qc.inspector_id
  JOIN orders AS o ON o.order_id = st.order_id
  WHERE o.status = p_status AND i.seniority = 'senior'
  GROUP BY st.stage_name, i.inspector_name, i.seniority
  ORDER BY rejection_rate_pct DESC;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE scrapped_material(IN p_status VARCHAR(30))
BEGIN
  SELECT st.stage_name, i.inspector_name, s.house_name AS leather_house,
         rb.hide_grade, rb.rejected_on
  FROM rejected_batches AS rb
  JOIN quality_checks AS qc ON qc.check_id = rb.check_id
  JOIN assembly_stages AS st ON st.stage_id = qc.stage_id
  JOIN inspectors AS i ON i.inspector_id = qc.inspector_id
  JOIN suppliers AS s ON s.supplier_id = rb.supplier_id
  JOIN orders AS o ON o.order_id = st.order_id
  WHERE o.status = p_status
  ORDER BY rb.rejected_on DESC;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE return_log(IN p_status VARCHAR(30))
BEGIN
  SELECT rs.return_id, o.order_id, c.full_name AS client, cr.courier_name, cr.service_level,
         rs.shipped_on, DATEDIFF(rs.received_on, rs.shipped_on) AS transit_days
  FROM return_shipments AS rs
  JOIN orders AS o ON o.order_id = rs.order_id
  JOIN clients AS c ON c.client_id = o.client_id
  JOIN couriers AS cr ON cr.courier_id = rs.courier_id
  WHERE o.status = p_status
  ORDER BY transit_days DESC;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE sourcing_compliance()
BEGIN
  SELECT s.house_name, s.country, ip.species, ip.valid_until,
         tr.hygiene_score, tr.inspected_on
  FROM suppliers AS s
  JOIN import_permits AS ip ON ip.supplier_id = s.supplier_id
  JOIN tannery_reports AS tr ON tr.supplier_id = s.supplier_id
  WHERE ip.valid_until < CURRENT_DATE OR tr.hygiene_score < 70
  ORDER BY ip.valid_until, tr.hygiene_score;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE material_shipping_delays()
BEGIN
  SELECT s.house_name, ip.species, cr.courier_name, cr.service_level,
         ms.dispatched_on, ms.promised_on, ms.arrived_on,
         DATEDIFF(COALESCE(ms.arrived_on, CURRENT_DATE), ms.promised_on) AS delay_days
  FROM material_shipments AS ms
  JOIN suppliers AS s ON s.supplier_id = ms.supplier_id
  JOIN import_permits AS ip ON ip.permit_id = ms.permit_id
  JOIN couriers AS cr ON cr.courier_id = ms.courier_id
  WHERE COALESCE(ms.arrived_on, CURRENT_DATE) > ms.promised_on
  ORDER BY delay_days DESC, s.house_name;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE trace(IN p_status VARCHAR(30))
BEGIN
  CALL order_progress(p_status);
  CALL stage_timeline(p_status);
  CALL quality_control(p_status);
  CALL scrapped_material(p_status);
  CALL return_log(p_status);
  CALL sourcing_compliance();
  CALL material_shipping_delays();
END$$

DELIMITER ;

CALL trace('awaiting assembly');

END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE sourcing_compliance()
BEGIN
  SELECT s.house_name, s.country, ip.species, ip.valid_until,
         tr.hygiene_score, tr.inspected_on
  FROM suppliers AS s, import_permits AS ip, tannery_reports AS tr
  WHERE ip.supplier_id = s.supplier_id
  AND tr.supplier_id = s.supplier_id
  AND (ip.valid_until < CURRENT_DATE OR tr.hygiene_score < 70)
  ORDER BY ip.valid_until, tr.hygiene_score;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE material_shipping_delays()
BEGIN
  SELECT s.house_name, ip.species, cr.courier_name, cr.service_level,
         ms.dispatched_on, ms.promised_on, ms.arrived_on,
         DATEDIFF(COALESCE(ms.arrived_on, CURRENT_DATE), ms.promised_on) AS delay_days
  FROM material_shipments AS ms, suppliers AS s, import_permits AS ip, couriers AS cr
  WHERE s.supplier_id = ms.supplier_id
  AND ip.permit_id = ms.permit_id
  AND cr.courier_id = ms.courier_id
  AND COALESCE(ms.arrived_on, CURRENT_DATE) > ms.promised_on
  ORDER BY delay_days DESC, s.house_name;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE trace(IN p_status VARCHAR(30))
BEGIN
  CALL order_progress(p_status);
  CALL stage_timeline(p_status);
  CALL quality_control(p_status);
  CALL scrapped_material(p_status);
  CALL return_log(p_status);
  CALL sourcing_compliance();
  CALL material_shipping_delays();
END$$
