text_es: Write a social services tracking script anchored by the function monitor(region) to generate three operational summaries for a child welfare agency. Map the current placements by associating the foster children with their approved foster families, their assigned social workers, their mandatory monthly case visits, and their upcoming family court dates in the provided region. Ensure medical compliance by connecting the foster children to their historical medical records, the regional pediatric clinics, the prescribed medication logs, and the specialized trauma counselors. Evaluate foster family retention by linking the approved foster families to their initial background check clearances, the required training seminars they attended, and the support group facilitators. Example input: southern district. Example output: lists of placement statuses, medical compliance alerts, and family retention metrics.
text_nat:
-- Social services tracking module for a child welfare agency: schema, the
-- summary views behind monitor(region), and a driver for one region.
CREATE TABLE Regions (region_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE FosterFamilies (family_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, family_name TEXT NOT NULL, region_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES Regions(region_id), approved_on DATE NOT NULL, license_status TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE SocialWorkers (worker_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, worker_name TEXT NOT NULL, region_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES Regions(region_id), caseload_cap INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE FosterChildren (child_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, child_name TEXT NOT NULL, date_of_birth DATE NOT NULL, family_id INTEGER REFERENCES FosterFamilies(family_id), worker_id INTEGER REFERENCES SocialWorkers(worker_id), placement_start DATE NOT NULL, placement_state TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE CaseVisits (visit_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, child_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES FosterChildren(child_id), visit_date DATE NOT NULL, visit_outcome TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE CourtDates (hearing_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, child_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES FosterChildren(child_id), hearing_date DATE NOT NULL, hearing_type TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE PediatricClinics (clinic_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, clinic_name TEXT NOT NULL, region_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES Regions(region_id));
CREATE TABLE MedicalRecords (record_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, child_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES FosterChildren(child_id), clinic_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES PediatricClinics(clinic_id), exam_date DATE NOT NULL, immunizations_current INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE MedicationLogs (log_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, record_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES MedicalRecords(record_id), medication TEXT NOT NULL, refill_due DATE, adherence_pct INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE TraumaCounselors (counselor_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, counselor_name TEXT NOT NULL, specialty TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE CounselingAssignments (child_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES FosterChildren(child_id), counselor_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES TraumaCounselors(counselor_id), sessions_held INTEGER NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (child_id, counselor_id));
CREATE TABLE BackgroundChecks (check_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, family_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES FosterFamilies(family_id), cleared_on DATE, clearance_level TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE TrainingSeminars (seminar_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, seminar_title TEXT NOT NULL, required_hours INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE SeminarAttendance (family_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES FosterFamilies(family_id), seminar_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES TrainingSeminars(seminar_id), attended_on DATE NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (family_id, seminar_id));
CREATE TABLE SupportGroups (group_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, facilitator TEXT NOT NULL, family_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES FosterFamilies(family_id), meetings_hosted INTEGER NOT NULL);
-- Each child resolved to its approved family, region and assigned worker.
CREATE VIEW ChildPlacement AS
SELECT R.region_name, C.child_id, C.child_name, C.placement_state,
       F.family_name, F.license_status, W.worker_name
FROM FosterChildren AS C
JOIN FosterFamilies AS F ON C.family_id = F.family_id
JOIN Regions AS R ON F.region_id = R.region_id
JOIN SocialWorkers AS W ON C.worker_id = W.worker_id;
-- Medication logs hang off medical records, so roll them up per child.
CREATE VIEW MedicationAdherence AS
SELECT M.child_id, MIN(L.adherence_pct) AS worst_adherence,
       MIN(L.refill_due) AS earliest_refill_due
FROM MedicationLogs AS L
JOIN MedicalRecords AS M ON L.record_id = M.record_id
GROUP BY M.child_id;
CREATE VIEW CounselingLoad AS
SELECT A.child_id, CO.counselor_name, CO.specialty, SUM(A.sessions_held) AS sessions_held
FROM CounselingAssignments AS A
JOIN TraumaCounselors AS CO ON A.counselor_id = CO.counselor_id
GROUP BY A.child_id, CO.counselor_name, CO.specialty;
CREATE VIEW TrainingProgress AS
SELECT SA.family_id, COUNT(*) AS seminars_attended, SUM(T.required_hours) AS training_hours
FROM SeminarAttendance AS SA
JOIN TrainingSeminars AS T ON SA.seminar_id = T.seminar_id
GROUP BY SA.family_id;
-- Summary 1: placement map with visit history and the next court date.
CREATE VIEW PlacementStatus AS
SELECT P.region_name, P.child_id, P.child_name, P.family_name, P.license_status,
       P.worker_name, P.placement_state,
       (SELECT MAX(V.visit_date) FROM CaseVisits AS V WHERE V.child_id = P.child_id) AS last_visit,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM CaseVisits AS V WHERE V.child_id = P.child_id) AS visits_logged,
       (SELECT MIN(H.hearing_date) FROM CourtDates AS H WHERE H.child_id = P.child_id
          AND H.hearing_date >= DATE('now')) AS next_hearing
FROM ChildPlacement AS P;
-- Summary 2: medical compliance, keyed on the clinic's region.
CREATE VIEW MedicalCompliance AS
SELECT R.region_name, C.child_id, C.child_name, CL.clinic_name,
       MAX(M.exam_date) AS latest_exam,
       MIN(M.immunizations_current) AS immunizations_current,
       (SELECT MA.worst_adherence FROM MedicationAdherence AS MA
          WHERE MA.child_id = C.child_id) AS worst_adherence,
       (SELECT MA.earliest_refill_due FROM MedicationAdherence AS MA
          WHERE MA.child_id = C.child_id) AS earliest_refill_due,
       (SELECT CO.counselor_name FROM CounselingLoad AS CO WHERE CO.child_id = C.child_id
          ORDER BY CO.sessions_held DESC LIMIT 1) AS counselor_name,
       (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(CO.sessions_held), 0) FROM CounselingLoad AS CO
          WHERE CO.child_id = C.child_id) AS sessions_held
FROM FosterChildren AS C
JOIN MedicalRecords AS M ON M.child_id = C.child_id
JOIN PediatricClinics AS CL ON M.clinic_id = CL.clinic_id
JOIN Regions AS R ON CL.region_id = R.region_id
GROUP BY R.region_name, C.child_id, C.child_name, CL.clinic_name;
-- Summary 3: retention metrics per approved foster family.
CREATE VIEW FamilyRetention AS
SELECT R.region_name, F.family_id, F.family_name, F.approved_on,
       (SELECT B.clearance_level FROM BackgroundChecks AS B WHERE B.family_id = F.family_id
          ORDER BY B.cleared_on LIMIT 1) AS clearance_level,
       (SELECT MIN(B.cleared_on) FROM BackgroundChecks AS B
          WHERE B.family_id = F.family_id) AS cleared_on,
       (SELECT COALESCE(TP.seminars_attended, 0) FROM TrainingProgress AS TP
          WHERE TP.family_id = F.family_id) AS seminars_attended,
       (SELECT COALESCE(TP.training_hours, 0) FROM TrainingProgress AS TP
          WHERE TP.family_id = F.family_id) AS training_hours,
       (SELECT G.facilitator FROM SupportGroups AS G WHERE G.family_id = F.family_id
          ORDER BY G.meetings_hosted DESC LIMIT 1) AS facilitator,
       (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(G.meetings_hosted), 0) FROM SupportGroups AS G
          WHERE G.family_id = F.family_id) AS support_meetings
FROM FosterFamilies AS F
JOIN Regions AS R ON F.region_id = R.region_id;
-- monitor('southern district'): the three operational summaries.
SELECT * FROM PlacementStatus WHERE region_name = 'southern district'
ORDER BY next_hearing, child_name;
SELECT * FROM MedicalCompliance WHERE region_name = 'southern district'
  AND (immunizations_current = 0 OR worst_adherence < 85 OR sessions_held = 0)
ORDER BY earliest_refill_due, child_name;
SELECT * FROM FamilyRetention WHERE region_name = 'southern district'
ORDER BY training_hours DESC, family_name;

Schema: Users (user_id INT, username VARCHAR, join_date DATE), Posts (post_id INT, user_id INT, title VARCHAR, content TEXT, post_date DATETIME).

Queries:
1. Select all posts and their authors.
2. Find all posts by a specific user (e.g., username = 'TechGeek').
3. Count the number of posts made by each user.
4. Create a new forum post.
5. Update the content of a post.

SELECT
  P.post_id,
  P.title,
  P.content,
  P.post_date,
  U.username
FROM Posts AS P
JOIN Users AS U
  ON P.user_id = U.user_id;

  P.content,
  P.post_date,
  U.username

SELECT

Schema: Teams (team_id INT, team_name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR), Players (player_id INT, first_name VARCHAR, last_name VARCHAR, team_id INT, position VARCHAR, jersey_number INT).

Queries:
1. List all players and their teams.
2. Find all players on a specific team (e.g., 'Lakers').
3. Count the number of players per position.
4. Add a new player to a team.
5. Update a player's position.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Teams (
    team_id   INT PRIMARY KEY,
    team_name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    city      VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE Players (
    player_id     INT PRIMARY KEY,
    first_name    VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    last_name     VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    team_id       INT REFERENCES Teams(team_id),
    position      VARCHAR(20),
    jersey_number INT
);

INSERT INTO Teams (team_id, team_name, city) VALUES
    (1, 'Lakers', 'Los Angeles'),
    (2, 'Celtics', 'Boston'),
    (3, 'Bulls', 'Chicago');

INSERT INTO Players (player_id, first_name, last_name, team_id, position, jersey_number) VALUES
    (10, 'Alan', 'Reyes', 1, 'Guard', 3),
    (11, 'Bruno', 'Kessler', 1, 'Center', 14),
    (12, 'Caleb', 'Ortiz', 1, 'Forward', 23),
    (13, 'Dmitri', 'Volkov', 2, 'Guard', 7),
    (14, 'Elias', 'Park', 2, 'Forward', 21),
    (15, 'Farid', 'Nasser', 3, 'Center', 33);

-- 1. All players with the team and city they play for.
CREATE VIEW v_player_roster AS
SELECT p.player_id, p.first_name || ' ' || p.last_name AS player_name,
       p.position, p.jersey_number, t.team_name, t.city
FROM Players p
INNER JOIN Teams t ON t.team_id = p.team_id;

SELECT player_name, position, jersey_number, team_name, city
FROM v_player_roster ORDER BY team_name, jersey_number;

-- 2. Players on a specific team, selected by team name.
SELECT p.jersey_number, p.first_name, p.last_name, p.position
FROM Players p
INNER JOIN Teams t ON t.team_id = p.team_id
WHERE t.team_name = 'Lakers' ORDER BY p.jersey_number;

-- 3. Number of players per position, then the same breakdown per team.
SELECT position, COUNT(*) AS player_count
FROM Players GROUP BY position ORDER BY player_count DESC, position;

SELECT t.team_name, p.position, COUNT(*) AS player_count
FROM Teams t
INNER JOIN Players p ON p.team_id = t.team_id
GROUP BY t.team_name, p.position ORDER BY t.team_name, p.position;

-- Teammates of a given player.
SELECT mate.jersey_number, mate.first_name, mate.last_name, mate.position
FROM Players me
INNER JOIN Players mate ON mate.team_id = me.team_id AND mate.player_id <> me.player_id
WHERE me.last_name = 'Reyes' ORDER BY mate.jersey_number;

-- 4. Add a new player, resolving the team by name instead of hard-coding the id.

-- 5. Update a player's position and read the result back.

FROM Players p
INNER JOIN Teams t ON t.team_id = p.team_id
WHERE p.player_id = 10;

-- Jersey numbers must be unique inside a team; list any collisions.
SELECT t.team_name, a.jersey_number, a.last_name AS player_a, b.last_name AS player_b
FROM Players a
INNER JOIN Players b ON b.team_id = a.team_id AND b.jersey_number = a.jersey_number
INNER JOIN Teams t ON t.team_id = a.team_id
WHERE a.player_id < b.player_id ORDER BY t.team_name, a.jersey_number;

-- Squad report: roster size and captain (lowest jersey number) per team.
SELECT t.city || ' ' || t.team_name AS squad, COUNT(p.player_id) AS squad_size,
       MIN(p.jersey_number) AS captain_number
FROM Teams t
INNER JOIN Players p ON p.team_id = t.team_id
GROUP BY t.city, t.team_name ORDER BY squad_size DESC, squad;

Schema: Documents (doc_id INT, title VARCHAR, content TEXT, created_at DATETIME, author_id INT), Authors (author_id INT, name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR).
Queries:
1. Select all documents created by a specific author.
2. Find the total number of documents for each author.
3. Insert a new document.
4. Update the content of an existing document.
5. Select the 5 most recent documents.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Authors (
    author_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    email VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Documents (
    doc_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    title VARCHAR(255),
    content TEXT,
    created_at DATETIME,
    author_id INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (author_id) REFERENCES Authors(author_id)
);

-- Insert sample data
INSERT INTO Authors (author_id, name, email) VALUES
(1, 'Alice Smith', 'alice@example.com'),
(2, 'Bob Johnson', 'bob@example.com');

INSERT INTO Documents (doc_id, title, content, created_at, author_id) VALUES
(101, 'My First Post', 'This is the content of my first post.', '2023-01-01 10:00:00', 1),
(102, 'Database Design', 'Details about database design.', '2023-01-02 11:00:00', 2),
(103, 'SQL Joins', 'Understanding different types of SQL joins.', '2023-01-03 12:00:00', 1),
(104, 'New Tech Trends', 'Exploring the latest tech trends.', '2023-01-04 13:00:00', 2),
(105, 'Advanced SQL', 'Advanced SQL concepts and queries.', '2023-01-05 14:00:00', 1);

-- 1. Select all documents created by a specific author (e.g., 'Alice Smith')
SELECT D.title, D.content
FROM Documents AS D
JOIN Authors AS A ON D.author_id = A.author_id
WHERE A.name = 'Alice Smith';

-- 2. Find the total number of documents for each author.
SELECT A.name, COUNT(D.doc_id) AS total_documents
FROM Authors AS A
JOIN Documents AS D ON A.author_id = D.author_id
GROUP BY A.name;

-- 3. Insert a new document
INSERT INTO Documents (doc_id, title, content, created_at, author_id)
VALUES (106, 'Another Document', 'Content for another document.', '2023-01-06 15:00:00', 2);

-- 4. Update the content of an existing document
UPDATE Documents
SET content = 'Updated content for My First Post.'
WHERE doc_id = 101;

-- 5. Select the 5 most recent documents.
SELECT doc_id, title, created_at
FROM Documents
ORDER BY created_at DESC
LIMIT 5;

-- SEPARATE QUERIES WITH EXACTLY ONE JOIN

-- Select document titles and author emails
SELECT D.title, A.email
FROM Documents AS D
JOIN Authors AS A ON D.author_id = A.author_id;

-- Get author names and their document titles, even if no documents
SELECT A.name, D.title
FROM Authors AS A
LEFT JOIN Documents AS D ON A.author_id = D.author_id;

-- Get documents and author names for specific document ID
SELECT D.title, A.name
FROM Documents AS D
JOIN Authors AS A ON D.author_id = A.author_id
WHERE D.doc_id = 103;

-- List all authors and the count of their documents
SELECT A.name, COUNT(D.doc_id)
FROM Authors AS A
LEFT JOIN Documents AS D ON A.author_id = D.author_id
GROUP BY A.name;

-- Get document creation dates and author names
SELECT D.created_at, A.name
FROM Documents AS D
JOIN Authors AS A ON D.author_id = A.author_id;

-- Select documents whose author's email ends with 'example.com'
SELECT D.title, A.email
FROM Documents AS D
JOIN Authors AS A ON D.author_id = A.author_id
WHERE A.email LIKE '%@example.com';

-- Find documents written by authors whose name starts with 'B'
SELECT D.title, A.name
FROM Documents AS D
JOIN Authors AS A ON D.author_id = A.author_id
WHERE A.name LIKE 'B%';

-- Retrieve author names and the titles of documents they published after '2023-01-03'
SELECT A.name, D.title
FROM Authors AS A
JOIN Documents AS D ON A.author_id = D.author_id
WHERE D.created_at > '2023-01-03';

Schema: Events (event_id INT, name VARCHAR, date DATETIME, location VARCHAR, ticket_price DECIMAL), Attendees (attendee_id INT, name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR), Tickets (ticket_id INT, event_id INT, attendee_id INT, purchase_date DATETIME, price_paid DECIMAL).
Queries:
1. Select all attendees for a specific event.
2. Find the total revenue generated by each event.
3. Register a new attendee for an event.
4. Update an event's location.
5. List events with more than 50 tickets sold.
text_nat:
SELECT A.name, A.email
FROM Attendees AS A
JOIN Tickets AS T
ON A.attendee_id = T.attendee_id
JOIN Events AS E
ON T.event_id = E.event_id
WHERE E.name = 'Conference 2023';

SELECT E.name, SUM(T.price_paid) AS total_revenue
FROM Events AS E
JOIN Tickets AS T
ON E.event_id = T.event_id
GROUP BY E.name;

INSERT INTO Tickets (ticket_id, event_id, attendee_id, purchase_date, price_paid) VALUES (501, 1, 101, NOW(), 75.00);

UPDATE Events
SET location = 'Grand Hall B'
WHERE event_id = 1;

SELECT E.name, COUNT(T.ticket_id) AS tickets_sold
FROM Events AS E
JOIN Tickets AS T
ON E.event_id = T.event_id
GROUP BY E.name
HAVING COUNT(T.ticket_id) > 50;

SELECT T.ticket_id, E.name AS event_name
FROM Tickets AS T
JOIN Events AS E
ON T.event_id = E.event_id;

SELECT A.name AS attendee_name, T.purchase_date
FROM Attendees AS A
JOIN Tickets AS T
ON A.attendee_id = T.attendee_id;

SELECT E.name, E.date
FROM Events AS E
JOIN Tickets AS T
ON E.event_id = T.event_id
WHERE T.price_paid > 100;

SELECT A.name, E.location
FROM Attendees AS A
JOIN Tickets AS T
ON A.attendee_id = T.attendee_id
JOIN Events AS E
ON T.event_id = E.event_id;

SELECT T.ticket_id, A.email
FROM Tickets AS T
JOIN Attendees AS A
ON T.attendee_id = A.attendee_id;

SELECT E.event_id, SUM(T.price_paid)
FROM Events AS E
JOIN Tickets AS T
ON E.event_id = T.event_id
GROUP BY E.event_id;

SELECT A.name, COUNT(T.ticket_id)
FROM Attendees AS A
JOIN Tickets AS T
ON A.attendee_id = T.attendee_id
GROUP BY A.name;

SELECT E.name, E.ticket_price
FROM Events AS E
JOIN Tickets AS T
ON E.event_id = T.event_id
WHERE T.purchase_date < '2023-01-01';

Schema: Jobs (job_id INT, title VARCHAR, company VARCHAR, location VARCHAR, post_date DATE), Applicants (applicant_id INT, first_name VARCHAR, last_name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR), Applications (application_id INT, job_id INT, applicant_id INT, application_date DATE, status VARCHAR).
Queries:
1. Find all applications for a specific job.
2. List all jobs applied to by a particular applicant.
3. Submit a new job application.
4. Update an application's status.
5. Count the number of applications per job.
text_nat:

-- 1. Find all applications for a specific job (job_id = 1)
SELECT
    A.application_id,
    A.application_date,
    A.status,
    Ap.first_name,
    Ap.last_name
FROM
    Applications AS A
JOIN
    Applicants AS Ap ON A.applicant_id = Ap.applicant_id

    A.job_id = 1;

SELECT
    J.title,
    J.company,
    A.application_date,
    A.status
FROM
    Applications AS A
JOIN
    Jobs AS J ON A.job_id = J.job_id

    Applications

    J.title,
    COUNT(A.application_id) AS total_applications

    Jobs AS J

Schema: Donors (donor_id INT, name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR, address VARCHAR), Campaigns (campaign_id INT, name VARCHAR, target_amount DECIMAL, start_date DATE, end_date DATE), Donations (donation_id INT, donor_id INT, campaign_id INT, amount DECIMAL, donation_date DATETIME).
Queries:
1. Find all donations made by a specific donor.
2. List all donations for a particular campaign.

4. Update a campaign's target amount.
5. Calculate the total amount raised for each campaign.
text_nat:
INSERT INTO Donations (donor_id, campaign_id, amount, donation_date) VALUES (1, 1, 100.00, NOW());

FROM Donations

WHERE Donors.name = 'John Doe';

FROM Donations AS D
JOIN Donors AS DN ON D.donor_id = DN.donor_id
JOIN Campaigns AS C ON D.campaign_id = C.campaign_id
WHERE C.name = 'Emergency Relief Fund';

SELECT D.donation_id, DN.name AS donor_name
FROM Donations AS D
JOIN Donors AS DN ON D.donor_id = DN.donor_id;

JOIN Donors AS DN ON D.donor_id = DN.donor_id;

JOIN Campaigns AS C ON D.campaign_id = C.campaign_id

Schema: 
`Customers` (customer_id PK, first_name, last_name, email, join_date)
`Tiers` (tier_id PK, tier_name, min_points, max_points, benefits)
`LoyaltyPoints` (point_id PK, customer_id FK, points_earned, transaction_date, description)

Queries:
1. Get the current loyalty points for a specific customer.
2. Find all customers in a particular loyalty tier.
3. Calculate the total points earned by each customer.
4. Award loyalty points to a customer for a transaction.
5. Update a customer's loyalty tier based on their points.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE CustomerTiers (
    customer_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    tier_id     INT NOT NULL,
    updated_at  DATETIME NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT fk_ct_customer FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES Customers(customer_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_ct_tier     FOREIGN KEY (tier_id)     REFERENCES Tiers(tier_id)
);

CREATE VIEW CustomerPointTotals AS
SELECT c.customer_id,
       c.email,
       SUM(lp.points_earned) AS total_points,
       COUNT(lp.point_id)    AS transaction_count,
       MAX(lp.transaction_date) AS last_transaction
FROM Customers c
JOIN LoyaltyPoints lp ON lp.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.email;

DELIMITER $$

CREATE PROCEDURE GetCustomerPoints(IN p_customer_id INT)
BEGIN
    SELECT p.customer_id,
           CONCAT(c.first_name, ' ', c.last_name) AS customer_name,
           p.total_points,
           t.tier_name,
           t.benefits
    FROM CustomerPointTotals p
    JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = p.customer_id
    JOIN CustomerTiers ct ON ct.customer_id = p.customer_id
    JOIN Tiers t ON t.tier_id = ct.tier_id
    WHERE p.customer_id = p_customer_id;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE GetCustomersInTier(IN p_tier_name VARCHAR(50))
BEGIN
    SELECT c.customer_id,
           c.first_name,
           c.last_name,
           c.email,
           c.join_date,
           ct.updated_at AS tier_assigned_on
    FROM Tiers t
    JOIN CustomerTiers ct ON ct.tier_id = t.tier_id
    JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = ct.customer_id
    WHERE t.tier_name = p_tier_name
    ORDER BY c.last_name, c.first_name;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE GetTotalPointsByCustomer()
BEGIN
    SELECT c.customer_id,
           c.email,
           SUM(lp.points_earned) AS total_points,
           COUNT(lp.point_id) AS transaction_count,
           MAX(lp.transaction_date) AS last_transaction
    FROM Customers c
    JOIN LoyaltyPoints lp ON lp.customer_id = c.customer_id
    GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.email
    ORDER BY total_points DESC;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE GetTierSummary()
BEGIN
    SELECT t.tier_name,
           t.min_points,
           COUNT(ct.customer_id) AS member_count,
           ROUND(AVG(p.total_points), 1) AS avg_points
    FROM Tiers t
    JOIN CustomerTiers ct ON ct.tier_id = t.tier_id
    JOIN CustomerPointTotals p ON p.customer_id = ct.customer_id
    GROUP BY t.tier_id, t.tier_name, t.min_points
    ORDER BY t.min_points;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE UpdateCustomerTier(IN p_customer_id INT)
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO CustomerTiers (customer_id, tier_id, updated_at)
    SELECT p.customer_id, t.tier_id, NOW()
    FROM CustomerPointTotals p
    JOIN Tiers t ON p.total_points BETWEEN t.min_points AND COALESCE(t.max_points, 2147483647)
    WHERE p.customer_id = p_customer_id
    ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE tier_id = VALUES(tier_id), updated_at = NOW();
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE AwardPoints(IN p_customer_id INT, IN p_points INT, IN p_description VARCHAR(255))
BEGIN
    IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Customers WHERE customer_id = p_customer_id) THEN
        SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000' SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'Unknown customer_id';
    END IF;
    INSERT INTO LoyaltyPoints (customer_id, points_earned, transaction_date, description)
    VALUES (p_customer_id, p_points, NOW(), p_description);
    CALL UpdateCustomerTier(p_customer_id);
END$$

DELIMITER ;

CALL AwardPoints(101, 250, 'Order #5521 - electronics');
CALL AwardPoints(102, 40, 'Order #5522 - groceries');
CALL GetCustomerPoints(101);
CALL GetCustomersInTier('Gold');
CALL GetTotalPointsByCustomer();
CALL GetTierSummary();

Schema: 
`Organizations` (organization_id PK, org_name, contact_person, type)
`Grants` (grant_id PK, grant_name, description, available_funds, deadline)
`Applications` (application_id PK, organization_id FK, grant_id FK, submission_date, requested_amount, status)

Queries:
1. List all applications for a specific grant, including organization details.
2. Find all grants with a deadline in the next month.
3. Count the number of applications by status for each grant.
4. Submit a new grant application for an organization.
5. Update the status of an application to 'Approved'.
text_nat:
-- Grant management module: reporting views, lookup procedures and write operations.

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v_application_detail AS
SELECT a.application_id,
       a.grant_id,
       g.grant_name,
       g.deadline,
       o.organization_id,
       o.org_name,
       o.contact_person,
       o.type AS org_type,
       a.submission_date,
       a.requested_amount,
       a.status
FROM Applications a
JOIN Grants g ON g.grant_id = a.grant_id
JOIN Organizations o ON o.organization_id = a.organization_id;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v_application_counts_by_status AS
SELECT g.grant_id, g.grant_name, a.status, COUNT(a.application_id) AS application_count
FROM Grants g
JOIN Applications a ON a.grant_id = g.grant_id
GROUP BY g.grant_id, g.grant_name, a.status;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v_grants_due_next_month AS
SELECT g.grant_id, g.grant_name, g.available_funds, g.deadline
FROM Grants g
WHERE g.deadline >= DATE_FORMAT(CURDATE() + INTERVAL 1 MONTH, '%Y-%m-01')
  AND g.deadline <  DATE_FORMAT(CURDATE() + INTERVAL 2 MONTH, '%Y-%m-01');

DELIMITER //

CREATE PROCEDURE list_applications_for_grant(IN p_grant_id INT)
BEGIN
    SELECT a.application_id, o.org_name, o.contact_person, o.type AS org_type,
           a.submission_date, a.requested_amount, a.status
    FROM Applications a
    JOIN Organizations o ON o.organization_id = a.organization_id
    WHERE a.grant_id = p_grant_id
    ORDER BY a.submission_date, a.application_id;
END //

CREATE PROCEDURE organization_history(IN p_organization_id INT)
BEGIN
    SELECT a.application_id, g.grant_name, g.deadline,
           a.submission_date, a.requested_amount, a.status
    FROM Applications a
    JOIN Grants g ON g.grant_id = a.grant_id
    WHERE a.organization_id = p_organization_id
    ORDER BY a.submission_date DESC;
END //

CREATE PROCEDURE submit_application(IN p_organization_id INT,
                                    IN p_grant_id INT,
                                    IN p_requested_amount DECIMAL(12,2))
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO Applications (organization_id, grant_id, submission_date, requested_amount, status)
    SELECT o.organization_id, g.grant_id, CURDATE(), p_requested_amount, 'Submitted'
    FROM Grants g
    JOIN Organizations o ON o.organization_id = p_organization_id
    WHERE g.grant_id = p_grant_id
      AND g.deadline >= CURDATE()
      AND g.available_funds >= p_requested_amount;

    IF ROW_COUNT() = 0 THEN
        SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000'
            SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'Application rejected: unknown organization/grant, past deadline or insufficient funds';
    END IF;
END //

CREATE PROCEDURE approve_application(IN p_application_id INT)
BEGIN
    UPDATE Applications a
    JOIN Grants g ON g.grant_id = a.grant_id
    SET a.status = 'Approved',
        g.available_funds = g.available_funds - a.requested_amount
    WHERE a.application_id = p_application_id
      AND a.status <> 'Approved'
      AND g.available_funds >= a.requested_amount;

    IF ROW_COUNT() = 0 THEN
        SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000'
            SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'Approval failed: application already approved, missing or funds exhausted';
    END IF;
END //

DELIMITER ;

CALL submit_application(3, 7, 25000.00);
CALL approve_application(LAST_INSERT_ID());
CALL list_applications_for_grant(7);
CALL organization_history(3);
SELECT * FROM v_grants_due_next_month;
SELECT * FROM v_application_counts_by_status WHERE grant_id = 7;
SELECT * FROM v_application_detail WHERE organization_id = 3;

Schema:

`Players` (player_id PK, username, join_date)
`HighScores` (score_id PK, game_id FK, player_id FK, score, achieve_date)

Queries:
1. Get the top 10 high scores for a specific game, including player usernames.
2. Find all high scores achieved by a specific player.
3. Count the number of scores submitted for each game.
4. Record a new high score for a player in a game.
5. Update a player's high score for a specific game if the new score is higher.
text_nat:
-- Arcade high-score module: leaderboard views and the five required operations.

-- Leaderboard view: every score with its game and player details, ranked per game.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v_game_leaderboard AS
SELECT g.game_id,
       g.game_name,
       g.genre,
       p.player_id,
       p.username,
       h.score,
       h.achieve_date,
       RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY g.game_id
                    ORDER BY h.score DESC, h.achieve_date ASC) AS rank_in_game
FROM HighScores h
JOIN Games g ON g.game_id = h.game_id
JOIN Players p ON p.player_id = h.player_id;

-- Per-game score volume; subqueries keep games that have never been played.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v_game_score_counts AS
SELECT g.game_id,
       g.game_name,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM HighScores h WHERE h.game_id = g.game_id) AS score_count,
       (SELECT COALESCE(MAX(h.score), 0) FROM HighScores h WHERE h.game_id = g.game_id) AS best_score
FROM Games g;

-- 1. Top 10 high scores for a specific game, with player usernames.
SELECT p.username, h.score, h.achieve_date
FROM HighScores h
JOIN Games g ON g.game_id = h.game_id
JOIN Players p ON p.player_id = h.player_id
WHERE g.game_id = 3
ORDER BY h.score DESC, h.achieve_date ASC
LIMIT 10;

-- 2. All high scores achieved by a specific player.
SELECT p.username, g.game_name, g.genre, g.release_year, h.score, h.achieve_date
FROM HighScores h
JOIN Games g ON g.game_id = h.game_id
JOIN Players p ON p.player_id = h.player_id
WHERE h.player_id = 17
ORDER BY h.achieve_date DESC, h.score DESC;

-- 3. Number of scores submitted for each game.
SELECT game_id, game_name, score_count, best_score
FROM v_game_score_counts
ORDER BY score_count DESC, game_name;

-- 4. Record a new high score; the join rejects unknown ids and pre-join dates.
INSERT INTO HighScores (game_id, player_id, score, achieve_date)
SELECT g.game_id, p.player_id, 48200, DATE '2024-05-02'
FROM Games g
JOIN Players p ON p.join_date <= DATE '2024-05-02'
WHERE g.game_id = 3 AND p.player_id = 17;

-- 5. Raise a player's score for a game (identified by name) only if the run is better.
UPDATE HighScores h
JOIN Games g ON g.game_id = h.game_id
SET h.score = 51750,
    h.achieve_date = DATE '2024-06-11'
WHERE h.player_id = 17
  AND g.game_name = 'Nebula Rally'
  AND h.score < 51750;

-- Report: current leader of every game next to that game's score volume.
SELECT c.game_name, c.score_count, l.username AS leader, l.score AS leading_score
FROM v_game_score_counts c
JOIN v_game_leaderboard l ON l.game_id = c.game_id AND l.rank_in_game = 1
ORDER BY l.score DESC;

-- Report: genre totals built from the ranked leaderboard rows.
SELECT l.genre,
       COUNT(DISTINCT l.game_id) AS games_played,
       COUNT(DISTINCT l.player_id) AS players,
       MAX(l.score) AS genre_record
FROM v_game_leaderboard l
JOIN Players p ON p.player_id = l.player_id
WHERE p.join_date >= DATE '2023-01-01'
GROUP BY l.genre
ORDER BY genre_record DESC;
